mediaRemoteAdapter.note: Built as an embedded, unlinked arm64 framework by project.yml. The bundled Perl entry point reads system now-playing metadata only while a wallpaper has media integration enabled. Its `send` command is now invoked as well, but only for the three transport actions a user can bind to a wallpaper's own `usershortcut` property (TogglePlayPause, NextTrack, PreviousTrack), only for a wallpaper listed by system_media_scene_handles, and only as a short-lived process off the main actor. A wallpaper cannot name a command: it names one of its own properties, and the value its user chose decides what happens. The test client is not invoked.

auditRemediation.changes: Pair process identity with now-playing metadata and fence asynchronous notification callbacks by generation so departed sources cannot replace current state. The regression compiles the adapter against controlled platform callbacks; no player is launched.
auditRemediation.reviewFollowup: PR #24 review: ignore playback notifications without a value before advancing the callback generation, preserving pending startup and track lookups.

sceneMediaChanges: 2026-09-21: media delivery follows the effective consumer set (pause, power policy, presentation suspend, per-display suspend) while consent stays a separate question; cover updates replace one texture instead of rebuilding the render graph, and an unchanged cover is a true no-op. 2026-09-20: SceneScript video.isPlaying, vector.mix and MediaPlaybackEvent compatibility; native host media snapshots routed through the bridge and core actor to scene scripts, $mediaThumbnail and $mediaPreviousThumbnail. Effect shaders receive owner layer and screen projection matrices; empty scenes initialize their camera pointer. Shader pipeline revision 6 reserves array varying locations, narrows unambiguous vector function arguments, and shares compatible custom uniform vector prefixes across stages. Synthetic media events/artwork and asset inspection options added to the offscreen probe. Regression coverage in Swift, bridge, shader and C++ tests.

renderer.mediaIntegrationDefaultChanges: 2026-10-19: WallpaperConfig enables system media integration for new wallpapers and for stored configurations without the field, using the same explicit default for construction and Serde. Saved true and false values remain unchanged; no forced migration is performed. Desktop scenes and web descriptors inherit the preference, while low-level renderer defaults, previews and lock-screen isolation stay disabled. Bridge tests exercise media delivery without setup, disabling/clearing/re-enabling, web descriptors, consumer handles and saved-choice round trips. No renderer, protocol, dependency or per-frame work change.
renderer.displayPlaybackReconciliationChanges: 2026-10-18: The bridge reconciles each live scene's paused state against its current global playback and per-display suspension decisions after a successful reconcile, including the unchanged-configuration path. Core deliberately preserves runtime pause across scene rebuilds and reconnects; that retained state could outlive the bridge's decision and leave one display frozen even when its new descriptor said paused=false. Synchronization runs on the bridge actor with current policy, after generation validation for delegated work, and only changes mismatched live displays. No per-frame work, polling, new renderer, API or schema is added. General multi-display tests cover retained pause, unchanged assignments, independent hidden displays, manual pause, and policy changes during an in-flight reconcile. Desktop multi-monitor behavior and Wallpaper Engine frames were not compared.
renderer.hostedRunnerTestGuards: 2026-10-17: Test-only changes to tests/text_object_runtime_test.cpp, tests/apple_video_frame_test.mm and tests/metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm, no renderer source. Why: the v1.5.0 release gate on a hosted macOS 26 runner failed five tests that pass on real hardware. The PingFang tests (HanFallbackUsesTheSimplifiedFace, AGlyphTheFontLacksComesFromTheFirstFaceOfWallpaperEnginesList, CjkPunctuationIsNotDrawnByTheSymbolFace) now need HasReadablePingFangSC: a file FreeType opens with a face named PingFangSC-Regular that has Han; a Mac without the downloaded PingFang font asset matches the family to a copy the renderer cannot draw with. VideoDecoderSelection.AnAv1FrameReachesMetalWhenTheDefaultDecoderIsSoftwareOnly skips on a paravirtual Metal device, whose VideoToolbox reports AV1 hardware it cannot open (FFmpeg: hwaccel initialisation returned error). MetalSceneDraw.ParsedParticleBillboardsKeepTheirAuthoredScaleThroughParentsAndChildren lets through only an all-black compatibility frame on a paravirtual GPU (seen once, for the first case, on the runner; not reproduced in 30 local runs at 6-way concurrency) and runs the other cases; any other wrong picture still fails. Cause of that black frame not established.
renderer.stepMaskBooleanChanges: 2026-10-15: The shader crate's control-flow coercion reads an `int` declared from a two-argument `step` as a float (SymbolFacts::new in codegen/strategies/control_flow_coercion/symbols.rs, through int_step::float_step_names, which shares IntStepInitializer's own predicate), so a boolean stored into it converts and the other repairs agree with the declaration rewrite. Why: Wallpaper Engine's HLSL promotes a bool to a number, and the workshop Simple Audio Bars effect masks with `int barLeft = step(shapeCoord.y, barHeightLeft); barLeft *= isLeftChannel;`. IntStepInitializer rewrites the declaration to float but the symbol facts were built from the unrepaired source, where `barLeft` is an int, so FloatBoolAssignment left the bool bare and Naga rejected `Float * Bool`; the whole effect failed to load (`Rust shader compile failed`) for its circle and centre shapes without anti-aliasing, invisible at silence and missing under music. How established: Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42 draws the effect (the comparison's screenshot with the wallpaper's own music shows 9 bars where this renderer drew none) and its HLSL converts the bool implicitly; the mechanism from the legalized GLSL (`float barLeft = step(..); barLeft *= isLeftChannel;`) and Naga's `Operation Multiply can't work with ... Float ... and ... Bool` before the change, from a 320-combination matrix of the effect (128 of 640 compilations failed, all `SHAPE` 4 to 7 without `ANTIALIAS`, none after), and from a whole-library A/B over 1,857 shader jobs on SPIR-V and MSL (6 fixed, none regressed, every one of the 3,706 programs in that library that compiled before has byte-identical output). No pipeline revision bump: a compile that failed is never cached, so the effects that compile now meet no stale entry, and the forms that can read differently for other programs that compiled before (`x % 2` becomes `_we_Fmod(x, float(2))`, an `if (x)` compares with `0.0` instead of `0`, shown by probing the shader crate before and after) mean the same, so a stored program stays correct. Compile time only: no pass, buffer or per-frame work. The opt-in corpus sweep in tests/unpack_shader_compile_smoke.cpp compiled only each material's own combos; it now overlays the effect file's pass combos and the scene's entry for the pass, as the engine merges them, which is what exposes this. Tests: shader crate `legalize` `control_flow_coercion_strategy_lowers_bool_stored_into_step_repaired_int` and four more beside it, `MetalSceneDraw.ABooleanMultipliedIntoAStepMaskClipsItOnBothRenderers` and `UnpackShaderCompileSmoke.CompilesAnEffectUnderTheCombosTheSceneSetsOnIt`; the first two fail without the change. Not changed: a bool stored into a genuine `int` or `uint` (`int n = 2; n *= flag;`) and a number as an operand of `!`, `&&` or `||` (a float or int alike, probed) are still rejected by Naga.
renderer.writtenVertexInputChanges: 2026-10-15: The shader crate reports a written vertex input under its source name (backend/naga/reflector.rs through StageInterface::source_name in codegen/declarations/interface.rs), and pipeline revision 16 recompiles stored programs. Why: Wallpaper Engine's HLSL lets a vertex shader assign to its inputs, so the workshop Shadow effect's default AT combo writes `a_TexCoord *= atFactor` (a factor of 1 at its defaults) and WE draws the layer with a subtle shadow. The legalizer reads such an input through a local copy (declares `_we_in_a_TexCoord`, keeps `a_TexCoord` as the local) and Naga names the entry-point argument after the declaration, so reflection listed `_we_in_a_TexCoord`; both renderers bind a vertex attribute by its reflected name and give a name the mesh lacks the first buffer at offset 0, so the shader's texture coordinate was the vertex position and a text layer sampled empty texels and vanished. How established: WE's behaviour from a WE 2.8.42 screenshot of the scene that showed the layer (the text drawn with a ~4 px shadow); the mechanism from a probe scene that put copies of the layer under the effect with AT=0 (drawn), AT=1 and offset 0 (missing) and no write otherwise, from the reflected names before the change (`_we_in_a_TexCoord` for AT=1, `a_TexCoord` for AT=0), and by drawing the same probe again afterwards (the two text layers that were missing are drawn). Only the reflected name changes: SPIR-V and MSL are byte-identical, and there is no added pass, buffer or per-frame work. Tests: pipeline `a_vertex_input_the_shader_writes_keeps_the_attribute_name_the_mesh_provides` and `MetalSceneDraw.AVertexShaderThatWritesItsInputsStillReadsTheMeshOnBothRenderers`, which fail without the change. Not changed: the renderers still bind a vertex input the mesh lacks to the first buffer silently, which suits an input a shader never reads.
renderer.sourceDefinedMulChanges: 2026-10-15: The shader legalizer's HLSL multiplication strategy preserves a source-defined mul helper, using the declaration query already used by compatibility helpers. Call-like token facts include function definitions and prototypes; treating those as HLSL calls corrupted a mat3/vec3 helper's declaration and dropped the full color-grading/tone-mapping effect in Workshop 2806956811 on both renderers. The guard is local to the stage declaring the helper, so ordinary builtin mul lowering in the other stage is unchanged. Shader pipeline revision 16 -> 17 invalidates old generated programs. An original GPU regression compiles overloaded helpers, a prototype and nested calls and draws their analytically known color and card coverage through both production renderers, with builtin multiplication still placing the card in the other stage. No private assets, wallpaper-specific rules or per-frame work.
renderer.livePropertyChanges: 2026-10-13: A running scene can be handed a whole property document, so a property edit can be shown without loading the scene again. This part keeps the project's authored defaults apart from the values the scene loaded with. SceneParseRequest gains authored_project_properties (null means the loaded table is also the authored one) and SceneRuntimeBootstrap the same optional table; MainHandler::loadScene copies the table ParseProjectProperties returns before the saved override JSON is merged over it and passes it, and WPSceneParser forwards it into the bootstrap. SceneRuntimeContext keeps the authored table as its defaults and the loaded table as the values in effect, so ApplyProjectPropertyOverride(document) means the authored defaults plus exactly this document, and a property the document leaves out (and ResetProjectPropertyOverride, the empty document) returns to what the project declares rather than to what the scene loaded with. Both now return the sorted names whose value in effect changed (ProjectPropertyValueChanged, a change of kind counts). A request without an authored table behaves as before. defaultProjectProperties() has no other consumer, and nothing in the app or the bridge calls the apply function yet, so behaviour is unchanged. New CPU-only gtest binary project_property_preview_test (tests/CMakeLists.txt, registered in REGRESSION_BINARIES so check_renderer.py runs it): the table arithmetic with and without an authored table, and, through the real WPSceneParser with an in-memory file system, a flag and a choice with a user condition (visibility), a slider (g_UserAlpha), a colour (g_Color4), a bound text and a bound material constant each returning to the authored value bit for bit against a fresh parse, a document equalling a load with it, and a document adding no time-advancing work. No wallpaper-specific branches, passes, allocations or per-frame work: the apply function still runs only when something calls it. Not exercised here: MainHandler::loadScene handing the table to a live engine, which needs the engine command a later change adds. Properties a scene reads only while it loads. A parse-time audit of every property read found that everything bound through the SceneSettingResolver (layer visibility, alpha, colour, origin, scale and angles, camera, clear colour, bloom, shader constants, rope UVs, particle overrides, text, puppets) or a dynamic-value listener is live, and three readers are not: a usertextures slot that names a scenetexture property (ApplySystemUserTextures in LoadMaterial), an effect whose visible is bound to a property (ResolveUserEffectVisibility builds the effect only when visible, and building every hidden effect would cost passes and memory, so it stays load-only), and a sound layer's volume binding (WPSoundParser; made live by a later part, see Sound layer volume below). SceneRuntimeContext gains NoteLoadOnlyProperty(name), which records the name and the value it was read with (absent when the table does not name it), LoadOnlyProperties() (the sorted names) and PreviewProjectPropertyOverride(document), which returns ProjectPropertyPreview{changed, deferred}: it is ApplyProjectPropertyOverride with every noted name forced back to the value it was read with, for every consumer of that name, live ones included so that no property is half applied, and lists in deferred each noted name the document asked for something else (a name it leaves out counts as the declared default). ApplyProjectPropertyOverride and the new function share a private ApplyProjectProperties(table). SceneSettingResolver gains UserPropertyName(setting), the reading parse_condition already did for both authored forms ({user: name} and {user: {name, condition}}), and WPSceneParser gains UserTexturePropertyName(slot), the bare-string slot form ApplySystemUserTextures already resolved, so the parser notes names without duplicating either format. LoadMaterial notes every usertextures property name after ApplySystemUserTextures and ResolveUserEffectVisibility (image and text objects) notes the user name of an effect's visible setting; a scripted effect visibility is not user-form (WPImageEffect::FromJson keeps visible_setting only without a script) and is not noted. No wallpaper-specific branches, passes, allocations or per-frame work: a scene notes a handful of names while it loads, and the new function runs only when something calls it, which nothing in the app does yet. Tests (project_property_preview_test, LoadOnlyProperties.*): UserPropertyName and UserTexturePropertyName on every form, the names noted for a scenetexture slot, an effect toggle and a combo condition on an image layer and on a text object (and none for a scripted visibility, a plain value or a live slider), a preview holding them and reporting deferred (a document that leaves out a name loaded with a saved choice defers it, asking for the loaded value defers nothing), a toggle that also shows a layer held for the layer as well, and a fresh parse with the new values building a different effect set and slot texture, which is why a running scene cannot take them. The existing RenderGraph.parsedEffectVisibilityFollowsTheBoundUserProperty and TextObjectRuntime.TextEffectVisibilityFollowsTheBoundUserProperty are unchanged. Sound layer volume. WPSoundParser::Parse read a slider-bound volume once, when the layer was created, so a sound layer could never follow a property change; it is now live and is not a load-only property. WPSoundParser gains BindVolumeProperty(runtime, weak_ptr<WPSoundStream>, property, authored_volume), which resolves {user: property, value: authored_volume} with the same ResolveFloatSetting every slider-driven setting uses (the authored volume while the project declares no such property, the property's value once it does) and registers it with RegisterDynamicValueListener; the listener calls WPSoundStream::SetVolume, an atomic store clamped by ClampVolume that the audio thread already reads, for a Float or Int value only (a choice or a switch leaves the volume alone, as Parse already did), only when the value differs from the last one it applied (ApplyProjectProperties refreshes every property on every document, so an unrelated edit must not undo a volume a script set with SetSoundLayerVolume), and not at all once the stream is gone (the listener holds a weak_ptr, as the runtime's sound layer registry does). Parse keeps its initial read of the property and calls the binder after RegisterSoundLayer when the object names a volume property and a runtime exists. No wallpaper-specific branches, passes, allocations or per-frame work: one listener per bound sound layer, run only when a document is applied. Tests (project_property_preview_test, SoundLayerVolume.*, a fake sound stream and a null-backend sound manager, so no audio device is opened): the volume follows a property, clamps above full, returns to the project's own volume on the empty document, on a reset and after a saved choice (not to the saved choice or to the layer's authored volume), and a preview moves it with nothing deferred; an undeclared, empty-named or non-numeric property leaves the volume alone; an unchanged property does not undo a script's volume; a released stream is not touched; and the real Parse binds a user-bound volume and leaves a plain number alone. Audible output on real hardware was not checked. Not exercised here: a preview on a live renderer. Property preview command. SceneWallpaper gains the string property PROPERTY_PROJECT_PROPERTY_PREVIEW_JSON ('project_property_preview_json', SceneWallpaper.hpp) and the C ABI accessor owe_property_project_property_preview_json (SceneWallpaperBindings.h/.mm), set with the existing owe_scene_wallpaper_set_property_string. The existing override and reset properties keep their LOAD_SCENE behaviour. MainHandler's SET_PROPERTY branch parses the value with ParseFlatProjectPropertyOverrideJson (a document that is not a JSON object is logged and changes nothing) and does not touch m_project_property_override_json, so any later load shows the saved look. The parsed map goes into a latest-wins slot owned by RenderHandler (a mutex-protected std::optional<ProjectProperties>, stageProjectPropertyPreview); a new RenderHandler command CMD_APPLY_PROJECT_PROPERTIES, dispatched by a CASE_CMD entry in onMessageReceived, is posted only when the slot was empty, so a burst of documents queues at most one command behind the one it waits for. Its handler takes the slot on the render looper, the only thread that ticks the runtime, and calls SceneRuntimeContext::PreviewProjectPropertyOverride; it is dropped when there is no scene or the scene has no runtime (a plain video). Nothing is replayed after SET_SCENE, so a document cannot reach another wallpaper by sharing a property name. Like every RenderHandler command except DRAW it calls requestFrame(), so an idle on-demand scene draws one frame and a paused one shows the change when it resumes; no per-frame code and no DescribeTimeAdvancingWork entry is added. A layer the document reveals that the render graph left out needs no new code: Tick sees it shown, RequestGraphForShownLayers sets the graph-mutation flag and DRAW rebuilds the graph once, the path a script showing the layer takes; a layer a preview hides again keeps its passes until the next build, and sceneToRenderGraph recomputes its exclusions on every build, so the graph holds at most the layers a preview showed since it was last built (never more than the wallpaper ships) and is back to what a fresh load with the current values holds at the next build. The deferred names are logged once as a set, when the set changes (the log has only info and error levels), and reset on a new scene; under WESCENE_BUILD_TESTS a counter of handled commands is readable through SceneWallpaperInputTestAccess::PropertyPreviewCommandsHandled. No wallpaper-specific branches. Tests: project_property_preview_test ScenePropertyPreview.* sends documents through SceneWallpaper::setPropertyString to scenes with a runtime and nothing to draw (a document reaches the runtime and a load-only property stays put; a burst of 500 documents queued while the render thread waits inside a listener runs the runtime twice and handles two commands; a bad document or a missing scene changes nothing and is not kept for the next scene; a second scene shows its own loaded values; a preview adds no time-advancing work); layer_texture_reference_test HiddenLayers.APropertyPreviewRevealsALayerWithOneGraphRebuildAndAGraphBuiltLaterLeavesTheHiddenOneOutAgain pins the one graph rebuild and that a held property reveals nothing; metal_scene_draw_smoke MetalSceneDraw.APropertyPreviewChangesThePixelsAndAnEmptyDocumentRestoresThemByteForByte (private textures, skips without a Metal device) shows a slider-bound alpha changing the picture with no new graph, a switch rebuilding the graph once and drawing what a fresh load with the same values draws, and the empty document restoring the first frame byte for byte. Nothing in the app or the bridge sends the property yet, so behaviour is unchanged. unchanged_present_test UnchangedPresent.APropertyPreviewShowsOnAStillSceneAndWakesAnIdleOneForOneFrame (Compatibility backend on a layer no window owns, added to REALTIME_TESTS in scripts/check_renderer.py) sends a slider through the property: a still scene with every pass reused submits exactly one frame and presents a different picture, and with the on-demand clock the stopped scene draws exactly one frame and goes back to sleep. Not exercised here: a preview on a real display, a paused scene showing the change on resume, and the hitch of a revealed layer compiling new pipelines. Engine side. The Rust core mirrors preview_framing for a property document. OweScene gains project_property_preview_json() (the owe_property_project_property_preview_json name, null-checked like its neighbours) and preview_property_override(flat_json), which refuses a document with a NUL byte or a closed scene and sets that string property with set_property_string; unlike set_property_override it asks for no shader refresh, because nothing is loaded again. OweScene also records the document it was last shown (previewed_properties) and does not send the same one again; set_property_override and reset_property_override, which load the scene again, drop the record, and a replaced renderer is a new object that starts without one, so no path that rebuilds a scene (a descriptor change, a shader cache clear, the wake check's repair, the engine's own recovery of a failed frame) can leave a record of a look the scene no longer has, including the ones the bridge never sees. A refused update and a closed scene leave nothing recorded or are refused before the record is read. SceneRuntime::preview_property_override_json takes the project file the document was made for: preview_on_scene_of compares it with the scene's own scene_path when the request is handled, which is after any reconcile that was queued ahead of it, and answers PropertyPreview::OtherWallpaper without touching the renderer for a scene that draws another wallpaper, because a reconcile replaces the renderer inside the same SceneRuntime and keeps the handle while the bridge still maps the display to the first wallpaper. Otherwise it asks the renderer only: it leaves the runtime's property_override_json, its descriptor, the stored SceneTemplate and pointer delivery alone, so SceneRuntimeState, property_override_update and RuntimeRefreshMode::from_transition keep comparing the saved configuration and an abandoned edit leaves nothing to rebuild. It travels as messages::PreviewPropertyOverride (handle, expected_scene_path, flat_json) to an actor handler that uses state.scene_mut(handle), records no runtime state, publishes no snapshot and replies with PropertyPreview (Shown, or OtherWallpaper; exported from wallpaper_core), and WallpaperEngine::preview_property_override(handle, scene_path, json) parses and flattens the document with the private helper flat_property_document, which set_property_override now shares, before it asks the actor, so a document that is not a JSON object, has an array leaf or is not JSON is InvalidInput and never reaches C++. set_property_override and reset_property_override keep their reload semantics and are still what SceneRuntimeState replays. Rust only: no C++, no bridge change, no generated binding, and nothing calls the new method yet, so behaviour is unchanged. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-core --lib property; --test core_audio_api): the refusal before the actor, with the loading call's message, for an array, a number, a string, null, text that is not JSON, nothing and an array leaf; a valid empty, flat and nested document reaching the actor; the flat form the renderer receives; the preview property being distinct from the override, reset and shader-refresh ones; a NUL byte and a closed scene (also one that was last shown the document) refused by OweScene; the method's signature; through an allocated, never initialised renderer object, which takes property updates like a running one, the record of what it was shown surviving a repeat and a refused document and dropped by set_property_override and reset_property_override, and preview_on_scene_of leaving the renderer untouched for another wallpaper's document and showing its own. Device-free: how SceneRuntime::preview_property_override_json behaves on a live renderer was not exercised, as for preview_framing. Bridge, property document. The bridge builds the property document of a scene descriptor with project::overrides::scene_property_override_json(model, overrides) instead of inline in SceneDescBuilderExt::build_from_wallpaper_config (engine/activation.rs), which now calls it, so the document a later preview pushes to a running scene comes out of the same function as the one Apply loads: the defaults this host supplies (default_is_host_supplied), the overrides on top through PropertyValue::from_json, keys in sorted order, None when there is nothing to send. ProjectModel::live_property_overrides(committed, current) is the set of values a preview shows: the draft is taken as it is, except that a texture, file or directory property stays at its committed value (and leaves the set when nothing is committed), because a texture is read only while a scene loads and a file or folder is saved the moment it is picked. WallpaperOptionsDraft::committed() is a read-only getter beside current(). Rust only: no C++, no generated binding, and no behaviour change (the descriptors are byte for byte the ones built before; tests::settings_intents and tests::activation_plan pass unchanged), and nothing calls live_property_overrides or committed() yet. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-bridge --lib project::overrides; state::drafts): the document is absent for nothing to send, carries a host-supplied transport shortcut default, lets the user value (including an empty one) win, keeps undeclared ids in key order, with and without a manifest; the live set takes the draft for a flag, slider, colour, combo and text, drops a value the draft restored to default, holds a texture, file and folder at their committed values, keeps a frozen id the draft removed and leaves out one it only added, follows the draft for undeclared ids, and a preview document differs from the Apply document only in the frozen kinds; the committed config ignores pending edits until Apply. Bridge, scenes that draw the wallpaper. WallpaperBridge gains preview_wallpaper_properties(wallpaper_id, show) -> Result<(), BridgeError> (message PreviewWallpaperProperties; one UniFFI method, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated by scripts/build.py). EngineFacade gains preview_property_override(handle, scene_path: String, flat_json: String) -> PropertyPreview, which RealEngineFacade forwards to WallpaperEngine::preview_property_override, ArcEngineFacade forwards, the two playback test engines accept and FakeEngineFacade follows the engine's rules (it declines a scene that draws another wallpaper, remembers per display what it was shown, forgets it when a reconcile gives the display a scene that is not the same wallpaper or rebuild_renderer_of stands for an engine-internal recovery) and records the documents that reach a renderer (preview_property_calls(), declined_property_previews(), fail_next_property_preview()). BridgePaths::project_json(wallpaper_id) is the one place the project file of a Workshop wallpaper is built, for the scene descriptor's scene_path and for the path a preview names. The handler asks BridgeActorState::pending_property_documents, which returns None for a wallpaper that is not a scene project (a video, a web page, a project that is not loaded) and otherwise the draft's PropertyDocuments { shown, saved }: both come out of scene_property_override_json, `saved` from the committed overrides and `shown` from ProjectModel::live_property_overrides(committed, current), with {} standing for a descriptor that carries no document. With show true it pushes `shown`, with show false `saved`, to every handle wallpaper_handles(wallpaper_id, true) returns (a mirror runs a scene of its own), and sends nothing when the wallpaper has no mark and the document is the saved one; whether a scene already shows a document is the engine's to say, so the call asks for every scene and the engine skips the ones that do. previewed_properties (a set of the wallpapers whose scenes may be showing an edit; the bridge keeps no copy of what a scene shows, because anything that loads a scene again would leave it wrong) is marked before the first push, so an engine refusal midway (BridgeError::engine) leaves a mark that makes the next call ask again; it is removed when the document pushed is the saved one, when no handle draws the wallpaper, and when the engine declined every scene because each now draws another wallpaper (a handle found from the committed configuration can already run the next wallpaper while a reconcile that moves the display has not committed yet; a declined scene is skipped, not an error). CancelWallpaperOptions puts the saved look back first (show false), before the scale factor rollback and before the draft is cancelled, so a refusal returns the error with the draft still dirty and Revert can be asked again. CommitApplyAfterReconcile removes the wallpaper's mark once the reconcile is known current, because Apply opens its scenes again from the saved configuration. Nothing in the bridge resets a mark when a reconcile, a shader cache clear or a recovery loads scenes again; the engine drops what each renderer was shown, and a mark that outlives a rebuild only makes the next restore put back a saved look the scene already has. A ReconcileFailed does not remove the mark (the restore that follows may keep a previewed scene). Nothing is saved, the draft and the generation are not touched, no snapshot is built, lock_screen_scenes and the Mission Control picture follow the saved configuration, and no log line is written per step, the same contract as preview_display_position, so a reconcile that is under way is not made stale. The renderer gains nothing: the call only reaches PreviewPropertyOverride. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-bridge --lib property_preview; state::drafts): a pending edit reaches the scene on each of two displays and on a mirror with the whole document and writes no file, changes no export and leaves a display refresh nothing to rebuild; the document is the one Apply loads byte for byte; a restored property or restore all defaults sends the saved document with the host-supplied default; a texture waits for Apply while a picked file stays in later documents; an identical document, an untouched wallpaper and a shown saved look send nothing; Revert and show false put the saved look back once and keep the draft, and a second Revert sends nothing; a refused update and a refused restore are repeated and the restore keeps the draft dirty; Apply removes the mark; a scene the engine kept is not told again, and one it opened afresh, a shader cache clear rebuilt or a recovery replaced is; a document made for a wallpaper that a reconcile just moved off a display (the apply held after the engine switched it, before the bridge committed) is declined for that display and never recorded as sent to the scene that now draws another wallpaper, while a display still showing the wallpaper follows; a preview while an Apply is loading does not make it stale; a video, a web page and a wallpaper no display shows are silent and an unknown wallpaper is InvalidInput; the documents of a draft differ only by what a scene can take. Device-free: no renderer is opened, so what a real scene does with the document is covered only by the renderer tests above and a desktop run. Nothing in the app calls the method yet. Bridge, values being dragged. preview_wallpaper_properties(wallpaper_id, show, pending) and wallpaper_preview(wallpaper_id, display_id, pending) take pending: Vec<BridgePropertyEdit> (a new UniFFI record, property_id and a BridgePropertyValue), the values of sliders and colours the host is showing without having saved them; App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated by scripts/build.py. The checks EditProperty ran inline are now ProjectModel::check_edit(property_id, value), one function that EditProperty, the property preview and the preview export all call (the same kinds, finite ranges, colour channels and combo options, the same two messages), and ProjectModel::checked_edits turns a list of pending values into the (id, PropertyValue) pairs the editing functions take or refuses the whole list. ProjectModel::edited_overrides(values, edits) makes the edits one after another with edit_overrides on a copy, and WallpaperOptionsDraft::with_edits(model, edits) returns the draft with them made, the draft itself untouched. BridgeActorState::pending_property_documents(wallpaper_id, pending) takes the documents from that copy (the saved configuration twice, as before, when there is no draft), and checks pending only for a scene whose project is loaded: a video, a web page and an unloaded project stay silent whatever the list holds. show_wallpaper_properties passes the list through, so a drag step is the same push as an edit's: the documents differ only by the value on top, the previewed_properties mark records what was shown, and a later call that does not name the value shows the draft again, so the value is kept nowhere (not in the draft, the saved configuration, the generation, a snapshot or the dirty state). show false validates the list and ignores it, because it asks for the saved document. wallpaper_preview applies the list to the draft for the export alone, so a Web page's applyUserProperties payload and a scene's flat document follow the drag too. A texture, file or directory among the pending values is frozen at its committed value like one in the draft. No C++ and no renderer change; the one extra cost is, per step of a drag (the panel sends at most one every 100 ms), a draft copy and the document build the edit already paid. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-bridge --lib property_preview; wallpaper_preview; state::drafts): a step lands over the draft on every scene that draws the wallpaper and over an edit already made, keeps nothing and writes no file, a drag alone leaves a clean wallpaper clean and Revert puts the saved look back, dragging back to the authored value sends the saved document, later steps win and a texture among them waits, committing the value last shown sends nothing more while another value does, a list with one refused step (unknown id, out of range, NaN, an infinity, the wrong kind, a colour channel, an option that is not offered) is refused with the edit's own message and sends nothing, and a video is not asked; the export puts the step over the draft without moving the draft or its dirty marks, follows for a Web page, and refuses what an edit refuses. Device-free, as above.
renderer.qualityThrottleChanges: 2026-10-13: The bridge can hold a runtime-only request for the reduced-quality profile, separate from the saved battery mode. WallpaperBridge::set_quality_throttle(causes) (message SetQualityThrottle, reply the usual snapshot bundle) takes a list of the new uniffi enum api::BridgeQualityThrottleCause (LowPowerMode, Heat, LowBattery), keeps it as BridgeActorState::quality_throttle (a BTreeSet, so duplicates count once and the snapshot lists the causes sorted; never written to config.toml, empty at every start), and applies it live like the battery profile: apply_quality_profile pushes the render scale and per-display rate to every open scene with the existing set_render_scale and set_fps calls, with no rebuild of the scene list and no change to playback. The ceiling is still the existing min logic: active_target_fps_cap takes the profile's rate into the minimum when the battery profile holds (Reduced quality while on battery) or any cause is set, so a request can only lower what the user's own cap allows. The scale takes a new config::QualityInForce { battery_profile, throttled } in AppConfig::effective_render_scale: a throttle gives the lower of the user's clamped scale and the profile's clamped scale, the battery profile alone keeps returning the profile's scale as is (unchanged, and possibly above a lower saved scale), and neither gives the user's scale, so adding a request to the battery profile never raises quality. BridgeSettingsSnapshot gains quality_throttle (the causes in force) and effective_frame_rate_cap (the ceiling in force; frame_rate_cap stays the saved global cap), filled from the same helpers the descriptors use, so web, native-video and lock-screen descriptors, the activation inputs and the native admission keys follow the request exactly as they follow the battery profile. The handler does not return early for an unchanged set, so asking again after a refused renderer update re-asserts it (the request is kept on error, like a frame-rate cap), applies it through apply_quality_profile, which also hands back a clip whose native refusal described the old ceiling (release_stale_native_video: a changed ceiling changes the admission keys, so refusals that match no live key are dropped and the scene list is reconciled unless presentation is unloaded; BridgeActorState::native_video_release_owed keeps that rebuild owed until one succeeds, so a request that failed halfway and is repeated, a rebuild that failed and the host's next ask for the native list all finish it instead of finding nothing left to drop, and the cap, the battery profile, the battery mode and the power source, which all end in apply_quality_profile, release a refused clip as well), and ends with bump_generation so an in-flight Apply is made stale and restored with the current quality. apply_quality_profile's log line also names the causes. FakeEngineFacade gains fail_next_render_scale. Bridge-side Rust only: no vendored C++ or config schema change (MetalRender::ApplyRenderScale already returns early on an unchanged scale); one uniffi export, one enum and two snapshot fields are added, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated by scripts/build.py. Device-free regressions in tests::quality_throttle (live lowering and restoring without a rebuild, never raising above the user's scale or cap, a table over saved scale, saved cap, battery profile and request, causes ending one at a time, not persisted, a wallpaper applied under the request, web, lock-screen and native-video descriptors, playback untouched, retry after a refused update) and tests::settings_intents (a display refresh and a reconcile keep a scene held to the request); a refused clip goes back to the native player at once whichever change moved the ceiling (the throttle, the cap, the rate or mode of the battery profile, the power source), also after a request that failed halfway and after a rebuild that failed. Each of these tests keeps a tests::engine_release::EngineRelease for its fake engine, which drops the engine's first-frame callback when the test ends: that callback holds the actor and its runtime and the actor holds the engine, so without it a test bridge keeps about twenty threads until the test process exits. A live Metal or Vulkan scene following the change, and any power effect, were not exercised here.
renderer.metalMatrixInverseChanges: 2026-10-13: Naga 29's MSL writer has no inverse(), so any stage that inverted a matrix failed native Metal translation (`metal translation of '<shader>' failed`), which dropped the effect or sent the whole wallpaper to the compatibility renderer, while it drew under Vulkan: the stock perspective and lightshafts effects with any combos, and reflection, clouds and waterwaves with PERSPECTIVE=1, each undoing squareToQuad in its vertex stage. The legalizer's compatibility_functions strategy renames builtin inverse calls to _we_Inverse (unless the shader declares its own inverse) and emits mat2/mat3/mat4 adjugate-over-determinant overloads behind #ifdef _WE_POLYFILL_INVERSE, with #define _we_Inverse inverse otherwise; NagaCompiler defines the macro only for the MetalMsl target, so SPIR-V keeps GLSL.std.450 MatrixInverse. ShaderPipelineRevision stays 12: across 1,269 (scene, shader, combos) programs from the local scene library, compiled for SPIR-V and MSL (2,538 compilations), the 20 MSL inverse() failures compile, nothing that compiled stops compiling, and every program that already compiled keeps byte-identical SPIR-V, MSL, bindings, reflection and metadata; failed compiles were never cached. On the 11 local scenes that use these effects, native Metal reported 10 translation failures and 8 scenes fell back with `a shader could not be translated to Metal`; after the change there are none, 4 of those scenes run natively, and 4 now stop at the separate history-feedback limitation. The generated helpers match simd_inverse to within 1.5e-5 relative error on 4,096 random matrices per size on the GPU. Regressions: tests/naga_metal.rs (MSL translation of all three sizes; SPIR-V still uses MatrixInverse and gains no function) and MetalSceneDraw.MatrixInversesOfEverySizeAreTranslatedAndDrawnExactly (round-trip residuals drawn by the native backend). Compile-time only: no pass, per-frame work or allocation beyond the restored effects' own, and no wallpaper-specific rules.
renderer.legacyShaderExpressionChanges: 2026-10-13: The shader legalizer (crates/shader) repairs more expressions Wallpaper Engine's permissive path accepts and strict GLSL rejects; each dropped a whole effect on both renderers (`effect '<name>' failed to load`). A component-wise builtin of known scalars and a one-component read count as scalars, so pow, mix, min, max and the other broadcasting builtins broadcast them (`pow(abs(c), color)`); the legacy saturate, log10, lerp, fmod and atan2 spellings are classified with their GLSL forms, and a vector or matrix constructor no longer reads as scalar. Declaration and assignment truncation measures operands that are calls, constructors or parenthesized groups and swizzles only the innermost wider ones (`round(v2) * v4`, `(CAST2(500) / res4) * s`). A scalar stored into a vector by plain `=` broadcasts, as compound assignment already did, and an expression of known vector width is never broadcast; a returned value converts to the declared return type (narrowed, broadcast, or `.x` for a scalar return). A comparison stored into a float lvalue by =, +=, -=, *= or /= becomes 1.0/0.0 (FloatBoolAssignment replaces FloatTimesBool, keeping its output), and BoolExpression reads a conditional by its selected branch, so `float x = a < b ? 1.0 : 2.0;` is no longer rewritten into an invalid nested conditional. A second subscript on a widened float uniform-array element selects the element itself (`.x`). A new global_initializers strategy wraps a global initializer that reads a runtime value (uniform, texture, stage input, mutable or moved global, user function, gl_ builtin) in `void _we_init_<name>()`, called at the start of main after the input copies; Naga rejected it on a const global and silently dropped it on a mutable one, which then read zero. Constant initializers stay constant expressions. Statements after a JSON annotation or a #define get declaration, expression and statement facts (TokenCursor::next_statement_start); the annotation or directive had been taken for the statement's first token, so every repair skipped them. ShaderPipelineRevision 11 -> 12. Across 1,269 (scene, shader, combos) programs from the 60 local scene wallpapers, compiled for SPIR-V and MSL (2,538 compilations): failures fall from 64 to 28, nothing that compiled stops compiling, and outputs that changed for programs that already compiled change only in semantically neutral ways (genuine scalars broadcast in compound assignments, mistaken identity broadcasts removed, existing int loop-bound casts reaching loops after a directive). The 28 left are outside this change: Naga's MSL backend lacks inverse() (stock lightshafts, perspective, reflection, clouds and waterwaves variants), two preprocessor #if forms, and a builtin scalar call initializing a vector. Synthetic regressions in tests/legalize_type_coercion.rs, legalize.rs, naga_compile.rs and tokenizer.rs fail with the changes removed. Compile-time only: no pass, per-frame work or allocation is added beyond the restored effects' own, and no wallpaper-specific rules.
renderer.shaderDirectiveAndScalarCallChanges: 2026-10-13: Three more Workshop effects that the shader crate (crates/shader) dropped on both renderers (`effect '<name>' failed to load`) now compile. A preprocessor directive keyword ends at its first non-identifier character instead of the first whitespace, so `#if(A == B)`, `#elif(...)` and `#endif// note` are conditionals; before, `#if(` passed through as an unknown directive, its `#endif` closed the enclosing block and Naga reported an unfinished block. When a trailing `//` comment is stripped from a directive, only a body that starts with `<` (an `#include <path>`) opens angle brackets, so a `<` comparison (`#if A < 1 && B == 0 //note`) no longer keeps the comment in the expression (`#if expression is unsupported`). A whole call of a builtin that returns a scalar whatever its argument widths (dot, length, distance, textureQueryLevels) counts as a scalar unless a visible user overload of that name returns something else, so it broadcasts when it initializes, is assigned or added to, or is returned as a vector (`vec2 proj = dot(a, b);`). ShaderPipelineRevision 12 -> 13. Across the same 1,269 (scene, shader, combos) programs from the 60 local scene wallpapers (2,538 SPIR-V and MSL compilations), on top of the Metal inverse helper: failures fall from 8 to 0, so every program in the local library now compiles for both targets; nothing that compiled stops compiling, and the only output that changes for programs that already compiled broadcasts a dot() added to a vec3 (`p3 += vec3(dot(p3, p3.yzx + 33.33));`, the same value). Synthetic regressions in tests/preprocess.rs and tests/legalize_type_coercion.rs fail with the changes removed. Compile-time only: no pass, per-frame work or allocation is added beyond the restored effects' own, and no wallpaper-specific rules.
renderer.wallpaperFramingChanges: 2026-10-13: The Rust engine carries a scene's framing, the position of the presented wallpaper inside the room its display leaves around it, the way it carries the scaling factor. project::SceneFraming (pan_x, pan_y: fractions from 0, the left or top edge, to 1, the right or bottom edge; default 0.5, the centre; is_valid and validate refuse a value that is not finite or lies outside 0..=1) is a field of SceneDesc, SceneTemplate and both builders (framing(), with_framing()), validated by every validate() and build(), copied by SceneTemplate::from_scene_desc and for_display, and part of SceneDesc::same_wallpaper, so only a genuinely different descriptor forces a rebuild and the live setter, which updates the stored descriptor, never does. OweBackend::open_scene takes the framing after the scaling factor, applies it right after set_scaling_factor and prints the pan on the load line; OweScene::set_framing wraps owe_scene_wallpaper_set_framing through call_status. SceneRuntime and SceneRuntimeState gain framing: the first open and every rebuild pass it to the renderer, runtime_state and TryFrom<&SceneDesc> carry it, inherit_descriptor_defaults takes the next descriptor's framing for a different wallpaper and keeps the live one for the same wallpaper (as for scaling), and SceneRuntime::set_framing restarts pointer delivery (the mapping changed), asks the renderer and only then updates the runtime and its descriptor, so a renderer rejection leaves both unchanged. The engine gains messages::SetFraming, the actor handler (with_scene_mut records the runtime state and syncs the stored SceneTemplate that the bridge compares, with_snapshot_update publishes the snapshot) and WallpaperEngine::set_framing, which refuses an invalid framing with InvalidInput before any message is sent, so it never reaches C++. A drag in progress is shown without being kept: SceneRuntime::preview_framing restarts pointer delivery and asks the renderer but leaves the runtime and its descriptor alone, so an abandoned drag leaves the live descriptor equal to the saved configuration (the next reconcile finds nothing to rebuild, and a renderer rebuild returns to the committed position); it travels as messages::PreviewFraming to an actor handler that records no runtime state and publishes no snapshot, and WallpaperEngine::preview_framing refuses an invalid framing with InvalidInput before any message is sent. The bridge reads the position from the wallpaper config when it builds scenes: config::FramingCfg (pan_x, pan_y, centre 0.5; normalized() pulls an axis into 0..=1 and sends a non-finite one to the centre; to_scene() always yields a valid SceneFraming) is the new MonitorRender.framing field. A wallpaper file that fails to parse is set aside as corrupted with all its settings, so reading is lenient: an out-of-range axis is clamped, and an axis that is not a number or a framing that is not an object reads as centred, never as a parse error. The key is omitted while centred, so the wallpaper config stays at schema version 1 and an older build ignores the key. SceneDescBuilderExt::build_from_wallpaper_config reads it from the display's render override beside the scaling mode and factor and hands it to the SceneTemplate builder; ActivationInputs::build_owned sets a mirror's scene to the centre explicitly, because a mirror copies its source's scene but has its own display settings and a later live change on the source never reaches the mirror's handle. NativeVideoWallpaperDesc, native_video_candidate and the admission key are untouched: the native player ignores the position. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-core --lib framing): defaults, validation at every entry point, same_wallpaper and template round trip in project::scene; descriptor seeding, the two inheritance directions and the rebuild-versus-unchanged classification in engine::runtime; the stored template in engine::state; the new wallpaper's framing in engine::actor; the refusal before the actor in engine::tests. Bridge (cargo test -p wallpaper-bridge --lib -- config::wallpaper tests::activation_plan): a centred display writes no framing key and a saved position round-trips; hand-edited values degrade to clamped or centred ones without losing the file's other settings and never reach the engine invalid; the position reaches only the scene built for its display, whichever selector addresses that display; a mirror is centred when its source is positioned; and a position changes neither the native video descriptor nor its admission key. The bridge moves a wallpaper live: WallpaperBridge::set_display_position(wallpaper_id, display_id, pan_x, pan_y) (message SetDisplayPosition; an axis passed as None keeps its saved value) refuses any given axis that is not a finite fraction in 0..=1 with InvalidInput before changing anything (no silent clamping at the API), writes the position into both copies of the wallpaper draft with WallpaperOptionsDraft::set_position_immediate (committed and current, like the scaling mode, so Cancel keeps it and Apply neither sees a pending change nor reopens the scene; the scale factor stays Apply-gated), saves the wallpaper config, then asks the new EngineFacade::set_framing (RealEngineFacade forwards to WallpaperEngine::set_framing, ArcEngineFacade and the two playback test engines implement it, FakeEngineFacade records framing_calls(), can fail_next_framing() and updates the stored direct-assignment template as the real engine does) to move the scene that runs on that display, without a rebuild. A position equal to the saved one writes nothing and tells nobody; a failed save is undone in the draft so the same position asked again is saved; a refused engine update leaves the position saved and the next reconcile builds the scene at it, because the stored template no longer matches. requires_reconcile no longer treats a draft-only display entry holding a non-centred position as a default entry. One UniFFI method is added, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated by scripts/build.py. Bridge only: no C++, no change to the config schema. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-bridge --lib -- display_position wallpaper_options_draft drafts::): the live scene is told once with the live handle and is not reopened by a display refresh, a restart opens it at the saved position, the same position again writes and asks nothing, an axis left out keeps its value, naming neither axis changes nothing, NaN, infinite and out-of-range axes are refused whole (the good axis of a pair too) with nothing saved or sent, an unknown display or wallpaper saves nothing, Cancel keeps the position while undoing a pending scale factor and Apply does not reopen the scene yet carries the position into one it does reopen, a refused engine update keeps the position for the next reconcile, a failed save is retried, two displays keep their own positions, and a display that shows nothing can be positioned for later. The bridge reports each display's position to the app and to the lock-screen export. A new uniffi record api::BridgeFraming (pan_x, pan_y, always a finite fraction in 0..=1; From<SceneFraming> and From<FramingCfg>, the latter through to_scene so a saved value that is not valid reads the way it plays) is a field of BridgeDisplayConfigRow, which the wallpaper options snapshot fills from the display's saved render (a display with none reads centred), and of BridgeLockScreenScene, which lock_screen_scenes fills from the SceneDesc that ActivationInputs::build produces from the committed configuration with native video disabled. So the export covers a scene and a video the desktop plays natively, is the centre for a mirror (its scene is centred, see above) and for a web page (which fills its window), and never holds a draft. The row's dirty and can_restore_defaults already compare the whole render with the default, so a moved display enables Restore defaults without further code. BridgeDisplaySettingsRow, BridgeMonitorInfoRow, BridgeNativeVideoWallpaper, BridgeWebWallpaper and BridgeWallpaperPreview are unchanged: the native player, web pages and previews take no position. The two records change in the generated Swift bindings; no FFI function is added, so the header and checksums are unchanged. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-bridge --lib display_position): the options snapshot reports each display's position and offers to restore it only for a moved display, the reply to a move already carries it, a restart loads it, and the lock-screen export carries a scene's and a video's saved position, centres a web page and a mirror, and follows a position at once while an unapplied scale factor stays out. The bridge also shows a drag in progress: WallpaperBridge::preview_display_position(wallpaper_id, display_id, pan_x, pan_y) (message PreviewDisplayPosition; an axis passed as None follows the saved position, a given axis that is not a finite fraction in 0..=1 or an unknown wallpaper id is InvalidInput, and a display that is gone or that no engine scene draws, a native video for one, is a silent Ok) asks the new EngineFacade::preview_framing (RealEngineFacade forwards to WallpaperEngine::preview_framing, ArcEngineFacade and the two playback test engines implement it, FakeEngineFacade records preview_framing_calls() and stores nothing) and returns, with no save, no generation bump, no snapshot bundle and no log line, so the config file, the options and the lock-screen export do not change. The bridge remembers which scenes were previewed (previewed_framing): SetDisplayPosition for a position equal to the saved one still tells such a scene the saved position once, because a drag that ends where it began fires no change event in the page and the renderer would otherwise stay on the last step shown, and a committed move or that restore clears the mark (a refused engine update keeps it, so asking again retries). state::drafts gains saved_framing and moved_framing, which both messages share. One more UniFFI method is added, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated by scripts/build.py. Tests (cargo test -p wallpaper-core --lib framing; cargo test -p wallpaper-bridge --lib display_position): WallpaperEngine::preview_framing refuses an invalid position before it asks the actor and forwards a valid one; a preview tells the fake engine's preview call once per step with the live handle, writes no file, does not change the export or the options, leaves nothing for a display refresh to rebuild and a restart opens the scene centred; an axis left out follows the saved position, not the last step; invalid positions and an unknown wallpaper are refused with nothing shown while a display no scene draws is not an error; a release after a drag is an ordinary commit that saves and clears the mark; a drag that ends at the saved position puts the scene back without writing, a scene of another display is not told, and a refused release keeps the mark for the next try. Device-free: no renderer or window is opened, so how SceneRuntime::set_framing and SceneRuntime::preview_framing behave on a live renderer was not exercised here.
renderer.heldWallpaperChanges: 2026-10-13: A wallpaper the load journal holds back is now reported as state instead of an English line in the app errors. BridgeAppSnapshot gains `held_wallpaper_ids` (sorted ids of held wallpapers that a display is assigned to; an unassigned hold is kept in the journal but not reported), and WallpaperBridge gains `release_held_wallpaper(wallpaper_id)`, a message that opens the wallpaper through reconcile_configured and lifts the hold only after that reconcile succeeded: a failed reconcile leaves it held in both the actor and the journal, and a crash during the attempt counts against the wallpaper again. A wallpaper that is not held is left alone. Two UniFFI changes, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated by scripts/build.py. Bridge only: no C++, no change to config.toml or load-journal.json. Unit tests (tests/crash_loop_guard.rs) cover the sorted field, the release, a stale release, a failing release and an unassigned hold against the fake engine.
renderer.loadJournalChanges: 2026-10-12: The bridge keeps a load journal (engine/load_journal.rs, file load-journal.json beside config.toml) of the wallpapers it is about to open or replace, written before the engine is asked and kept for a 20 s settle window after the first frame. A launch that finds entries left by another session counts one strike per wallpaper; at two consecutive strikes the wallpaper is held: ActivationInputs gains `held` and slots() leaves its display out of the scene, web and native-video plans, and Bootstrap keeps the set in BridgeActorState::held_wallpapers (see heldWallpaperChanges for how the app learns of it). Apply releases a hold (and reconciles even when the draft is unchanged), an app update (WALLPAPER_MACHINE_BUILD, set by the host from the bundle version and build) or a later load that survives the settle window clears strikes, a quit clears the record, and nothing is ever deleted. reconcile_with now takes a LoadGuard and uses ActivationInputs::build_owned, which pairs each scene with the wallpaper that owns it (a mirror takes its source's). ConfigStore::root and displays_awaiting_first_frame become reachable from the bridge. Bridge only: no C++, no change to config.toml or the wallpaper config schema; one new file, load-journal.json, version 1. Unit tests cover the journal and the bootstrap, apply and shutdown paths against the fake engine; a real crash while a scene loads is not reproducible headlessly.
renderer.wallpaperPreviewChanges: 2026-10-08: Add a read-only wallpaper preview descriptor with current draft properties, preserving Web combo scalar types and a frame-rate request capped at 30 FPS (Web pages honor this cooperatively). Export does not select, assign, save or start desktop wallpapers. Isolated native preview surfaces are implemented in App/ using the existing C renderer API.
renderer.loadJournalShutdownChanges: 2026-10-13: WallpaperBridge keeps a clone of the actor's LoadJournal and closes it in `shutdown` before the Shutdown request is sent. The actor handles one message at a time and Bootstrap, RefreshDisplays and the other reconciles that await a first frame hold it, so a quit that waited for the actor left the record open for the length of a load, and the next launch counted a strike against a wallpaper that was fine. LoadJournal::clean_shutdown now also latches the journal closed: a scene that starts opening afterwards is not recorded, and a late `succeed` does nothing. Bridge only: no UniFFI change, no C++, no change to load-journal.json. Unit tests (engine::load_journal::tests, tests::crash_loop_guard) cover a quit while startup's reconcile is blocked, a quit from another thread and a load that begins after the quit.
renderer.layerTextureSamplingChanges: 2026-10-03: Image-layer composites honour the source layer's clampuvs (false repeats; true or absent keeps clamp), so models tiling a layer texture no longer smear edge texels into solid bands. Alpha-to-coverage passes write kept samples unblended on both backends instead of also alpha-blending them. randomframe particles carry a fixed per-particle frame value hashed from spawn state (no extra random draws), replacing an integral lifetime that always selected frame 0. Synthetic layer-reference, Metal blend-state and emitter regressions. No wallpaper-specific branches, MSAA, extra passes, mip generation or texture allocations.
renderer.perspectiveScenePlaybackChanges: 2026-10-03: Perspective camera objects register authored-order runtime shots instead of letting hidden presets reattach the shared camera during parsing. Visibility selects the pose and FOV after each tick, with editor-pose fallback. Packaged eye/center/up/FOV paths use predecoded scalar curves, sequential/random queues and bounded catch-up; hidden paths add no animation demand. WPModelObject shares image puppet animation-layer decoding and the existing shared playback across every material slot, runtime controls and attachments, so skinned models upload their bind/animated poses rather than zero bones. Model materials start with opaque 3D blend/cull/depth defaults before authored overrides are read; image defaults remain unchanged. Synthetic scene-schema regressions cover selection, curves, queues, default/explicit material state and per-slot bone uploads. No wallpaper-specific branches, asset edits, new render passes or texture allocations. Camera path zoom/events and cut fades remain unsupported.
renderer.webAudioCaptureChanges: 2026-10-02: Bridge audio demand carries presenting, opted-in web consumers to the production capture worker independently of scene handles. AudioCaptureController atomically updates external demand and suspension, shares one tap with scenes, preserves external ownership during scene cleanup and restores both inputs after a failed transition. Web-only startup uses the same authorization path as scenes; shutdown explicitly releases external capture. Device-free regressions exercise the production demand handler and real controller, including permission, pause, ownership and teardown. No wallpaper-specific rules, polling additions, FFT or delivery-rate changes; no UniFFI or persisted schema change.
renderer.declarationScopeAndCameraFovChanges: 2026-10-04: Shader interface arrays resolve macro values at each original declaration, including active directives between ordinary items and inside earlier functions. Codegen freezes literal bounds before hoisting declarations or emitting input copies; location allocation uses the same resolver. Undefined/nonpositive/expression bounds still fail explicitly. Pipeline revision 10 -> 11 invalidates stale-sized compiled programs. Perspective camera objects with omitted/nonpositive FOV inherit the scene-resolved FOV instead of 50 or an earlier shot's mutable camera FOV; positive overrides remain authoritative in named camera creation, runtime shot selection and non-runtime playback. Synthetic SPIR-V/MSL and camera schema regressions cover per-declaration bounds, undefined/replaced macros, scene/shot overrides and visibility fallback. No new render passes, targets, per-frame paths or wallpaper-specific rules.
renderer.auditMergeCompatibilityChanges: 2026-10-03: Merge the audit renderer and shader changes without dropping the scene/playback review fixes. Stage-interface array resolution follows leading macro undefinitions and redefinitions, matching the audit's uniform and preprocessing behavior; a synthetic regression covers object/function replacements and removed definitions. The expanded renderer registry retains all twelve synthetic scenes, GPU prerequisite handling and fail-closed verdicts. No wallpaper-specific rules or new per-frame work.
renderer.reviewInputValidationChanges: 2026-10-03: Parallax inheritance checks signed and unsigned JSON IDs and parent references against the int32 range before narrowing, so unrelated layers cannot alias through truncation. The layer-alias registration pass skips non-object entries, non-string names and nonnumeric IDs while preserving missing-field defaults. Synthetic scene-schema tests cover both range boundaries, unsigned overflow, declaration order, invalid entries and valid alias-driven script updates. No bridge API, persisted schema, render pass or per-frame work changes.
renderer.reviewFollowupChanges: 2026-10-03: Stage-interface array allocation and emission share one positive-integer/leading-macro resolver; unsupported expressions, missing or late definitions and nonpositive bounds fail explicitly instead of reserving one location. Accepted numeric array layouts are unchanged. Alpha-to-coverage uses unblended coverage only on multisampled attachments, with source-over fallback and coverage disabled for single-sample Metal/Vulkan targets and presentation. Original synthetic GPU regressions cover transparent/partial/opaque pixels and composed coverage; the new Compatibility fixture fails with the preceding renderer. CPU tests preserve the multisample contract. Added steep/rolled camera orientation, shared scaled/zero clock delta and late-registration fallback regressions, and a direct array header include. No new render targets, passes, asset rules, bridge APIs or persisted settings.
renderer.macroInterfaceShaderChanges: 2026-10-02: Numeric combo-sized varying arrays resolve before generated declarations and reserve consecutive interface locations for every element. Legacy builtin conversion visits macro replacements inside functions as well as top-level directives. Synthetic regressions fail before the repairs and compile SPIR-V/MSL afterward, covering annotation defaults, explicit counts, adjacent arrays and nested object/function macros. Reads reached through `#define` aliases and through array-parameter specialization are swizzled too, which is what five installed wallpapers need: their audio-bars shader writes `#define u_AudioSpectrumLeft g_AudioSpectrum16Left` inside `main`. Measured on `3799253558` through `metal_scene_draw_smoke`: audio versus silence changed 929 pixels whole-frame and 0 in the ring annulus before, 11428244 and 66995 after; the frame went from 30.0% to 99.8% non-black as its background, flowers and fog returned. Installed corpus unchanged at 4 pre-existing failures in `3292361861`. `ShaderPipelineRevision::CURRENT` goes 7 -> 8. The same swizzle follows a local array alias (`float s[16] = g_AudioSpectrum16Left;`), whose uses the alias lowering replaces with the target name; no installed wallpaper needs that path today. A `#define` alias with any definition naming a differently widened member, or one naming something not widened, is disqualified permanently rather than re-admitted by a later agreeing branch. Checked on the native backend across all ten installed scenes rather than the one that prompted it: backend decisions are identical before and after, so nothing moves onto a path it had not run on, and `metal translation of ... failed` goes 11 to 8 -- the three repaired shaders, with `lightshafts`, `perspective` and `clipping_mask` unchanged. 2026-09-20 (texture annotation defaults and slot combos): a sampler slot filled only by the shader's own annotation `default` no longer reports itself as author-bound to the shader compiler, so its `combo` stays 0. The default still binds for sampling; only the question the combo answers changed. `WPSceneParser`'s default-texture stabilisation loop fed the defaulted list back as `present`, which turned every `{"combo":...,"default":...}` sampler permanently on: `workshop/3083593512/effects/rounded_mask` then read its corner radius from a white default instead of `u_Radius` and masked the album cover of 3280146735 into a circle. Measured with the probe: that cover goes from an inscribed circle (fill 0.790) to the authored rounded square. Same-seed frames for all ten installed scenes: six byte-identical, and the only change outside the wall-clock text layers is the cover itself. 2026-09-20 (media replay and screen resolution): `MEDIA_EVENT_JSON` was dropped whenever the wallpaper had no scene or runtime, which is exactly the window a settings change opens and exactly when the host replays what is playing, because the rebuilt scene is a new handle. The artwork already survived that window by being parked; the events describing what is playing did not, so a cover group revealed by `mediaPlaybackChanged` stayed hidden until the next live event. SceneWallpaper now retains the latest event per type, in first-arrival order, and replays them when a scene is attached; withdrawing media consent clears them. `engine.screenResolution` no longer follows the cursor viewport, which is the scene's own world extent -- `SceneRuntimeContext::SetScreenResolution` is its own setter and SceneWallpaper publishes `RenderInitInfo::width`/`height`, which are already physical pixels, on scene attach and on surface replacement. 2026-09-21 (project rename): the renamed application is carried into the vendored crates -- `BridgePaths` uses the `app.wallpapermachine` app-support constant and reads the four `WALLPAPER_MACHINE_SUPPORT_ROOT`/`_LIBRARY_ROOT`/`_ASSETS_ROOT`/`_USER_ASSETS_ROOT` overrides the Swift side now exports, the audio-permission failure message names WallpaperMachine in System Settings, and the shader pipeline test reads `WALLPAPER_MACHINE_ASSETS_ROOT` and `WALLPAPER_MACHINE_UNPACK_ROOT`. Names only; no behavior change.
renderer.snapshotStorageChanges: Shader-cache size measurements are shared across snapshot bursts for at most two seconds; explicit settings reads and cache clearing invalidate the measurement. Regression coverage checks directory-walk counts, expiry, new files, and clearing without changing the bridge API.
renderer.loadJournalHoldReleaseChanges: 2026-10-13: ApplyWallpaperOptions carries `user_initiated`, and WallpaperBridge.apply_wallpaper_options gains a `user_initiated` argument (one UniFFI change, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated by scripts/build.py). Only a user-initiated apply calls LoadJournal::forgive: a playlist, schedule or rule that comes round to a held wallpaper no longer lifts the hold and no longer clears a wallpaper's strikes. ok_wallpaper_options, the options dialog's OK, counts as the user's. The apply lifts the hold only in memory and calls forgive once its reconcile has succeeded, as ReleaseHeldWallpaper does, so a crash during the load counts a third strike and holds the wallpaper again; a failed reconcile puts the hold back through a new `restore_hold` field on the internal ReconcileFailed message, and an apply that reconciles nothing forgives at once. Bridge only: no C++, no change to config.toml or load-journal.json. tests::crash_loop_guard covers a rotation back to a held wallpaper, an automated apply leaving a strike count alone, the user's apply starting it over, a failed apply leaving the wallpaper held and a crash while an apply loads it.

auditRemediation.changes: Repair bridge state, persistence and lifecycle consistency; report host startup by current display/wallpaper/reconcile revision instead of treating assignment as first-frame readiness; preserve audio ownership and partial successful work. Register resources without retaining renderer handles indefinitely and persist shader cache updates without dropping existing entries. Correct shader helper, macro and modulo transformations, advance shader pipeline revision to 10, carry affine video UV transforms, and reject unsupported used reflection resources. A zero-size empty media-artwork event explicitly clears cached artwork; malformed partial dimensions remain invalid.
auditRemediation.reviewFollowup: PR #24 review: share effective battery/global frame-rate caps between routing and settings admission keys; simplify bounded artwork validation; ignore dangling source symlinks while retaining other metadata errors.

renderer.releaseTestReliabilityChanges: 2026-10-04: Remove a source-text-only apply-config binding test that depends on bindgen formatting. Synchronize monitor-gap mouse assertions with the fake engine sample barrier instead of fixed completion sleeps. Test-only changes; renderer runtime behavior and notices are unchanged. Follow-up: wait for observed cursor-probe progress and close the monitor gap while the sample barrier holds the poller, removing the remaining completion-sleep and in-flight-probe races.
renderer.firstFrameWaitChanges: 2026-10-05: RealEngineFacade::reconcile_scenes waits for a first frame only on displays where the engine opens or replaces a scene, judged against the engine's live display snapshot (displays_awaiting_first_frame) instead of the descriptors the facade last handed it. A display refresh moves and resizes scenes in place without passing through the facade, and a scene that only gets new geometry keeps its renderer, which announces its first frame once; the next Apply then waited the full 90 seconds on such a display, reported that the wallpaper did not render, and rolled back a wallpaper that was playing (issue #30). The facade keeps only a lock that runs one reconcile at a time. Device-free regressions cover moved, resized, refresh-rate, paused, consumed shader-refresh, new, closed and changed-wallpaper scenes. No API, schema or binding change.
renderer.displayIdentityChanges: 2026-10-05: DisplayIdentity::match_score lets a UUID both sides carry decide on its own, then vendor, model and serial; the unit number stays a last resort and never overrides a UUID or serial that disagrees. is_same_physical_display_as, the primary-display dedupe in DisplayStateModel and the bridge same_physical_identity now use it instead of three diverging copies. AppConfig::sync_known_monitors keeps one [[monitors]] block per display (the first, which the renderer was showing), renamed to the display's current selector, merges [[monitor_settings]] entries (preferring the one under the current selector), retargets mirror references, and keeps only the first block for a disconnected display. selector_for maps an identity display id from before a renumbering to the display's current selector. macOS renumbers displays and renames identical models across reboots and reconnects; each change appended a block, and with two monitors of one vendor and model a stale block matched the other monitor by unit number, so it showed the wrong wallpaper and panel changes never reached it (issue #33). Per-wallpaper [[monitors]] render overrides keep their selectors and still resolve through the identity fallback. Bridge display_identity tests replay the reported four-display configuration; core tests cover identical models sharing a unit number. No API, schema or binding change.
renderer.displayGeometryChanges: 2026-10-12: A display that is still connecting can be listed as active while it reports 0x0 pixels. EngineActor::refresh_displays_now now splits the platform report with plan_refresh: a display without a presentable size stays out of the refresh instead of reaching WallpaperWindow::open, which refuses zero dimensions and made one such display fail every other display's Apply. DisplayStateModel::refresh_connected_keeping lets a display that already runs a scene keep the descriptor it had (matched by id or identity), because leaving it out would plan a Close and reload a scene that is running fine; a display without a record gets none until it reports a size, and a primary display without pixels skips the refresh so every runtime stays as it is. The skip and the ignored displays are logged once per change. The display reconfiguration watcher already schedules another refresh when the display settles. Device-free regressions use synthetic descriptors. No API, schema or binding change; a real display that reports 0x0 while connecting was not reproduced.
renderer.audioDeviceChanges: 2026-10-13: The system-audio tap is rebuilt when the default output device changes. core/src/media/audio/device_watch.rs registers one process-wide CoreAudio HAL listener on the system object for kAudioHardwarePropertyDefaultOutputDevice the first time a watcher starts and never removes it; the callback only walks a static table of debouncers (no per-watcher client data, so it cannot dangle), and a watcher adds itself to the table and removes itself on drop. Notifications are debounced for 300 ms so one Bluetooth switch is one report. AudioCaptureController::restart_capture stops and starts a running tap with the existing consumer (never a new permission request), does nothing while capture is stopped, suspended or unwanted, and remembers a failed start so a retry can start it without another device change.
