The bridge audio worker holds a watcher only while its controller wants capture (OutputWatchGate starts one on the change to wanted and drops it on the change away from it, so a process that never reads audio has none and the HAL listener is not registered until audio is first used), rebuilds on the debounced event, and retries a failed rebuild three times (500, 1000 and 1500 ms) through its own channel from short detached threads, so it never sleeps; a newer device change supersedes pending retries and a retry that finds capture running is ignored. The worker thread now ends through an explicit Shutdown command sent when the last handle drops, because it holds a sender of its own. Giving up is a log line, not an alert; any scene or demand change still starts the tap. Device-free regressions cover the debounce, the controller restart, the retry chain and generations. No API, schema or binding change; whether the tap really stops after a switch on a given Mac, and the HAL listener itself, were not exercised.
renderer.surfaceRecoveryChanges: 2026-10-13: A scene that stops drawing after a failed frame is rebuilt within a budget. core/src/engine/surface_recovery.rs is pure state with injected instants: a ladder of an in-place surface reconfigure after 0.5 s, then a renderer rebuild after 2 s and again after 8 s, counted over a rolling 60 s, giving up without scheduling when the budget is spent, ignoring a failure while an attempt is pending, and refusing a stall check once the budget is spent (a reloaded wallpaper gets a new renderer and with it a fresh budget). OweBackend::open_scene registers the render-failure callback and OweScene keeps the load number so recovery lines carry the same load#N as the lines that opened the renderer; OweScene::surface_health reads the surface health of its own scene. SceneRuntime gains a per-renderer RenderFailureRelay (a watch signal like the audio-requirement relay, so a burst is one report and a report names its renderer instance), a SurfaceRecovery that a rebuild done by recovery keeps and a different wallpaper replaces, and recover_surface, which reconfigures the surface and falls straight through to a renderer rebuild when that fails. EngineActor handles NativeRenderFailed by spending one rung and scheduling RecoverSurfaceAttempt on itself after the delay (holding only a weak reference while it waits); the attempt re-checks the renderer instance, skips a surface that is already drawing again, runs the step, schedules the next rung when it fails, and logs one line per step and one error line when it gives up. A renderer reports a failed frame only after its first present, so an attempt that rebuilt the renderer stays pending and the actor looks at the new renderer once a second (SettleRecoveredSurface, surface_recovery::settle) until it has presented a frame, ending the attempt as a success, or has stopped before drawing, which feeds the failure it never reported to the ladder; a renderer that does neither within 30 s is logged and left alone. WallpaperEngine::recover_surface(display_id, reason) asks for the next rung from outside and returns a RecoveryOutcome. wallpaper-core's tokio dependency gains the time feature for the delay. SceneRuntime also remembers the internal render scale it last set on its renderer (RenderScale) and hands it to every renderer it opens through rebuild_for_desc, so a recovery rebuild, a wallpaper switch or a resolution change no longer brings the scene back at full size while the panel still reports the reduced scale; a renderer that cannot take it fails the rebuild, which is rolled back like any other. Device-free regressions cover the ladder, the relay, the callback lifecycle and the render-scale carry-over; the actor's reaction on a live scene needs a real window and is not covered, and no genuine presentation failure was produced.
renderer.wakeCheckChanges: 2026-10-13: The bridge can confirm after a wake that every scene that should be drawing still is, and repair only the ones that are not. WallpaperBridge::revalidate_scene_presentation(reason) runs engine::revalidate::revalidate_presentation on the bridge's own runtime, outside the actor, one check at a time: it reads the display snapshot and the scene reports, hands a scene whose surface stop latch is set straight to the engine, waits three seconds, reads again, and treats a scene as stalled only when the same scene is still continuous and unpaused and its always-on frames_completed did not move (a counter that went backwards is a replaced renderer). Paused or suspended displays, scenes that update on events or deadlines, and scenes the renderer could not be read for are skipped; presents are never used as the signal because a frame that would repeat the picture completes without presenting. Repair is WallpaperEngine::recover_surface with RecoveryReason::Stalled, so it spends the scene's existing recovery budget and cannot loop. EngineFacade gains recover_surface (forwarded by RealEngineFacade and ArcEngineFacade; the default answers NoScene), and the new uniffi record BridgeSurfaceCheck { display_id, outcome, frames_before, frames_after } carries one row per display with a scene open. The fake engine facade can script successive reads and record repair requests. Device-free regressions use scripted frame counters; whether a surface really stops across a sleep and whether the reconfigure restores it were not exercised. No change to vendored C++.
renderer.webRenderScaleChanges: 2026-10-13: BridgeWebWallpaper carries render_scale, the effective internal render scale (the saved scale, or the battery profile's while Reduced quality is selected and the Mac is on battery, clamped to 0.25..=1.0), built by the actor from effective_render_scale(). RenderBackendSurvey::render_scale_supported is now true while a web wallpaper runs, so the Performance control is no longer reported as not applicable for web-only desktops. The stale ActivationInputs::frame_rate_cap documentation is corrected (call sites already pass the battery-capped ceiling). Swift bindings are regenerated from the extended record; the host applies the scale to window.devicePixelRatio. Regression coverage in the bridge's apply_options and quality_settings tests. No wallpaper assets or native rendering behavior are changed.
renderer.launchAtLoginApprovalChanges: 2026-10-13: LaunchAtLoginStatus gains RequiresApproval for a login item the user switched off in System Settings (SMAppServiceStatus::RequiresApproval), which used to read as a plain off that registering could turn on; registering leaves such an item switched off, so the toggle silently did nothing. SystemLaunchAtLogin now reaches the service manager through a small LoginItemService trait, so its rules are tested without touching the real one: enabling while approval is pending returns RequiresApproval without calling register, disabling unregisters, an app outside Applications stays Unavailable, and not-registered, not-found and unknown states still read as off. BridgeSettingsSnapshot gains launch_at_login_needs_approval (a uniffi record field, bindings regenerated); launch_at_login_available stays true and launch_at_login_enabled false for RequiresApproval. The two-second status cache is unchanged. No vendored C++ is touched.
renderer.hiddenPropertyRowChanges: 2026-10-13: The bridge's wallpaper options snapshot (actor/snapshots.rs) keeps a property that a visibility rule hides, with enabled false and its current value and modified state, instead of leaving the row out; a rule that cannot be read still leaves the property enabled. Hosts list the enabled rows. A doc comment on BridgePropertyDescriptor.enabled records this (bindings regenerated for the comment only). Bridge-side Rust only: no vendored C++, field, API or schema change. Synthetic-id regressions in tests::property_snapshot.
renderer.visibilityRuleChanges: 2026-10-13: The bridge crate's property visibility rule parser (project/condition.rs) also reads parenthesised groups, constant true and false, single-quoted text, === and !==, and [a, b].includes(id.value) list membership, so rules such as `a.value == true && [3, 4, 5].includes(n.value)` and a bare `false` decide whether a property is listed instead of being left visible. Rules are bounded (2,048 bytes, 24 levels of nesting, 256 list elements) because project files are untrusted; anything not read in full stays an error and its property stays visible. ProjectModel::unreadable_condition_count backs one app-log line per wallpaper at library refresh. Bridge-side Rust only: no vendored C++, API, schema or binding change. Synthetic-id regressions in project::condition, project::manifest and tests::property_snapshot.
renderer.labelLocalizationChanges: 2026-10-13: The bridge crate reads a project's general.localization tables (project/localization.rs: Wallpaper Engine locale code to token to text, bounded to 64 languages, 4,096 tokens each, 2 KiB per text and 1 MiB overall because project files are untrusted) into ProjectModel::localization, shared by Arc since every property edit clones the model. The host names the languages with the new set_label_languages export (transient actor state, never persisted, with English always added as the fallback), and the options snapshot replaces a property label or combo option label that is exactly a token with the text from the first language that has it. Bridge-side Rust only: no vendored C++ or schema change; the uniffi API gains set_label_languages, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated. Synthetic-id regressions in project::localization, project::manifest and tests::property_snapshot.
renderer.restoreAllDefaultsChanges: 2026-10-13: The bridge crate gains a restore_all_property_defaults export (RestoreAllPropertyDefaults message, WallpaperOptionsDraft::restore_all_property_defaults, ProjectModel::user_asset_property_ids) that stages the authored default for every property in the draft, hidden and stale overrides included, and leaves file and directory properties alone because those are written to the committed config the moment they are chosen. Nothing is committed until Apply and cancel_wallpaper_options brings every value back. Bridge-side Rust only: no vendored C++ or schema change; the uniffi API gains restore_all_property_defaults, so App/Bridge/Generated is regenerated. Regressions in tests::property_snapshot.
renderer.powerWatcherChanges: 2026-10-13: The bridge's power-source watcher thread sleeps in its run loop until IOKit reports a change or a latched wake source is signalled, instead of waking every five seconds to read a stop flag; dropping the watcher signals it, so shutdown no longer waits on a timeout. PowerNotificationContext no longer depends on the engine and takes its power read and delivery as closures, and a delivery the actor rejected is retried at the next callback instead of being remembered as delivered. Device-free regressions cover prompt shutdown of a sleeping and of a just-started watcher, a wake signalled before the loop runs, and retry after a rejected delivery. 2026-10-13 (second change): WallpaperBridge gains resample_power_source(), a synchronous call that asks the watcher to read the power source again and hand it over only if it differs from what the actor last took; the host calls it when the Mac wakes (and once more two seconds later), because a plug or unplug during sleep may not be reported. The request is a latched flag plus the existing wake source, so the thread still sleeps until something happens; a reading that fails (unknown source) is not handed over, so a slow answer after waking cannot erase a known source. The binding gains one method, no schema change. Device-free regressions cover a changed source delivered once, a rejected delivery offered again, an unreadable source left alone, a resample requested as the watcher stops or after it stopped, and the battery policy applied through the bridge from a source change nobody reported; a real plug or unplug during sleep is not exercised.
renderer.wallpaperLayerSwapChanges: 2026-10-13: Replacing the scene a window shows is a transaction on its CAMetalLayer. WallpaperWindow::begin_layer_swap (window.rs) installs the fresh layer under the NSView as update_layer did, but keeps the layer it replaced in a LayerSwap instead of releasing it; LayerSwap::finish releases it, and WallpaperWindow::revert_layer_swap puts it back under the view with the window, content view and layer geometry of the display it was installed for (written only where it differs, inside a transaction with implicit actions disabled) and releases the abandoned layer. A LayerSwap is consumed by either, and update_layer, still used by reconfigure_for_display, is begin plus finish with unchanged behaviour. SceneRuntime::rebuild_for_desc swaps the layer with begin_layer_swap, and when open_scene fails, or the new renderer rejects the saved settings after it was closed, reverts the swap, logs one warning and returns the original error, instead of restoring only the window geometry: the old renderer, which the engine puts back, had been left drawing on a layer that was no longer in the view while the display showed the empty replacement, and the bridge's restore found the descriptor unchanged and rebuilt nothing. A successful replacement changes no pixels. No bridge API, schema or binding change, and no vendored C++ change. The layer-swap cases in tests::general::platform need a real window (WE_RUN_MACOS_WINDOW_TESTS, an authorized desktop run), are listed in scripts/check_rust.py CORE_EXCLUSIONS, and have not been run; the revert in a real window after a forced open_scene failure is unverified.
renderer.wallpaperLayerAnnouncementChanges: 2026-10-13: A wallpaper window announces every content layer it gets. window.rs posts WallpaperMachine.wallpaperLayerInstalled on the default NSNotificationCenter, synchronously on the main thread, with the new CAMetalLayer as the object and userInfo displayID (NSNumber, DisplayDesc.display_id) and reason (NSString: open, replace or reconfigure, the LayerInstall enum): from WallpaperWindowBuilder::open just before orderFrontRegardless, and from WindowHandleRef::replace_metal_layer once the new layer is under the view and shaped. begin_layer_swap takes the LayerInstall (SceneRuntime::rebuild_for_desc passes Replace) and update_layer, used by reconfigure_for_display, announces Reconfigure; a reverted swap posts nothing. Additive: the notification is the only new behaviour, with no observer it is a dictionary allocation and a no-op post per layer, and no pixel changes. No bridge API, schema or binding change and no vendored C++ change; the Swift observer lands separately. window::tests pins the payload on a private center and the name and reason strings that Swift matches literally; tests::general::platform::case_wallpaper_window_announces_layers needs a real window (WE_RUN_MACOS_WINDOW_TESTS, an authorized desktop run), is listed in scripts/check_rust.py CORE_EXCLUSIONS and has not been run, so that the post precedes the first composite is unverified.
renderer.nativeMetalDefaultChanges: 2026-10-13: Bridge: SceneRendererModeCfg defaults to NativeMetalPreferred, and AppConfig gains native_metal_default_applied (serde default false, true in AppConfig::default()): migrate_legacy_keys moves a config that lacks it to NativeMetalPreferred once and sets it, so a later choice of Compatibility is kept. Older builds ignore the key and the schema version stays 1. Tests: config::store a_config_from_before_the_native_default_moves_to_it_once and the updated defaults, tests::scene_settings scene_renderer_defaults_to_native_metal_and_reaches_both_facade_halves.
renderer.shaderLightingV1Changes: 2026-10-14: The shader crate writes Wallpaper Engine's LightingV1 block in at `#require LightingV1` (preprocess/lighting.rs) when the pass's LIGHTING macro is non-zero: `uniform vec4` arrays per light kind (g_LPoint_Color/Origin, g_LSpot_Color/Origin/Direction/Exponent, g_LTube_Color/OriginA/OriginB, g_LDirectional_Color/Direction) sized by the LIGHTS_POINT/SPOT/TUBE/DIRECTIONAL macros (clamped to 0..15) and a PerformLighting_V1 unrolled per light that calls the author's ComputePBRLightShadow / ComputePBRLightShadowInfinite (and PointSegmentDelta for tubes) from the shader's own common_pbr_2.h, spots attenuated by smoothstep over their cone cosines, every shadow factor 1. Before, the directive was dropped and codegen substituted a headlight stub (albedo x N.V) that ignored every light. Any other `#require` is still dropped, and the stub remains for a shader that calls PerformLighting_V1 without requiring it. ShaderPipelineRevision 13 -> 14 so cached programs built with the stub recompile. Shape read from the 2.8.42 binary's generator (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: preprocess::lighting unit tests; pipeline.rs a_lit_pass_gets_wallpaper_engines_light_arrays_sized_by_the_scene_on_both_backends, an_unlit_pass_declares_no_light_arrays, every_asset_shader_that_requires_lighting_compiles_lit_on_both_backends.
renderer.hlslMacroChanges: 2026-10-14: The shader crate (crates/shader) defines HLSL and HLSL_SM40 as 1 for every stage (preprocess/macros.rs), keeping GLSL as 1 so the `#if GLSL` paths stay picked; HLSL was 0, which `#ifdef HLSL` cannot tell apart from 1 but `#if HLSL` can. Why: Wallpaper Engine 2.8 compiles its shaders as HLSL, prepending `#define HLSL 1` and `#define HLSL_SM40 1` and never defining GLSL (decompiled FUN_1400d5070 holds the prefix `#define HLSL 1\n#define HLSL_SM40 1\n` beside the `blobsSM40/` compile cache and the HLSL fallback shader paths, and the dialect's cast and sampler macros sit in a prelude string in the same binary; interoperability only, no code copied). Effect: every `#if HLSL` block of the shipped and local shaders is taken. effectcomposebackground (the first pass of every compose:true effect) and the COPYBG/TEX paths of the god rays, shine and clipping mask effects turn v_ScreenCoord.y over only there, so a layer composed over the screen sampled it mirrored vertically on both renderers. The other blocks are handled by rules, not per shader: a stage-qualified declaration that restates a builtin variable the backend provides and compiles (`in uint gl_VertexID;`, `in uint gl_InstanceID;`, `gl_Position`, `gl_FragCoord` and the like, under any of in/out/attribute/varying) is dropped (PlannedDeclaration::BuiltinRedeclaration) where it had become a vertex attribute of that name, and a new builtin_variables strategy spells the uses gl_VertexIndex and gl_InstanceIndex, which Naga types uint; a gl_ builtin the backend lacks (gl_ViewportIndex) or recognises but cannot compile (gl_ClipDistance, gl_CullDistance, gl_DrawID, gl_PrimitiveID), and an index declared as the author's own non-uint variable, keep their former handling and are not renamed; the author's own `mat3 inverse(mat3)` (common_perspective.h) is called by Naga in place of its builtin on both targets and suppresses the generated Metal helper as any user inverse does; the `pow(falloff + FLT_MIN, exponent)` of common_pbr_2.h is finite and defined at zero falloff; the bokeh brace-list kernel is read by Naga as it stands. ShaderPipelineRevision 14 -> 15. Tests: tests/preprocess.rs default_macros_are_wallpaper_engines_direct3d_dialect_plus_glsl and every_spelling_of_the_hlsl_test_takes_the_direct3d_branch; tests/legalize.rs a_redeclared_vertex_builtin_makes_no_attribute_and_its_uses_reach_the_builtin, an_index_builtin_read_through_a_macro_is_renamed_where_the_macro_is_written, a_builtin_is_dropped_whatever_its_qualifier_and_one_the_backend_lacks_is_not, an_index_restated_through_attribute_or_varying_is_dropped_and_not_given_a_location, a_name_the_backend_cannot_compile_as_a_builtin_keeps_its_declaration, brace_initialized_arrays_compile_on_both_backends; tests/naga_metal.rs a_redeclared_vertex_and_instance_index_reach_metal_as_builtins_not_attributes and a_stage_declaring_its_own_matrix_inverse_compiles_on_both_targets_and_calls_it; tests/pipeline.rs a_compositing_effect_turns_the_screen_coordinate_over_under_if_hlsl, a_bokeh_style_kernel_compiles_from_its_if_hlsl_brace_list_on_both_backends, the_direct3d_light_falloff_is_defined_for_zero_and_stays_finite_on_both_backends, a_redeclared_vertex_index_is_no_vertex_input_of_the_compiled_program, asset_vertex_stages_with_if_hlsl_blocks_compile_on_both_backends; MetalSceneDraw.ACompositingEffectSeesTheScreenUprightOnBothRenderers (failed before, passes after; the other 73 metal_scene_draw_smoke tests pass before and after). Corpus A/B over 1,269 (scene, shader, combos) programs from the 60 local scenes, compiled for SPIR-V and MSL (2,538 compilations): 2,538 compile before and after, no regression, none fixed; 2,126 legalized outputs are byte-identical and 412 differ only in the taken blocks (author inverse 224, light falloff 164, bokeh kernel 20, screen coordinate 8; four outputs carry two of these). The engine-level corpus smoke (unpack_shader_compile_smoke) gives identical reports before and after; it skips the layers whose puppet models the unpack left out, so those were compared only through the crate-level jobs (combos the scene files write, not the engine-derived ones). Real scenes were compared by render-pass counts, not pixels. Not handled, found on the way: the compiler does not supply the dialect's prelude macros CASTI/CASTU/CASTF/CAST4U, DECLARE_SAMPLER2D_PARAMETER and MAKE_SAMPLER2D_ARGUMENT, so the morph-target and fur stages that read them still do not compile on their own.
renderer.sceneResolutionChanges: 2026-10-15: A 2D scene (an authored canvas, not display-sized, not a plain video) can be rasterized at the size the canvas is presented at on the display instead of at the canvas's own size, so a display with more pixels than the canvas is not fed an upscaled picture; Wallpaper Engine rasterizes a scene at the output size (the owner's choice of semantics; not re-measured against a Wallpaper Engine frame here). Engine: SceneResolution (Canvas, Display) with the process-wide SetSceneResolution/CurrentSceneResolution (the engine's own default is Canvas, so every harness that builds a scene without a host is unchanged), Scene::resolution, owe_set_scene_resolution and owe_current_scene_resolution. ResolveScreenBoundRenderTargetSizes (VulkanRender/PassCommon.hpp, shared by both backends) takes a SceneRasterSurface and, in Display mode, sizes the raster as ResolveSceneDisplayExtent (the FILL layout of the canvas over the output in whole points at the display's backing scale, zoom left out so a slider does not rebuild the graph) times the render scale, capped by CapRasterExtent at the device's longest texture (Metal: Apple's published limit for the GPU family; Vulkan: maxImageDimension2D). The default target and every screen-bound target follow that raster; the canvas stays the source extent (scene_extent, layout, cursor mapping, scripts, camera) and an unbound author-sized target keeps scaling by ResolveRenderScaledSize alone. A perspective scene, a plain video and a media-sized default target do not read it. ApplyRenderScale on both backends takes the resolution too and rebuilds the targets only when the scale changed or the choice changed for a scene that has a canvas to rasterize; the render handler re-reads the process choice on SET_RENDER_SCALE and when a graph is built, so the host re-sends the render scale to every open scene when the choice changes, and a replaced surface (FINISH_SURFACE_RECONFIGURE) rebuilds the raster with the graph. VulkanRender's present key includes the resolution. Bridge: QualityCfg::scene_resolution (SceneResolutionCfg, `[quality] scene_resolution`, default display), the SetSceneResolution message and WallpaperBridge::set_scene_resolution ("display" or "canvas", any other name refused), pushed to the engine in Bootstrap before any scene opens and on a change, followed by apply_effective_render_scale; BridgeSettingsSnapshot::scene_resolution; wallpaper_core::SceneResolution and WallpaperEngine::set_scene_resolution. The lock-screen extension never sets it, so it keeps the canvas. Cost, headless (UnchangedPresent.LocalProjectEnergyIsMeasuredHeadlessly with WE_TEST_ENERGY_RESOLUTION and WE_TEST_ENERGY_SCALE_FACTOR, 60 fps clock, 20 s windows, canvas/display/display/canvas, 3456x2234 surface at 2x, 1920x1080 canvases): a bloom and effect-chain scene on Native Metal took 1.62 -> 3.42 ms of own GPU time per frame, 35 -> 94 MB of render targets (metal_scene_draw_smoke with WE_TEST_METAL_RESOLUTION) and 380 -> 455 MB peak footprint; on Compatibility 1.91 -> 3.27 ms and 399 -> 480 MB; a 26-layer scene of mostly author-sized buffers 1.76 -> 2.33 ms, 132 -> 160 MB of render targets and 515 -> 555 MB peak footprint (about +-30 MB of run-to-run noise); CPU time per frame did not move; energy was not measured. Both renderers drew those two scenes byte for byte alike in both modes (DrawTheSamePictureOnBothRenderers with WE_TEST_COMPARE_RESOLUTION, 3456x2234 at 2x). Tests: RasterResolution.* in render_scale_test, MetalSceneDraw.A2DSceneIsRasterizedAtTheSizeItIsPresentedAtWhenTheHostAsksForTheDisplay, MetalSceneDraw.ASceneRasterizedForTheDisplayIsTheSamePictureOnBothRenderers, UnchangedPresent.ARunningSceneTakesTheResolutionTheHostChoosesOnBothRenderers, bridge tests::scene_settings and config::store::tests, wallpaper-core owe::scene_demand::tests.

sceneEngine.videoRebuildChanges: 2026-10-16: A scene's video decoders are kept open across a rebuild of the render graph for the same scene, and a video that is opened under a running clock is sought to it once and left to land, its open waiting for no seek. Not a rule read from Wallpaper Engine's binary: it resizes a text card's buffers in place after every layout (textEffectBufferChanges) and touches nothing else a scene holds, so it has no reopening to compare, and the frame of Wallpaper Engine's that the re-test of 40 scenes found this against is a still one. The rule here is ours, for a defect of our build, and there is no function address to cite; what Wallpaper Engine shows, a video that neither goes back to the first frame of its clip nor stops when a clock's digits change size, is what the kept decoders give. Found: the commit that sizes a text effect's buffers from its card has the host build the render graph again whenever the card changes size in texels, which closed the scene's videos (MetalRender::releaseGraph through MetalVideoTextures::release, TextureCache::Clear) and opened them again at the head of the clip; FfmpegVideoTextureSource::refreshFrame then asked for a seek to the clock on every call while the frame on offer lagged by more than a second, each call restarting the decode from the keyframe and dropping what the last had decoded, so a clip whose seek took longer than a draw stayed on its first frame; and every open of a video packaged in the scene reads, copies and hashes the whole file (WriteVideoPayloadToTemp, utils::genSha1, about 7 ms a megabyte), which held the render thread for 0.2 to 2.5 s per rebuild. Now, keeping: SceneWallpaper::rebuildRenderGraph calls the new clearLastRenderGraphForRebuild (SceneRendererHandle, MetalRender, VulkanRender) when it builds the graph of the scene it is drawing again; a scene that is replaced still calls clearLastRenderGraph, which closes everything, and a scene that arrives has no graph to clear. On Native Metal MetalVideoTextures::hold moves each open source (the decoder, its frame-selection tracker and what has been reported of its work) to a held map and releases the rest as release() does; MetalVideoTextures::prepare takes a held source back by its texture key before it parses or opens anything, gives it the layer's clock (State::playbackFor, which beginFrame also uses) and refreshFrame as a draw would, and goes on to the same format checks; a source that fails when given the clock is dropped and opened like any other. MetalRender::Impl::compile closes what was held and not taken back (closeHeld, through AUTO_DELETER, however the compile ends), MetalRender::compileRenderGraph closes it when it refuses a compile because the renderer has no surface (not initialised, as after releaseSurface); clearLastRenderGraph and destroy close it too; ApplyRenderScale holds the sources before its compile, so a render-scale change on Native Metal keeps them as the Compatibility backend already did (TextureCache::ClearRenderTargets). On Compatibility TextureCache::ClearForRebuild does what Clear does but moves each VideoTex, without the frames imported from it (images of the graph that went), to m_held_video_tex_map; TextureCache::FindVideoTex gives back the slots of a video that is open or takes a held one back and asks it for its frame at the scene's clock (UpdateVideoFrame); CustomShaderPass::prepare asks it before it parses a texture the scene declares a video, so a video that two passes bind is not read twice either, which it was; CreateTex asks it for an image that was read anyway; VulkanRender::compileRenderGraph closes what was not taken back (CloseHeldVideos, through an AUTO_DELETER declared ahead of the guard that refuses a compile, so a refused compile closes them too), and clearLastRenderGraphForRebuild closes them when its clear fails after setting them aside; Clear (releasePresentation, a clear that is not for a rebuild), DiscardAfterDeviceLoss and the cache's destruction close it too. What identifies a video is its texture key within the scene that is drawing: only the rebuild of that scene holds anything, and holds it until the compile that follows ends, so nothing is kept across scenes or surfaces. Compatibility's CloseHeldVideos and Native Metal's prepare (of videos or of none) publish OWE_RC_VIDEO_SOURCE_COUNT and OWE_RC_VIDEO_SOURCE_INSTANCE, so after a compile the counters describe the videos it ended with; Native Metal's closeHeld only drops the held videos, so after a refused compile its counters keep the last prepare's values. No per-frame cost: the added work is a map lookup per video texture at a compile. No memory beyond what was open: the held decoders are the ones that were, their imported frames go as before, and a decoder decodes on only to fill its own queue while it waits. Now, opening: a video opened under a running clock (a scene that falls back to the other renderer, a surface split off a shared decoder with shared decode on, a held decoder that failed) opens at the head of the clip, as every open does (FfmpegVideoTextureSource::primeOnce is as it was), and the first call that gives it the layer's clock (MetalVideoTextures::prepare, and CustomShaderPass::prepare through TextureCache::CreateTex(Image&, VideoPlaybackState) and CreateVideoTex, which handed it a zero clock) has refreshFrame ask for the seek there, so it runs beside the rest of the compile. A seek that has been asked for and has not delivered a frame (m_seek_awaiting_frame, seekInFlightCoversLocked) is waited for and not asked for again while the clock has not gone back before its target by more than two frames and has not run past it by more than the forward resync threshold plus the time the seek has been made for (VideoSeekPolicy.hpp: SeekOnItsWayCoversClock, ClockRunOnSeconds), so a seek of any length lands unless the clock jumps again; the forward resync threshold is raised by how late the last seek landed (m_seek_landing_lag_seconds, ForwardResyncSeconds), so a landing a few seconds behind the clock is caught up with by decoding on and not sought to again. One steady_clock read per seek request, one in refreshFrame while a seek is on its way and one at its landing are all that this adds to a frame. Why not open at the clock: an open that waited for the seek held the calling thread, measured on libx264 clips (ffmpeg testsrc2, x264 ultrafast with two B-frames, 3840x2160 and 1920x1080, a keyframe every 250 frames at 30 per second, 3840x2160 at 60 per second with one every 600) through the same source on a Mac with other work running (load average 3 to 5), three runs each, for 0.30 to 0.32 s (1080p, clock 4 s), 0.60 to 0.63 s (8.2 s) and 0.50 s (15 s); 0.46 to 0.59 s, 1.0 to 1.13 s and 0.81 to 0.94 s on the 4K 30 clip; 1.4 to 1.5 s at 5 s on the 4K 60 clip, and failed with 'timed out waiting for the first FFmpeg video frame' after 2.1 to 2.2 s at 9.9 s and 19.9 s on it; a failed open is a whole-scene fallback to Compatibility on Native Metal, which is remembered. The head of the clip is on screen until the seek has landed and the decoder has caught up with the clock, which runs on while the seek is made (the picture within 0.15 s of the clock, from the open): 0.35 to 0.37 s, 0.72 to 0.76 s and 0.57 to 0.65 s on the 1080p clip at 4, 8.2 and 15 s; 0.69 to 0.73 s, 1.38 to 1.48 s and 1.16 to 1.21 s on the 4K 30 clip; 2.3 s at 5 s and 4.0 to 4.2 s at 9.9 s and 19.9 s on the 4K 60 clip, each with one seek request. With the slack for a seek on its way fixed at one second instead, the 4K 30 clip at 8.2 s asked again once, and the 4K 60 clip asked for the seek again each second, did not land at 5 s in six seconds (six requests) and landed at 3.2 to 3.7 s with three requests from 9.9 s on. Measured with the keeping: metal_scene_draw_smoke's comparison run on the clock wallpaper of the re-test (3326873240: five 4K videos packaged in one 235 MB scene, Native Metal, 3456x2024 display size, real-time pacing, a build with a line on stderr for every decoder opened and an environment switch that closes the videos as the build before did, on a Mac at load average 3 to 5). Forced rebuild (WE_TEST_COMPARE_REBUILD_AT=200 WE_TEST_COMPARE_STOP_AFTER_REBUILD=3): the rebuild before draw 200 opened no video and took 0.047 s; with the videos closed as before it opened all five and took 1.41 s (3.44 s in an earlier run at load average 5); the picture three draws later is, outside the box of the clock's digits, pixel for pixel the picture of a run to the same draw that did not rebuild, with the keeping and without it (mean difference over the whole frame 0.063 and 0.064, all of it in the clock's box: the first video opened, the one on screen, has its seek landed while the other four are still opening, so the head of the clip is not seen on this wallpaper, only the wait is). Rebuild the clock caused itself (the local clock set by TZ so that the minute turns over twelve seconds into the run): with the keeping, before draw 381, no video opened, 0.047 s; with the videos closed, before draw 630 (the clock caused a rebuild in some runs and not in others, for a reason not looked into), five opened again, 1.27 s; both pictures equal to the run that did not rebuild outside the clock's box (0.039 and 0.040 over the whole frame). Tests: MetalVideoTexture.AVideoSetAsideByARebuildIsTakenBackAsItIsAndNotReadAgain, .AVideoTheNewGraphDoesNotUseIsClosedWithItsCompile, .VideosSetAsideAreClosedByClosingThemAndByTheObjectGoingAway and .AVideoSetAsideThatFailedWhileItWaitedIsOpenedAgainLikeAnyOther in metal_video_texture_test, and PlaybackGPU.AVideoSetAsideByARebuildIsGivenBackToThePassThatBindsItNotOpenedAgain, .AVideoTheRebuiltGraphDoesNotBindIsClosedWithItsCompile, .AClearThatIsNotARebuildClosesEveryVideoAndSetAsideOnesToo and .AVideoSetAsideThatFailsWhenAskedForItsFrameIsLeftToBeOpenedAgain in playback_gpu_test and PlaybackGPU.APassBindingAVideoSetAsideByARebuildIsGivenItAndTheSceneIsNotReadForIt, which runs a real CustomShaderPass::prepare on a scene whose parser counts and refuses, from two passes that bind one video (with the keeping switched off, three of the four on Native Metal and four of the five on Compatibility fail; with the FindVideoTex ahead of the parse in CustomShaderPass::prepare taken out only the last does); in metal_scene_draw_smoke, MetalSceneDraw.AVideoStaysOpenAndOnItsFrameWhenATextCardResizesTheGraphUnderItOnBothRenderers on a 20 second clip in one group of pictures whose seek to 12 s takes 0.4 s (it waits, bounded by 900 draws, until the picture shows the clock's frame before it rebuilds, instead of rebuilding at a fixed draw; with the keeping switched off it fails on both renderers: decoder 1 then 2 on Compatibility, 3 then 4 on Native Metal, and the clip's frame 0 on screen with the clock at frame 365) and MetalSceneDraw.AVideoTheRebuiltGraphLeavesOutIsClosedOnBothRenderers, where a property hides the video layer in the tick that resizes a caption and the open media files of the process must be back to what they were before the scene (it fails on both renderers with the closing of what was kept taken out of either compile, and passes with the keeping switched off), MetalSceneDraw.AVideoStaysOpenWhenARenderScaleChangeCompilesTheGraphAgainOnNativeMetal (ApplyRenderScale on a Native Metal renderer drawing a video keeps the decoder; it fails with the hold() in MetalRender::ApplyRenderScale taken out) and MetalSceneDraw.AVideoSetAsideForACompileThatIsRefusedIsClosedOnNativeMetal (the open media files of the process are back to what they were after a rebuild whose compile is refused for want of a surface; it fails with the close in MetalRender::compileRenderGraph taken out); in video_source_input_test, VideoSourceClock.AReopenedSourceIsSoughtToTheClockOnceAndLeftToLand (2 to 1263 seek requests where one is asked, before the seek policy, and now also that the call that gives the clock returns with the head still on offer), .AJumpOfTheClockLandsWhileFramesAreAskedForFasterThanASeekTakes (1306 requests on a cold run before the policy, one when its seek landed inside a step: 2 of 6 runs red there), .AClockThatLeavesASeekBehindAsksForAnother and .ASourceThatIsKeptUpWithNeverSeeks, and VideoSeekPolicy.ASeekIsWaitedForAsLongAsItTakesWhileTheClockOnlyRunsOn and .ALandingThatCameLateIsCaughtUpWithByDecodingOn. The tests gained the long-clip writer (synthetic_video.hpp: WriteLongGopVideo, EncodeFrames) and the comparison harness of metal_scene_draw_smoke WE_TEST_COMPARE_STOP_AFTER_REBUILD, WE_TEST_COMPARE_REBUILD_FROM and WE_TEST_COMPARE_REBUILD_AT (test-only). A seek of seconds landing with one request is shown on the clips above only, by a temporary probe that is not in the tree; the long synthetic clip's seek lands in 0.1 s at 2 s, 0.34 s at 10 s, 0.40 s at 12 s and 0.60 s at 19 s with one request. The Compatibility refusals (device lost, a faulted frame) and a clear that fails have no test, since neither can be brought about without losing the device or faulting a frame. Not done: resizing a text card's buffers in place, as Wallpaper Engine does, so a card of another size in texels still builds the graph again; a video layer that a property shows again opens at the head of its clip and is sought to the clock, as the rebuild that hid it left the video out of the graph and closed it; a Compatibility surface that is released and set up again (a display change) still clears the texture cache with its videos; the experimental shared decode's detach (SharedVideoRegistry::detach) still opens its private decoder at the head of the clip and is sought by its first draw. No schema or binding change; SceneRendererHandle, MetalRender and VulkanRender gain clearLastRenderGraphForRebuild. The bridge's set_scene_resolution doc comment (upstream/renderer crates/bridge, regenerated into App/Bridge/Generated) now says a resolution change keeps a scene's video layers open.
sceneEngine.scriptAlphaAllPassesChanges: 2026-10-15: A layer's alpha is applied by the layer's own pass, once (twice on a puppet with bones under effects, as an authored one always was), and a script's write to it (`thisLayer.alpha = x`) reaches that pass, for interoperability; no code copied. (1) SceneRuntimeContext::RegisterNodeAlpha kept one material per layer name and the parser registered the layer's own material and then each of its effect passes under the same name, so the last registration won and a write changed only the pass built last: on a layer under an effect chain the layer's own pass, which carries the picture the chain goes on with, kept its authored alpha (an idle media widget's vinyl disc, whose script fades it to 0 when nothing plays, stayed on screen at 0.69 once its scripted effects were built). NodeAlphaBinding now holds the layer's materials and SetNodeAlpha writes them all; RegisterNodeAlpha takes the whole set and a second registration of a name replaces it; RegisterLayerAlpha collects the materials of an alpha no timeline, script or user property owns and ParseImageObj and ParseTextObj register them once, the first at the end of the layer's setup, so a bound alpha is untouched and still the only writer. (2) ApplyMaterialAlpha, the writer a user-bound, timeline and script-written alpha all use on each pass, also set the g_UserAlpha of every effect pass, but an effect's g_UserAlpha is the effect's own opacity: Wallpaper Engine's Opacity effect (`assets/shaders/effects/opacity.frag` of a scene, `uniform float g_UserAlpha; // {"material":"alpha"}`) declares it (every pass of a layer is seeded with the layer's authored alpha as its g_UserAlpha, the effect's own constantshadervalues `alpha` replaces that, and an effect that sets none keeps the seed), and a layer under N such effects drew a written, bound or keyed alpha as alpha^(1+N), a half as a quarter (the media widgets' album cover, which has two Opacity effects and writes its alpha, would have drawn 0.69 cubed; 51 layers in 10 of the local scenes combine a property-, timeline- or script-driven alpha with an Opacity effect). SceneMaterial::own_user_alpha, set on the passes of the layer's effects, makes ApplyMaterialAlpha leave their g_UserAlpha alone, so the layer's alpha and the effect's multiply as they do for an authored alpha, which is why a written alpha now matches it; their g_Color4 and g_Alpha keep following the layer, which is what an authored alpha gives every pass and what a workshop effect that reads them (texture_override, local scenes 3624257712 and 3675966045) sees. The skinned pass a puppet's chain ends in draws the layer with its own material and takes the layer's alpha; the layer's own pass, the texture sheet the chain starts from, takes it too, so a puppet with bones under effects applies its alpha in two passes, authored or driven (a script's write drew once there before, reaching only the skinned pass registered last, and now draws as the authored one does: a half draws a quarter; a known limitation, docs/testing/renderer.md, not measured against a Wallpaper Engine frame; local scenes 3444535389 and 3808922316 have an authored alpha under such a layer's effects). (3) The passes that blend the layer onto the screen are drawn with a white g_Color4 because the layer's own pass has applied its colour and alpha, as Wallpaper Engine draws them; the passthrough of a chain whose effects a script has all switched off took the layer's colour and alpha a second time (a layer authored below 1 or tinted drew them squared) and is now given white too, so the layer is drawn as one without effects, as Wallpaper Engine draws it. A compose layer's own pass (Wallpaper Engine's composelayer shader, `assets/shaders/composelayer.frag`) reads no g_Color4, so its passthrough keeps the colour and alpha and is registered for the layer's alpha, which makes a script-written, property-bound or timeline alpha reach it as the authored one always did (a compose layer with a bound alpha was not found among the 100 local scenes). Established: Wallpaper Engine's own frames of the scene (two captures, at 8 s and 15 s, draw nothing where the disc sat) and the scene's own scripts (layer 205's visible script steps thisLayer.alpha down to MinAlpha 0 while nothing plays and reads it back each step); that the layer's alpha is applied once, in the layer's first pass, is the existing colour-blend rule (the passthrough that blends onto the screen is drawn with white) and Wallpaper Engine's own frames of bound alpha under Opacity (below). Before and after with the same harness (WE_REF_CLOCK, 3456x2024, 8 s and 15 s): on 3000562427 playing (a synthetic player, playback state 1 with a 512x512 cover) ffe71ded and the fix differ by 1 and 7 px (max 1), while the first version of this change (4a367e75) differs from both by 15433 and 15239 px (max 43 and 53), the Opacity passes of the album cover written too; idle, the disc stays gone (mean absolute difference from Wallpaper Engine's frame over the 300 x 300 px around it 18.3 and 21.0 on ffe71ded, 1.1 and 8.0 with the fix, as with 4a367e75). Of the 23 other local scenes whose scripts write a layer's alpha or that drive a layer's alpha under an Opacity effect (idle, 8 s; 1, 3 and 8 s for the two keyed ones), 14 are identical to the pixel, 7 differ only by wall-clock text and orbiting bodies, as much as ffe71ded differs from itself, and 2 change, both with an alpha bound to a property under an Opacity effect, both toward Wallpaper Engine's frame: 3299228616 (3853 px, an AM label and its reflection, mean absolute error from Wallpaper Engine's frame on them 28.2 before, 7.5 after) and 3616389236 (58785 px of a dotted layer, 42.5 before, 28.9 after). Cost: none per frame (a flag per material and no pass or memory beyond a pointer per material in the layer's alpha set; a write that changes the value stores into each of the layer's materials instead of one, at most the layer's pass count). Tests: MetalSceneDraw.AScriptsLayerAlphaReachesTheLayerWhateverItsEffectsDoOnBothRenderers (a script switching alpha at 0.5 s from 1 to 0 and to half, with no effects, a copying effect, an effect with an alpha of its own at 1 and at 0.8, two of them, every effect off, and with a colour blend mode: opaque before, clear or half transparent after, the renderers equal), .AnAuthoredBoundOrScriptedAlphaIsAppliedOnceUnderEffectsOnBothRenderers (the same shapes at a half, authored, property-bound and script-owned), .ALayerColourIsAppliedOnceWhenEveryEffectIsSwitchedOffOnBothRenderers, .AComposeLayersAlphaFollowsWhatDrivesItOnBothRenderers, SceneSchema.AScriptsAlphaWriteReachesEveryMaterialOfTheLayer, .AnEffectsOwnAlphaIsLeftAloneWhenTheLayersAlphaIsDriven, .AnEffectThatSetsNoAlphaStartsFromTheLayersAuthoredAlphaAndKeepsIt, .APuppetsSkinnedPassUnderEffectsTakesTheLayersAlpha (a script's write equals the authored alpha on every material) and ScriptRuntimeCompat.LayerAlphaWritesReachEveryMaterialOfTheLayer (the read-back of a written alpha included).
sceneEngine.particleInitializerScalingChanges: 2026-10-15: A particle's size and alpha initializers scale the value the particle has so far instead of replacing it, for interoperability; no code copied. The initializer step FUN_14023b340 (the same function as the particleParityChanges entry) starts every particle's size at 0.5, its lifetime at 1 and its colour and alpha at the system's own, then runs the file's initializers in order: the lifetime record stores `rand * range + min` (floored at 0.001), but the size record (switch case 2, array 0x4f) and the alpha record (case 6, array 0x66) store `(rand * range + min) * <the value so far>`, through the shared tail at the label LAB_14023b684, as the colour records (cases 3 to 5) already multiply into the colour arrays. Other records write the same arrays: the event-inheritance record sets (case 0x4c) or multiplies (case 0x4d) the size, a mode-switched record sets, multiplies, adds or subtracts it, and the control point sequence's size reduction multiplies it (the `flags & 4` branch). A file with a second `sizerandom` after the first (the leaf preset of the 3479521040 test scene: 70 to 75, then 0.7 to 1, whose leaves our replacing draw made under a pixel) therefore draws a share of the first, and a file with one is unchanged. WPParticleParser now applies `sizerandom` and `alpharandom` with MutiplyInitSize and MutiplyInitAlpha (the lifetime, velocity, rotation and colour initializers are as they were), and Particle starts from kParticleStartSize and kParticleStartAlpha (Particle.h): our size is held at twice Wallpaper Engine's, since the sprite and rope generators draw half of it, so WE's 0.5 is 1 here and a single `sizerandom` still draws exactly the size it names (the default was 20, which a scaling initializer cannot start from; a file with no size initializer now draws at the engine's start size instead of 20). No local scene or shipped particle file that draws lacks a size initializer: Wallpaper Engine's own `powerup` preset and its `previewpowerup` copy have none, but their `renderer` list is empty; and no local file lists a second `alpharandom`, so the alpha rule rests on the decompile and its unit test, not on a frame. The inherited size records use the engine's own unit too: `multiplysize` (case 0x4d) multiplies the child's size by the parent's, both as the engine holds them, so WPParticleParser multiplies by half of the parent's size held here (kParticleSizeOverEngine in Particle.h), where it multiplied by all of it before, and `setsize` (case 0x4c) copies the parent's size, the same unit, unchanged; no local particle file uses either. Tests: Initializers.ASecondSizeInitializerScalesTheFirstInsteadOfReplacingIt, .ASizeInitializerAloneKeepsItsRange, .TwoSizeInitializersScaleInEitherOrder, .ASecondAlphaInitializerScalesTheFirstInsteadOfReplacingIt, .TheLifetimeStaysReplacedWhileSizeAndAlphaScale, SequenceInitializers.AnInheritedMultiplySizeScalesTheChildByHalfTheSizeHeldForTheParent and ParseLevel.TwoSizeInitializersOfOneFileScaleTheParticlesItSpawns in particle_parity_test; the two tests that read the old default size of 20 (SequenceInitializers.InheritInitialValueCopiesTheParentParticleOfAnEventChild, Oscillators.FrequencyMinimumDefaultsToOneNotZero) now read kParticleStartSize.
sceneEngine.textSceneFontChanges: 2026-10-15: A text layer's font is read as Wallpaper Engine reads it, the Windows fonts a Mac lacks are stood in for by installed faces fitted to the real fonts' advances and lines, a glyph the font lacks comes from the first face of Wallpaper Engine's list that has it, and `opaquebackground` is drawn, for interoperability; no code copied. Wallpaper Engine honours exactly eight whole-string, case-sensitive font keys, systemfont_arial, _calibri, _cambria, _comicsans, _consolas, _sansserif, _segoe and _verdana, read from the Windows Fonts folder (the key table at 0x140484cc0 and its lookup in FUN_140256f20, wallpaper64.c 413089-413160; the folder FUN_1401b0410 374607-374615 and FUN_1401ab7c0, CSIDL_FONTS), takes any other string as a path, draws a font that fails to load in arial.ttf (FUN_1401ad400, 314958-315011) and gives a text object with no font key systemfont_arial (the constructor FUN_140256ae0, 411770-411798); the face index is 0 (FUN_1401acaf0, 318092 on). Before, any suffix of systemfont_ was a CoreText family, missing fonts were Helvetica (whose ascender is 0.77 em and line 1.0 em where Arial's are 0.905 and 1.15), and a text object had no default font. Now SystemFontResolver::ResolveSceneFont takes the eight keys (IsSceneFontKey) and nothing else, gives Arial for everything it does not know, and ResolveInstalledFamily is the plain family lookup, kept for the fallback list and for tests; both cache their CoreText matches: a found face while its file is there (some system faces are downloadable assets in a hash-named folder, so an update can move it, and the next lookup finds the new path), a family not found for 30 seconds (it may be an asset not on the disk yet), so a layout does not run the system's font matching once per face and a font that appears or moves is found without a restart. WPSceneParser.cpp ResolveTextLayerFont tries the key, then a font the wallpaper ships, then Arial (the family branch is gone), WPMiscObject.hpp defaults font to systemfont_arial, and the script font setter without a resolver takes the same rule. Arial, Comic Sans MS, Microsoft Sans Serif and Verdana are on every Mac as the same fonts and stand for themselves; Consolas, Cambria, Segoe UI and Calibri are Andale Mono, Charter, PT Sans and PT Sans (SystemFontFace::fit, TextLayerState::resolved_font_fit, kept by TextLayer::SetFont and in the cache identity): the face is sized at the layer's point size times size_adjust (0.916, 0.996, 0.987, 0.93), the real font's digit advance over the stand-in's (1126, 1135, 1100 and 1038 over 2048 units; a clock's width is its digits), and its rows are set in the real font's line metrics by FreeType's own arithmetic (FT_Request_Metrics: the requested height at 300 dpi, the scale from font units, the ascender rounded up, the descender down, the height to the nearest pixel), which the cards Wallpaper Engine saved pin as sums (Consolas 1.1709 em, Cambria 1.170, Segoe UI 1.331, Calibri 1.2207: 161 and 171 pixels at 33 and 35 points, 156 at 32, 538 and 222 at 97 and 40, 163 at 32 for Calibri by its remembered line). The split between ascender and descender is a Windows font's table and is measured only for Consolas: its ascender is 0.743 em (1521 of 2048), since the digits of the centred clock of workshop 3299228616 stand 12 pixels higher in Wallpaper Engine's frame than 0.920 em (1884) puts them and within 1 pixel of where 0.743 does (rows 361-447 there, 362-448 here; the date's 470-491 against 471-491); Andale Mono rather than Menlo because its digits are 0.7021/0.6001 as tall as wide, Consolas's 0.643/0.5498, so that at Consolas's advance they stand 87 rows, as in the frame, where Menlo's 101. The other three splits are remembered from the fonts' tables and unchecked, and no frame of Cambria, Segoe UI or Calibri text was compared; a probe of the eight keys at three alignments (the ascender and descender fall out of the baselines within one frame) was written and queued, and the capture loader was not running, so it settles nothing here. The glyph fallback replaces the single face with the list (FUN_1401ad670, 317568-317990, read from the 2.8.42 binary): a code point takes the first face held that has it, and the next face of the list is loaded only when none does, in the fixed order arial.ttf, seguiemj.ttf, arialuni.ttf, segoeui.ttf, TwemojiMozilla.ttf (a wallpaper asset), seguisym.ttf, msyh.ttc (face 0) and Malgun.ttf, with white space and the zero-width joiner taking the face of their neighbours, and a code point no face has skipped. Here FaceChain (TextLayer.cpp) walks Arial, the Segoe UI stand-in, Apple Symbols (not asked for CJK Symbols and Punctuation, U+3000-303F, or Halfwidth and Fullwidth Forms, U+FF00-FFEF: it sets some of them centred in the cell, where Microsoft YaHei's stand-in below it sets them as Simplified Chinese does, and a string would mix the two; that Segoe UI Symbol lacks them is inferred, not read from its tables), PingFang SC, Apple SD Gothic Neo and Arial Unicode MS, each opened through the face cache only when asked, the glyphs carrying the index of the face that drew them (kerning stays between glyphs of one face); the colour emoji faces have no stand-in (FreeType's monochrome glyphs do not draw a colour bitmap) and Arial Unicode MS, which is Office's and not Windows', is last, so that Han comes from the face whose Simplified Chinese punctuation Microsoft YaHei has. An opaque background (the +0x594 & 2 bit) is drawn first: a card-sized fontbackground quad at the layer's alpha on the direct path (FUN_140258050, 412287-412372, the material fontbackground.json, with the quad placed by the same translation as the glyph quad) or, where the layer is a composite, the composite cleared to the colour at the layer's alpha where it is otherwise seeded from the scene (FUN_140257c30, 412021-412045); the colour is backgroundcolor times backgroundbrightness, the brightness only when the HDR flag (ctx+0x118 & 0x2000) is set, as the text's. Here the card's shader (BuildTextSceneShader, the filled variants) does it in the card's own pass: inside g_CardInset (the part of the card outside the card's rectangle, which the style's room makes, a DynamicValue the runtime refreshes on a relayout through TextEffectGate::card_inset) it writes the glyph over the fill as the two quads one after the other (straight over on colour and on alpha), or, for a composite, mix(fill, glyph, alpha) with the composite's alpha the fill's plus the glyph's squared alpha over it; the colour and brightness follow a property or script bound to them. Not seen in any local frame (no local scene sets opaquebackground), and under the colour blend add the two are added as one value where the reference adds two quads. Visible: text set in Consolas has the width and digit height of the original (the clock of 3299228616 87 digit rows against 87, 101 before), text in a family named by its bare name or a missing file is Arial (a line of 1.15 em, where it was Helvetica's 1.0 for the families Wallpaper Engine cannot load), the Latin glyph a font lacks is Arial's. Cost: no frame-time, memory or per-frame work; a layout that meets a glyph its font lacks opens at most the six fallback faces once and the cache keeps them (the cache's capacity covers the font, one stand-in and the whole list). Tests: TextObjectRuntime.SceneFontKeysAreTheEightWallpaperEngineKeys, .AMissingFontFileDrawsInArial, .ATextObjectWithoutAFontKeyIsArial, .AMissingWindowsFontIsSetInThatFontsAdvancesAndLine, .AStandInSetsTheBaselineByTheRealFontsAscenderAndDescender, .AGlyphTheFontLacksComesFromTheFirstFaceOfWallpaperEnginesList, .EachFaceOfTheFallbackListDrawsWhatTheFacesBeforeItLack, .CjkPunctuationIsNotDrawnByTheSymbolFace, .AFamilyThatMovedOrAppearedIsFoundAgain and .AnOpaqueBackgroundsColourBrightnessAndInsetReachTheCardsMaterial, MetalSceneDraw.AnOpaqueBackgroundFillsTheCardAtTheLayersAlphaOnBothRenderers and .AnOpaqueBackgroundFillsTheCardAndNotTheRoomAStyleNeedsAroundItOnBothRenderers (the last two fail with the fill off); the parser font tests, FontFallbackHandlesFamiliesMissingFilesAndCorruptAssets, ASystemFontIsOpenedOnceAndNotForEveryLayout and the face-name tests were migrated from the family rule and the single fallback face.
sceneEngine.textCompositeChanges: 2026-10-15: A text layer that draws through a visible effect is a composite of its own, and a text card's padding follows the effects that are visible while a scene runs, for interoperability; no code copied. Wallpaper Engine overwrites such a layer's composite with the scene behind it at alpha 0 (the util/composelayer_clearalpha material, FUN_140257c30, wallpaper64.c 412021-412120), blends the glyphs into it with the font material's translucent blend, which decodes to SRC_ALPHA / INV_SRC_ALPHA on colour and on alpha (FUN_140099f60, 109239-109351; the factors come from denormal constants, so the alpha factor is inferred), and draws the chain's last pass forced translucent whatever the colour blend mode (FUN_140258580, called from FUN_1401ebf60), so black text of alpha a through an opacity effect lands at a cubed (a skew chain of workshop 3465215190 measures at a squared, which this model does not reproduce, and a model with a single glyph alpha plus an opacity effect fed the layer alpha would; which a chain that leaves alpha alone follows is open, and one capture of no-op transform and skew chains at three alphas settles it): probetext4's opacity effect measures 0.275 and 0.125 for alpha 0.65 and 0.5 in Wallpaper Engine's own frames, the clock and the blurprecise heading of workshop 3819684521 agree, and the earlier single alpha was off by 2.5 to 4 times the ink. Here the text card's shader (WPSceneParser.cpp BuildTextSceneShader, composite variant) does the seed and the glyph blend in one pass, because the card covers the whole composite: it samples the scene (_rt_default as g_Texture1) at the fragment's screen position, through the engine's g_EffectModelViewProjectionMatrix with the Direct3D screen flip under HLSL, and writes mix(scene, glyph, alpha) with alpha raised to kTextCompositeAlphaExponent (2, declared in WPSceneParser.hpp with TextCompositeReach, so every test derives its expectation from it); no new blend mode, no second node, no extra pass. The material constant g_Composite (a DynamicValue the runtime owns) is 1 while some effect of the layer is visible and 0 otherwise, so a layer whose scripted effects are all off draws its glyphs straight onto the scene as Wallpaper Engine draws a layer with no effect pass: the passthrough that ends that chain (the shipped effectpassthrough material, the genericimage3 shader, which draws the card times g_Color4) is given a white g_Color4 because the card carries the layer's colour and alpha, and an unbound g_Color4 is zero, which drew nothing, and an "add" layer is drawn additively then (SceneImageEffectLayer::SetIdleFinalBlend, the final blend while no effect runs). A layer with a colour blend keeps the single alpha it had, and the last pass is drawn translucent while an effect runs (an "add" layer with an effect included, which Wallpaper Engine forces). Wallpaper Engine's padding gate counts the visible effect passes (FUN_140258900, 412672-412684; the count FUN_1401e7170, 362347-362352) and works the card out again when an effect's visibility changes (FUN_1401e6300, 346971). TextLayerState gains authored_padding and padding_applies and TextLayer::SetPaddingApplies relays the card out; the parser starts a scripted effect at the value its script starts from (InitialBoolSetting in Runtime/SceneSettingResolver) and registers a SceneRuntimeContext::TextEffectGate (RegisterTextEffectGate, RefreshTextEffectGate, kept in the node registration snapshot) for the layer's built effects, which the effect-visibility listener refreshes, replacing the load-time rule that kept a scripted effect's padding whatever its value. AttachEffectsToNode returns the effects it built and skips one with no pass, which counts for neither the padding, the composite nor the passthrough fallback (EffectCountsForText is the one predicate for the load-time padding and the composite's start). Tests: metal_scene_draw_smoke AnEffectsTextIsComposedOverTheSceneBehindItAsWallpaperEngineDoesOnBothRenderers and its turned, HDR, all-off, scripted (passthrough stand-in multiplies by g_Color4 as genericimage3 does), add, shipped-effects and same-picture companions, text_object_runtime_test ACardKeepsItsPaddingOnlyWhileAnEffectPassIsVisible and AnEffectWithNoPassCountsForNeitherTheMarginNorTheComposite; TextStylingChangesPixelsWithoutRerasterizingGlyphs and the add colour blend test were migrated from the single alpha.
sceneEngine.textEffectBufferChanges: 2026-10-15: The buffers an effect chain on a text layer draws into are the layer's card, not a capacity, for interoperability; no code copied. Wallpaper Engine builds a text object's composite targets as (int)width by (int)height of the card, at least 4, with no 2x or 4x capacity and no 4096 clamp in the path (FUN_1401ea500, called through the object's vtable +0xb8 by the size function FUN_140258900 after every layout; the size it passes comes from FUN_140258ab0 at vtable +0x128, read from the disassembly at 0x140258ab0), and draws the chain's last pass as a quad over the whole card with texture coordinates 0 to 1 (FUN_140258900 calls FUN_1401ea310 with w, h, w, h and scale 1), so v_TexCoord runs 0 to 1 across the card and g_Texture0Resolution is the card's size; read from the 2.8.42 binary. Before, ResolveTextEffectCapacity made the buffers max(card, 4 x the authored size) or, with no authored size, max(card, 2 x the canvas), at most 4096 a side, and the final card sampled the sub-rectangle of them the card covers (TextLayerRenderFrameForCapacity, TextLayerRenderFrameClampedToTarget, TextLayerTextureBoundsForRenderTarget, the three-argument GenTextCardMesh and ResizeCardMesh), so an effect's UV parameter was a fraction of a buffer 3.4x to 16x larger than the card: a shadow offset of 0.01 moved the shadow about 15 pixels where Wallpaper Engine moves it about 4, and a skew centre shift of 0.025 moved a clock 102 units where Wallpaper Engine moves it 26. Now TextLayerEffectFrame gives the buffers' frame (TextCardTexelExtent of the card, at most kTextEffectExtentLimit = 4096 a side, centred on the card), ParseTextObj registers the chain and the final card on it (texture coordinates exactly 0 to 1), and ApplyPreparedTextLayer, when a relayout changes the card, moves the chain's camera and final cards onto the new frame and, only when the card's size in texels changed, sets every buffer sized from the first one to it and flags the render graph for one rebuild; a card that only moved or changed by less than a texel flags nothing, and the flag is raised by a text change, never by a frame. Memory and bandwidth go down by the same factor (a capacity buffer was a median 25 MB against about 1.6 MB for the card, twice over for the ping-pong pair, plus its fbos). Not done: an effect's fbo `scale` is still ignored for text (the buffer is the card's size; an fbo that names its own `width`, `height` or `fit` keeps the fixed size FixedEffectFboExtent gives it and is not resized with the card), and a card past 4096 texels is still drawn cut off to the largest buffer, the one clamp kept from the capacity code. Cost of the rebuild, measured on the committed build with six forced rebuilds (clearLastRenderGraph, sceneToRenderGraph, compileRenderGraph) of a real clock scene (72 render passes per frame, 1920 by 1080, native Metal): 0.5 to 0.8 ms to lower the graph and 39 to 45 ms to compile it, about three frames at 60 Hz, where a one-layer scene takes 0.6 to 0.9 ms; a rebuild also drops every uploaded image and reopens every video of the scene, so a text with a visible effect whose card changes in texels on every update (proportional digits, a typewriter script) hitches a heavy scene once per change. Left open, as the spec has it: retargeting only the text layer's own buffers without a whole-graph rebuild, or drawing the card into a viewport of a larger buffer. Visible: an effect's offset, skew, scroll and shadow parameters on text move by the fraction of the card they name (a probe of an offset of 0.25 moves the text a quarter of its card, 162 canvas units for a 646-unit card, at any authored size), and a left-aligned padded clock through the skew effect stands where Wallpaper Engine's stands (3456 pixels wide: left edge 2964 against 2965, 22 pixels right before); probetext1, 4 and 5 differ by at most 1 of 255 per channel.
sceneEngine.textPlacementChanges: 2026-10-15: A text layer's alignment hangs its card from the layer's origin instead of moving the layer, padding grows the card outward, the rows of a block are set within the widest row, the cursor tests the card where it hangs, and a text layer's screen anchor shifts how it is drawn and not its node, for interoperability; no code copied. Wallpaper Engine's text object stores two offsets with its layout (FUN_140256f20, wallpaper64.c 413226-413284): +0x2f8 is +w/2, 0 or -w/2 for `left`, `center` and `right` (w = maxX - minX of the layout) and +0x2fc is (minY + maxY)/2 - X, X being the reference line the vertical alignment byte (+0x59e) selects: for bottom the descender (stored negative) less (rows - 1) pitches, for center (ascender - (rows - 1) pitch) * 0.5, for top the ascender; neither holds the padding. Its GetMatrix (FUN_140256e10, vtable +0x80, 411877-411921) adds the offset, in local space, to a copy of the node's world matrix (FUN_1401850a0 composes the parent chain and never calls it), so a child is composed from the unshifted base. The block is centred in the card (FUN_140258050 and FUN_140257d70, 412125-412449: translate pad - min(0, minX) and pad - minY into a (w + 2 padX) by (h + 2 padY) target), so padding grows the card outward from the aligned edge. A row's pen starts at 0 and its quads are offset by (W - w_i)/2 or W - w_i, W the widest row's width (the vertex build in FUN_1401b0410, 374924-375001), with no term for the bearing of the row's first glyph. The screen anchor shift is FUN_1402585c0 (vtable +0xa8, 412451-412650), applied in FUN_1401e8aa0 (353990-354095) to a copy of the model-matrix stack top, after which the layer's matrix is multiplied in and the copy popped: a translation outside every layer and ancestor transform, so in world space and not inherited by a child (the convention is from the decompile alone, and that its margins are those of the visible area is inferred). Read from the 2.8.42 binary. Before, ParseTextObj called SetNodeAnchorAlignment with the words of the alignment, which moved the node by half the card times the layer's scale along each named edge (turned with the layer), so the node was off the authored origin and a layer parented to the text sat half a card from it; the first baseline was found by BlockTopY inside the card, which centred the whole pitch box on the origin for `center` and put its bottom edge on it for `bottom`, so the text stood (pitch - ascender)/2 and the line gap above where Wallpaper Engine puts it (39.7 and 29.9 canvas units in the probe); the padding was an inset inside a card that stayed flush on the origin, so an effect that turned the padding on moved an aligned text; every row was placed by HorizontalLineStart in the card's width minus its own extent and then moved back by its own left extent, so a row that opened with a glyph overhanging to the left took the overhang of another row; the cursor tested a box centred on the node; the screen anchor was added to the node's translate, so children inherited it; and a script's `alignment` write replaced the layer's alignment words and shifted it by half its size. Now TextLayerLayout carries `centre` (LayoutOfBlock computes it from the block with ReferenceLine and CardCentre in TextLayer.cpp: the padding is in no term of it), RowOffset places a row by the widest row's width and the raster starts a row's pen at the padding less the block's left edge (RasterizeFreeTypeText and RasterizeFallbackText; HorizontalLineStart, BlockTopY and the node-shift anchor string TextAlignmentAnchor are gone), TextLayerRenderBoundsForRasterSize, TextLayerRenderFrameForRasterSize and the raster-sized TextLayerRenderFrameForCapacity became TextLayerRenderBoundsForLayout, TextLayerRenderFrameForLayout and TextLayerRenderFrameForCapacity (the card centred on `centre`, plus the style's margin; the effect chain's frames follow it), and ParseTextObj leaves the node at the authored origin and no longer calls SetNodeAnchorAlignment or LoadAlignment for text. SceneRuntimeContext::ApplyPreparedTextLayer also resizes the card mesh when only the centre changed (a script's horizontalalign or verticalalign write, which now changes where the card hangs and not its size), SetNodeTextStyle no longer re-derives a node shift, SceneRuntimeContext::NodeBoxCentre (the text layer's layout centre) gives HitTestNode the centre of the box it tests and of the coverage mask's texture coordinates, and SetNodeAlignment turns a text layer down (a text object has no `alignment`). SceneNode gains SetDrawOffset and DrawOffset: RenderTrans() adds the offset to the node's world translation when the node is not drawn through an override (ModelTrans, so children, cameras and parallax of the world matrix, is untouched); ApplyNodeTransform stores a screen anchor's offset there and not in the translate, SyncEffectFinalNode gives the final card of an effect chain the source's world matrix with the offset in its override (the source node itself keeps the identity override it draws into the chain's buffer with), HitTestNode and IntersectNdcWithNodePlane test the plane where the node is drawn, and MetalRender's pass-change hash also takes RenderTrans() for a node with an override or an offset (128 bytes on those passes), a precaution so that an offset which changes alone cannot be taken for an unchanged pass: no scene was found in which the pass skip would miss it without, so no test needs it. WPShaderValueUpdater builds the effect model matrix, the effect model-view-projection matrices and the effect texture projection from the owner's world matrix plus its draw offset, so a pointer or world-position effect on a screen-anchored text finds the card where it is drawn (g_LayerModelMatrix stays the layer's own world matrix); ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.EffectModelMatrixAndInverseProjectionMatchTheEffectProjection and .EffectTextureProjectionMapsTheLayerCardOntoTheScreen cover an offset. NodeTranslate needs no change: the node translate is the authored origin for every text layer, with or without a screen offset. Visible, probes rendered from the 8 s and 15 s frames (identical): in probetext1 (DIN Engschrift 48 points, nine alignments) every glyph box agrees with Wallpaper Engine's own frame to 0.5 canvas unit (the H of the top row 651.0 to 793.0 in both; the centre and bottom rows merge into one box 320.1 to 602.5 in both, where before they were 642.7 and 492.0 at the top, 40 and 30 units high; the g's 609.2 to 753.2 and 278.3 to 562.7 in both; the right-aligned g ends at 1599.1 in both); in probetext2 (three-row blocks in two fonts, top, centre and bottom) all 18 H and g boxes of the three columns agree to 0.5 unit in y (e.g. 828.1 to 972.1, 588.0 to 727.9, 348.0 to 487.9 in both; before, 860.1 to 1007.2, 627.2 to 767.2 and 387.2 to 527.1); probetext3 (a parented right-aligned date with children, copied from a real clock) has its date at y 1938.0 to 2047.5 and x 3105.3 to 3349.0 against Wallpaper Engine's 3106.3 to 3350.0, and the child 'THU' at 3385.1 to 3462.6 against 3386.2 to 3462.6, where before the red child text sat 120 canvas units left of the parent's copy and 30 low; probetext5 puts its text 40 units lower than before, at 460.5 to 602.5 as Wallpaper Engine does, for plain and for effect text alike (an effect, which turns the padding on, no longer moves it; the plain text's sideways position in probetext5 follows camera parallax like any layer's, see textParallaxChanges), and probetext4's text lies at 750.1 to 893.1 against Wallpaper Engine's 750.6 to 892.6. In the real scene 2981249186 (right-aligned, padding 32 with an effect, scale 1.14) the last three glyphs of the right-aligned weekday start at 3191, 3277 and 3360 px in Wallpaper Engine's frame and in ours alike (the two frames show different weekdays), where the stored frame of the older build was 37 px off on every glyph. sceneEngine.textLayoutRecordChanges: 2026-10-15: A text layer's card is the laid-out text and nothing else, from one layout record, for interoperability; no code copied. Wallpaper Engine's text size function (FUN_140258900, wallpaper64.c 412651-412728, called by the layout step FUN_140256f20 after the layout FUN_1401b0410 builds) writes the card as (maxX - minX) + 2 padX by (maxY - minY) + 2 padY, and 2.0 plus twice the padding when there is no layout; its guard byte (+0x328) is set only while the effects are being parsed and cleared after (347990-348060), so the authored size never keeps the card. The layout record holds +0x90 minX, +0x94 minY, +0x98 maxX, +0x9c maxY, +0xa0 pitch and +0xa4 rows (375090-375100); the ascender and descender are the face's size metrics cut by >> 6 and the pitch is (height >> 6) plus spacing y; 15 of 15 single-line asset-font layers in the local scenes have a saved size.y equal to that pitch, plus twice the padding only where Wallpaper Engine pads. The buffers of a text's composite are built as (int)width by (int)height, at least 4 (FUN_1401ea500, FUN_140258ab0, the latter read from the disassembly). Read from the 2.8.42 binary. Before, TextLayerRasterSizeForMeasured made the card max(authored size, measured card) plus the style margin, TextLayerRenderBoundsForRasterSize and the node size used the authored box as the layout the layer is aligned in and the cursor tested (so a scripted text that got shorter kept its stale card), a layer was measured four times as it was parsed (TextLayerLayoutSize, TextLayerRasterSize, RegisterTextTexture and the TextLayer constructor), and ResolveTextRenderExtent rounded the card to the nearest texel. Now TextLayerState::explicit_size, layout_size and raster_size are gone, and TextLayerLayout (min_x, max_x, top, bottom, ascender, descender, pitch, rows, padding, card) is what MeasureTextLayerLayout returns (the FreeType face's metrics, or the 0.9 em, 0.3 em and 1.2 em boxes where no font opens; zero rows and a 2 by 2 card plus the padding for no text) and TextLayer holds; the node size is its card, the raster is the card plus the style margin, and the render bounds are the raster centred on the layer. ParseTextObj measures once and passes the layout to RegisterTextTexture's size and to RegisterTextLayer, PrepareTextLayerImage measures once per change of the text on the worker, RuntimePreparedTextLayerImage carries the layout, SceneRuntimeContext::NodeTextLayout reads it, and ResolveTextRenderExtent cuts the fraction (at least 4) and no longer falls back to the canvas. That rule is now one function, TextCardTexelExtent (Text/TextLayer), which ParseTextObj's effect buffers, RegisterTextComposite and SceneRuntimeContext::FitTextLayerComposite all take their size from: FitTextLayerComposite still rounded (std::lround) the composite's target on every relayout, so a referenced text layer was built at the cut size as the scene loaded and at the rounded one after its first change (a card of 628.56 got 629 texels, not 628). ApplyPreparedTextLayer asks the buffers of a text's effect chain for the card's size in texels, not its float size, before it doubles them and rebuilds the graph: a fractional card that grows by less than the texel the cut buffers already have is drawn into them as before (the part of a texel past them is cut off there, as in Wallpaper Engine) and no longer costs a rebuild at twice the size. ResolveTextEffectCapacity still reads the authored size for an effect chain's capacity; the alignment shift of the node, by the card, is unchanged. Visible: probetext1, 2, 4 and 5 at 8 s and 15 s, before and after, keep every vertical position to the pixel, and so the left- and right-aligned texts of probetext1, the effect text of probetext5 and the whole of probetext4, while text centred in a box wider than it moves 0.5 canvas unit to the left (the H block of probetext1 from 892.4 to 891.9, of probetext2 from 222.8 to 222.3, of probetext5 from 340.5 to 340.0), because its ink is no longer rounded to a texel inside a 400-unit card; probetext3, a date group whose text is smaller than the boxes it was authored in, keeps the parent's right-aligned copy where it was and moves its children, which still inherit the node shift, about 34 canvas units to the right (the red child text's left edge goes from 2726 to 2759 px, 33 px at the probe's 0.9685 scale: (317 - the card's width) / 2 for the 317-unit box the parent was authored in and a card about 247 wide), toward where Wallpaper Engine draws them (the placement change that stops children inheriting the shift is a separate step). A text that changes now has the card of its current text: a clock authored with a size (342 by 156) that shows a shorter time has the smaller card.
