Tests: wallpaper_scaling_test (CPU only, new, in the check) pins the default against an in-test copy of the old arithmetic across every mode, the edges for overflow and bars, the top row, clamping and the cursor mapping; playback_gpu_test extends the plain-video byte-for-byte comparison (direct present, copy path and poster) to panned rows and checks the picture's footprint; metal_scene_draw_smoke checks the picture's rows in a poster for the top, middle and bottom pan, in the presenting frame and from a retained output, and the present gate; unchanged_present_test checks a position change presents once through setFraming and then repeats. Verified on offscreen targets only; how a panned wallpaper looks on a physical display was not checked.
sceneEngine.settledHiddenLayerChanges: 2026-10-13: sceneToRenderGraph leaves out every layer hidden by a visibility only a reload changes (authored, or bound to a user property without a script), on the layer or an ancestor, unless it or a descendant must produce a composite another layer samples. The parser marks that visibility on the node (SceneNode::VisibilitySettled); the graph records each left-out subtree in Scene::render_excluded_nodes. SceneRuntimeContext::SetNodeVisible, the SceneScript `visible` setter, clears the mark for good, and when it or a property applied in place makes a left-out layer visible, RequestGraphForShownLayers sets the scene-graph mutation flag so the frame rebuilds the graph before it draws. When a left-out layer came before every scene-output writer and the scene does not clear, the first remaining writer keeps loading the output, as it did while the hidden writer ahead of it drew nothing. Previously every hidden variant of a customizable wallpaper kept its passes: both backends allocated their effect ping-pong and FBO targets, loaded their textures, and native Metal opened a render pass every frame for each hidden first-use clear and blitted framebuffer copies for hidden blend layers. Workshop 2531810451 under its defaults: native Metal render targets 11.42 GB -> 0.39 GB, 241 -> 19 render passes and 11 -> 1 blits per frame; Vulkan allocations 8.26 GB -> 0.54 GB; output byte-identical on both. Across 60 local scene wallpapers 29 use less memory and none more (native Metal render targets 24.3 GB -> 7.9 GB in total, Vulkan allocations 45.7 GB -> 27.3 GB), with the same backend choices; every frame matches the unchanged renderer except where two unchanged runs also differ (video decode timing, clocks). Fewer passes and no per-frame work are added; a script showing a left-out layer costs one graph rebuild per layer. No wallpaper-specific rules; the layer-texture graph and native Metal regressions fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.composeChildCompositeChanges: 2026-10-13: A layer another layer samples is drawn into its own composite even when it sits inside a compose layer. ToGraphPass isolates a referenced layer by where it would draw before the nearest compose layer claims the draw (the scene output), so such a child is drawn into _rt_imageLayerComposite_<id> through its layer-local camera (LayerCompositeCameraKey) as well as into the compose layer's target, and a referenced child with effects links that composite rather than the whole compose target. Drawn only into the compose target, the child had no composite: a compose layer's effect sampling its own child (a blend that reads a script-tinted solid card as a palette) logged `link tex <id> not found`, the compatibility backend skipped that effect pass and native Metal failed to prepare the scene and fell back. The second draw of a referenced layer (on screen, or into the compose target) is now left out only when the layer is hidden by a visibility only a reload changes (HiddenUntilReload, the rule the graph already leaves layers out by), instead of whenever it was hidden at graph build: a layer a script hides is drawn again when the script shows it, since nothing rebuilds the graph then, and both backends skip it per frame while it is hidden. Cost: one pass per sampled compose child, drawing its card into the composite target the parser already declares; no per-frame CPU work. Regressions: LayerTextureReference.AComposeLayersEffectCanSampleItsOwnChild (graph, three visibilities) and MetalSceneDraw.AComposeLayersEffectSamplesItsOwnChild (native pixels) fail with the change removed; LayerTextureReference.ExternalMaterialsKeepHiddenTransitiveProducers now parses with a runtime, as the wallpaper does.
sceneEngine.textLayerCompositeChanges: 2026-10-13: A text layer another layer samples (`_rt_imageLayerComposite_<id>_a` or a dependency) gets a composite of its own, as an image layer does. ParseTextObj calls RegisterTextComposite, and so does the deferred-source loop in WPSceneParser::Parse, from the card ParseContext::text_cards keeps, for a reference found only while a later consumer's material is parsed: the node must produce, the target is the card's size in texels, and the layer-local camera (LayerCompositeCameraKey), on a node of its own at the card's centre, frames the card exactly. The card is the text's render frame, or with effects the chain's final card, never the effect capacity the chain renders at; a card aligned to one side of a box the text overflows sits off the layer's origin. RegisterImageComposite and RegisterTextComposite share RegisterLayerComposite (image composites unchanged), and WPTextObject reads `clampuvs` for the composite's addressing. After a relayout SceneRuntimeContext::ApplyPreparedTextLayer calls FitTextLayerComposite: the camera follows the new card, and the target is resized to it, raising the scene-graph mutation flag, only when its size in texels changed. One texel per unit is kept because a consumer may place the image by its size (texture_override's "Original size" divides by g_Texture1Resolution). TextLayerIsBeingPrepared counts a node that must produce, so a hidden sampled text is laid out when its text changes. Previously a sampled text layer was drawn through the scene camera into the screen-sized fallback IsolateReferencedLayerOutput declares, so the consumer found the text wherever it sat on screen, and, hidden, both backends skipped its composite pass every frame and the consumer sampled an empty texture (local 3624257712: layer 680 scrolls hidden text layer 416, the now-playing title). Cost: a card-sized target and link per sampled text layer instead of screen-sized ones (3624257712 in offscreen_scene_probe: VMA allocated 777.6 MB -> 646.3 MB, footprint 2121.7 MB -> 2010.2 MB) and one graph rebuild when a relayout changes the card's size in texels; no per-frame work. No wallpaper-specific rules; LayerTextureReference.ASampledTextLayerIsItsCardInItsOwnComposite and MetalSceneDraw.AHiddenTextLayerAnotherSamplesIsItsCardInItsComposite fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.depthStateChanges: 2026-10-13: Both renderers take a draw's depth state from one rule, ResolveSceneDepthState in Scene/SceneMaterial.h: a pass depth-tests only when its target has a depth attachment (SceneRenderTarget::withDepth) and its material depth-tests, and writes depth only when it depth-tests and the material asks to, whatever its blending. Wallpaper Engine's own depth-tested font materials (materials/fonts/*_depth.json) are translucent with depthwrite enabled, and Compatibility already wrote depth for them. ScenePassDescription used to drop depth writes for translucent and additive materials (added untested with the Leon scene fixes, whose materials write no depth) and depth-tested passes into targets with no depth attachment, where CustomShaderPass draws in painter's order; it now sets depth_test/depth_write from the shared rule, and CustomShaderPass sets depthTestEnable/depthWriteEnable from it. Tests: metal_scene_draw_smoke gains DrawWithRenderer (one parse drawn through SceneRendererHandle on a layer no window owns, with the host's scaling, per-frame FrameBegin and graph rebuilds, the compiled graph released before its graph is replaced as SceneWallpaper does, and the last frame returned through the poster path) and ADepthWritingDrawHidesLaterDrawsAsOnCompatibility, which draws seven authored blend/depth cases through both renderers and requires identical pictures; before the change the translucent, additive and no-attachment opaque cases differed.
sceneEngine.ownEffectBufferAChanges: 2026-10-13: Inside a layer's own effect chain, `_rt_imageLayerComposite_<id>_a` (or the bare name) bound by one of that layer's effects is the chain's ping-pong buffer A, the image `previous` names at that point (for the first effect, the layer before any effect), not the layer's final composite. IsOwnEffectChainInput (SceneLayerReference) names the case; BindOwnEffectChainInput rewrites such a texture to the chain's input placeholder in ParseImageObj and AttachEffectsToNode (now given the layer id), so SceneImageEffectLayer::ResolveEffect assigns it the current ping-pong buffer exactly as it does `previous`; an effect `bind` to `previous` on the same slot still wins. HarvestTextures skips the same names under the layer's own `effects`, so they no longer make the layer a sampled one (no composite, MustProduce or link copy); other layers binding the name still get the final composite, and a self `_b` is still classified as last-frame history. Previously the effect read `_rt_link_<id>`, a copy of the composite the chain writes after it: the compatibility renderer logged `has no image` and the layer drew nothing every frame (local 3624257712: text layer 420's outline effect hid the clock; local 3255418892: a full-composition layer's scan-line effect left the whole wallpaper black), and native Metal refused the scene as history feedback (3624257712 now runs natively). Of the 5 local scenes with such a binding, the other frames match the unchanged renderer within run-to-run noise on both backends, with the same backend choices; built-in blur, shine and godrays carry these names in the slot their effect binds to `previous` and draw as before. Cost: none added; a self-sampling layer loses its composite pass and link copy (offscreen_scene_probe peak footprint 3255418892 855.9 -> 830.1 MB, 2234665570 1182.9 -> 1166.2 MB, 3624257712 unchanged). No wallpaper-specific rules; LayerTextureReference.ALayersOwnEffectReadsItsBufferANotItsComposite and MetalSceneDraw.ALayersOwnEffectReadsItsBufferANotItsComposite fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.ownEffectBufferBChanges: 2026-10-13: Inside a layer's own effect chain, `_rt_imageLayerComposite_<id>_b` bound by one of that layer's effects is the image the effect works on, as `_a` is since ownEffectBufferAChanges: IsOwnEffectChainInput (SceneLayerReference) accepts either suffix, so BindOwnEffectChainInput gives the slot the chain's current ping-pong buffer, the one `previous` names, and HarvestTextures no longer records it as a reference. Both names are the chain's ping-pong buffers. All 13 self `_a`/`_b` names in the 11 local layers that carry one sit in the slot `previous` fills (bound by the effect, or slot 0), and 10 name the buffer `previous` was in when the effect was added (effect ids give that order; one blur was moved up later): the layer is drawn into `_a` and each effect pass without a target of its own, hidden effects included, moves to the other buffer, as in linux-wallpaperengine's CImage ping-pong. The other 3 (a layer saved without effect ids, and a compose layer whose first effect names `_b`) are in slots their effect binds to `previous`, which wins either way. Wallpaper Engine keeps last-frame images in an effect's own `unique` buffers filled by a `copy` command (motionblur), not in these. A self `_b` was classified as last-frame history, so native Metal refused the whole scene (local 2234665570, 1406906866, 2294547604, 2440387496, 3627973226 and 3712014415, all now native), and a workshop sine wave naming `_b` in its first slot, after one audio-bar effect, sampled `_rt_link_<id>` with `has no image` every frame on the compatibility renderer, so its compose layer drew nothing (3627973226, 3712014415: the bottom band now shows; the other four are byte-identical, since blur, shine and godrays bind `previous` over the name). A self `_b` outside the layer's effects is still history. Cost: none added; a layer sampled only through its own `_b` loses its composite pass and link copy, and a hidden one leaves the graph (2440387496: 34 -> 27 Vulkan passes, offscreen_scene_probe peak footprint 746.6 -> 733.0 MB). No wallpaper-specific rules; LayerTextureReference.ALayersOwnEffectReadsItsBufferBAsTheImageItWorksOn, LayerTextureReference.SelfBInItsOwnEffectsIsNotAReference (formerly SelfBIsHistoryFeedback) and MetalSceneDraw.ALayersOwnEffectReadsItsBufferBAsTheImageItWorksOn fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.uncopyableTemplateCreateLayerChanges: 2026-10-13: SceneScript thisScene.createLayer copies the scene layer registered under the requested model, but SceneRuntimeContext::CreateLayerFromTemplate refused a registered layer it cannot copy, one with an effect chain (its own camera) or child layers, and returned nothing even when the model itself was in the package. It now asks the lazy template loader for the binding's model path, which parses the bare model (visible, sized by its picture, no effects) and replaces that registration, so later calls copy the loaded layer directly and the model is parsed once; a model that cannot be loaded, or loads into a shape that still cannot be copied, logs `createLayer unsupported template shape` and fails as before, and is not loaded again. The script's own layer is often the only scene layer using the model and often has an effect, so its init threw `Unable to create layer` before setting up state its update reads, and update threw every frame (local 2234665570: two audio-bar layers with a pulse effect each creating 63 bars from models/workshop/<item>/bar.json, now 126 created layers and no script errors on both probes; local 3786225131: models/util/solidlayer.json, now 74 created layers, its next error is the unimplemented thisScene.destroyLayer). The other five local scenes that call createLayer render and log as before (frames within base-vs-base noise). Cost: one hidden template per such model, parsed on the first call; no extra passes or per-frame work beyond the layers the script asked for. No wallpaper-specific rules; ScriptRuntimeCompat.CreateLayerBuildsTheModelsOwnLayerWhenTheLayerUsingItCannotBeCopied and .CreateLayerDoesNotReloadAModelThatLoadsIntoALayerItCannotCopy fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.ownEffectSelfDependencyChanges: 2026-10-13: An object's `dependencies` entry naming the object itself is no longer recorded as a layer reference: HarvestTextures (SceneLayerReference) skips a dependency id equal to the consumer, as it already skips the `_a`/`_b` self names in the layer's own `effects` (ownEffectBufferAChanges, ownEffectBufferBChanges). The editor lists the layers an object's textures name, and older versions list the layer itself too, once for each self name its effects bind (local 1406906866, layer 309: `[309, 309]` for two shine effects naming `_rt_imageLayerComposite_309_b` / `_a`, the only self-dependency among the 60 local scenes; every local `dependencies` entry is matched by a `_rt_imageLayerComposite_` name in the same object). A dependency carries no slot, so it cannot ask for the last frame, and a layer waits on nothing of its own; a self-sample from outside its effects is a texture name, still harvested with its slot (a self `_b` there is still history). Recorded, the self entry put the layer in referenced_layer_ids and Scene::layer_texture_sources, so it was given a composite pass (`_rt_imageLayerComposite_<id>`) nobody sampled, and a hidden such layer was kept in the graph, through CollectReachableLayerIds for a property-bound visibility and the deferred-source loop in WPSceneParser::Parse for an authored one. 1406906866 in offscreen_scene_probe and metal_scene_draw_smoke on 35ee28a9, two runs per arm: frames byte-identical on both backends; the pass dropped is the layer's last shine_combine drawn a second time at 2880x1800, Vulkan 43 -> 42 passes per frame, native Metal 15 -> 14 render passes per frame. Memory is unchanged within run-to-run noise, since the composite already shared memory with the chain's buffers (Vulkan pooling; metalTargetSharingChanges on native Metal, before which it cost 21.6 MB of render targets): VMA allocated and Metal render target bytes identical, peak footprint Vulkan 503-505 MB and Metal 474-478 MB in both arms. Cost: none added. No wallpaper-specific rules; LayerTextureReference.ALayersOwnEffectReadsItsBufferANotItsComposite, LayerTextureReference.ALayersOwnEffectReadsItsBufferBAsTheImageItWorksOn and HiddenLayers.ALayerItsPropertiesHideStaysOutOfTheGraphUntilSomethingShowsIt fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.userBoundImageColorChanges: 2026-10-13: An image layer's colour bound to a user property ({"user": ..., "value": ...}) takes the property's value instead of the scene file's default. ParseImageObj resolves it with ResolveVec3Setting before g_Color/g_Color4 are built, and SceneRuntimeContext::BindMaterialColor writes later property changes to the layer's own material, every effect pass and a compose layer's passthrough from one listener, keeping each g_Color4 alpha (ApplyMaterialColor, which SetNodeColor now shares). Only the colour was never bound, so a Workshop preset's colours, or the user's own, drew in the base wallpaper's default colours (issue #43). Scripted colours were left unchanged then, on the grounds that a binding would overwrite thisLayer.color writes; superseded by scriptedImageColorChanges (2026-10-15), which binds them and makes SetNodeColor update the bound value from scripts that return nothing. A solid instance layer whose placeholder a runtime image replaces drops a bound colour as it drops an authored one. No pass, per-frame work or allocation is added: the listener runs only when the property changes, and a static colour costs nothing. No wallpaper-specific rules; the scene schema regressions fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.scriptEngineQueryChanges: 2026-10-13: SceneScript's engine object has the three host queries Wallpaper Engine documents on IEngine and the runtime lacked: isDesktopDevice() returns true, isMobileDevice() false and isWallpaper() the negation of isScreensaver(), so it is true while isScreensaver() is the stub returning false and stays consistent if that ever reports a screensaver. AppendCommonHostBootstrap defines them beside isScreensaver and keeps an existing definition; the bootstrap is evaluated once per shared script context, so nothing runs per frame. A script that called any of them threw "not a function", which aborted that script's init or update. No wallpaper-specific rules; the script runtime regression fails with the change removed.
sceneEngine.destroyLayerChanges: 2026-10-13: SceneScript's scene object has IScene.destroyLayer, which Wallpaper Engine documents as removing a layer by reference, name or index, deferred, and answering a Boolean. SceneRuntimeContext::DestroyLayer removes a layer CreateLayerFromTemplate made (it now records their names): UnregisterNode drops it from every registry at once, so the layer object a script still holds reaches nothing (getters answer as for an unknown layer, setters do nothing) and a second call answers false. The node leaves its parent and the scene graph is marked mutated, but it stays in m_retired_layers until a Tick finds that mutation consumed, because the render graph compiled before holds raw pointers to it; ReleaseRetiredLayers then drops its copies of the template's material-constant bindings and its WPShaderValueUpdater entries (new IShaderValueUpdater::ForgetNode, a no-op by default) and frees it. The bootstrap's scene.destroyLayer resolves a layer object or a name, calls the native __layerDestroy and clears the script-side layer cache and order entries. A layer from the scene file, or one named by index (getLayer resolves no index either), stays and the call answers false. The call was missing, so a script that rebuilds the layers it made when a setting changes threw `not a function` from applyUserProperties before building the new set (local 3786225131, whose snap-to-grid script recreates 74 hidden grid lines: with uncopyableTemplateCreateLayerChanges in place it now ends with 74 created layers built by the second pass and no applyUserProperties error on both probes; its frames are pixel-identical on offscreen_scene_probe and within run-to-run noise on native Metal, since the grid shows only while dragging). The six other local scenes that call createLayer keep identical node graphs, script errors and frames. Cost: none per frame; ReleaseRetiredLayers returns at once when nothing is retired, and the graph is rebuilt once for the frame that destroyed layers, as it is for createLayer. No wallpaper-specific rules; ScriptRuntimeCompat.DestroyLayerRemovesALayerTheScriptCreated and ScriptRuntimeCompat.ADestroyedLayerIsFreedOnlyOnceTheGraphNoLongerDrawsIt fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.userEffectVisibilityChanges: 2026-10-13: An image or text layer's effect whose visible is bound to a user property ({"user": name} or a combo condition) is built from the property's current value, resolved by ResolveBoolSetting exactly as layer visibility is; WPImageEffect keeps the binding in visible_setting and ResolveUserEffectVisibility applies it at the start of ParseImageObj and ParseTextObj. Only the scene file's value, the editor's default, was read, so object colour modes, gradients and effect toggles in customizable wallpapers (Workshop 2531810451, seen while checking issue #44) never changed anything. A property the project does not declare keeps the authored value; scripted effect visibility and blacklisted effects are unchanged. Property changes reload the scene, so the decision is parse-time only: no extra passes, per-frame work or wallpaper-specific rules, and the 792 bound effects across 59 local scene wallpapers resolve to their authored value under saved defaults. The rendergraph (image) and text-object regressions fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.scriptTimeOfDayChanges: 2026-10-13: SceneScript has engine.timeOfDay, the local wall-clock time as a fraction of the day (00:00 is 0, noon 0.5), as Wallpaper Engine documents it. Utils/TimeOfDay.hpp computes it for both engine.timeOfDay and the g_Daytime/g_DayTime uniforms, so scripts and shaders agree; WPShaderValueUpdater::FrameBegin moved to it unchanged. The property is a native getter on the shared engine object, so the clock is read only when a script asks and other wallpapers pay nothing per frame. It was undefined, so a property script that blended day, dawn and sunset images by the hour (Workshop 2979524338, issue #46) returned NaN, and the blend effect drew the whole layer black under the clock. No extra passes or wallpaper-specific rules; the script runtime regression fails with the change removed.
sceneEngine.surfaceHealthChanges: 2026-10-13: A scene surface publishes its own health without anything being enabled. Core/SurfaceHealth.hpp (header-only) holds a few relaxed atomics: frames completed, frames presented, frames lost to a failed draw (never reset), the steady-clock time of the last present, and a stop latch that is FrameFailed (the draw itself failed) or GraphFailed (the render graph or its backend could not be built or released). SceneWallpaper's render handler counts a frame as completed when it returns success, whether or not it presented, because a frame that would repeat the picture completes without presenting; the draw failure branch notes FrameFailed only when the failure came from drawFrame and every graph lifecycle suspend (rebuildRenderGraph, SET_SCENE, creating the backend, a failed surface reconfigure) notes GraphFailed through suspendAfterGraphFailure, while a host-initiated suspend (the start of a surface reconfigure) notes nothing. clearRenderBlock replaces every assignment of m_render_blocked = false and clears the latch with it. owe_scene_wallpaper_surface_health (SceneWallpaperBindings.h/.mm) is a pull-only getter that is unaffected by renderer counting, like owe_scene_wallpaper_update_mode; the Rust sys bindings are regenerated by bindgen. core::SceneRuntimeReport gains surface: Option<SurfaceHealth> read under the SceneRegistry lock, and the bridge reports a stopped surface as the scene mode stopped_after_failure, below the user's pause and a suspended display and above the renderer's own classification. No uniffi record changes: the mode string was already free-form. surface_health_test (CPU only, injected clock) and unchanged_present_test (a still scene keeps completing frames while presenting none) cover it; a real MoltenVK or Metal presentation failure was not produced.
sceneEngine.renderFailureCallbackChanges: 2026-10-13: A scene that had already presented a frame and then fails one calls the host back once. SceneWallpaper gains PROPERTY_RENDER_FAILURE_CALLBACK (std::function<void()>, RenderFailureCallback), MainHandler::CMD_RENDER_FAILED and sendRenderFailure(), mirroring the audio-requirement callback: no payload, no replay on install, posted to the main looper. The render handler's failed-frame routine is now one function, failFrame(reached_draw), which counts the failure, latches FrameFailed or GraphFailed, suspends rendering and then, only for a draw failure (never a graph failure) on a scene whose first frame has been presented, posts the callback; a failure before the first frame keeps the host's first-frame timeout and rollback path. owe_scene_wallpaper_set_render_failure_callback (SceneWallpaperBindings.h/.mm) is registered exactly like owe_scene_wallpaper_set_audio_requirement_callback (registration struct, drop armed only after install, stored on struct owe_scene_wallpaper). Under WESCENE_BUILD_TESTS only, SceneWallpaperInputTestAccess::InjectFrameFailure posts a render command that runs failFrame(true), which is how unchanged_present_test drives the consequence of a presentation failure that cannot be produced without breaking the GPU. unchanged_present_test covers the callback firing once, the stop latching and the clock stopping, a surface reconfigure clearing the stop with the failure count kept, and no callback before the first frame; no real MoltenVK or Metal presentation failure was produced.
sceneEngine.audioSpectrumChanges: 2026-10-11: The audio-response spectrum follows Wallpaper Engine's documented and measured behaviour instead of a home-grown one that saturated. Capture hands the analyzer 48 kHz (the resampler had point-sampled the tap to 12 kHz without a filter, folding everything above 6 kHz into the bands). Each 1,600-frame block (33 ms, 30 a second, back to back) is Hann-windowed and zero-padded to a 2048-point FFT; 64 buckets are one ~23 Hz bin wide up to ~400 Hz and then widen exponentially to ~15 kHz, matching octave-tone measurements of Wallpaper Engine from 42 Hz to 12 kHz; 32 and 16 bands merge the same bins. A band is its energy on a 48 dB scale (1 for a full-scale tone, occasionally above 1 as documented). Removed: per-band peak hold over 8 bins, log compression that read 1.0 for a normally mastered track in every band, spreading each band into its neighbours, and attack/release smoothing, which Wallpaper Engine leaves to wallpapers. API, stereo handling, stale-input clearing and the 0..1 clamp on web delivery are unchanged. Probes take WE_TEST_AUDIO_FILE (raw 48 kHz float PCM). No per-frame cost: one 2048-point FFT per channel 30 times a second replaces a 1024-point one 60 times a second.
sceneEngine.historyTargetChanges: 2026-10-11: A render target the frame reads before anything writes it, and writes later (motion blur's history buffer), carries the previous frame's pixels. RenderGraph::getCarriedOverKeys finds such keys; sceneToRenderGraph flags their SceneRenderTarget (carriesPreviousFrame, not reusable) except the scene output, which the frame's prepass clears; TextureCache::Reserve gives each a fresh image that is never handed back to the pool, done by ReserveCarriedOverTargets before VulkanRender and offscreen_scene_probe prepare any pass. Pooled, the history took an image another target redraws every frame and lent its own to the next target of that size, so trails blended in a faint copy of some other layer that jumped between frames. No pass is added or removed; the cost is those buffers' own memory. CPU graph and GPU reservation regressions fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.historyFeedbackDemandChanges: 2026-10-13: A history loop keeps the frame clock running on the compatibility backend. VulkanRender::Impl::computeShaderDynamicReasons adds DynamicReason::Feedback when a pass of the compiled graph (a CustomShaderPass's target or inputs, a CopyPass's source or destination) touches a render target flagged carriesPreviousFrame, resolved through the scene's render-target aliases; the flag lives on the scene, so a target no pass of this graph touches does not count. ShaderUpdateDemandReasons, and through SceneDemandReasonsFromShaderInputs the scene's SceneDemandReason::Feedback, therefore report a motion-blur trail or an accumulation even when no shader reads the time, so with on-demand updating on such a scene no longer stops its clock mid-fade. Runs whether or not scene optimisation is on, like the rest of the analysis; nothing is drawn differently and nothing is added per frame (the walk runs once per compiled graph). Regression: UnchangedPresent.AHistoryLoopKeepsTheClockRunningWithoutATimeUniform (unchanged_present_test) runs a card beside an echo of _rt_MipMappedFrameBuffer through SceneWallpaper with on-demand updating on: it reports Feedback, no TimeUniform, stays Continuous and keeps drawing with pixel reuse off and on, while the card alone goes idle; with the change removed the loop reports no reason and stops drawing.
sceneEngine.rotatedAlignmentAnchorChanges: 2026-10-11: SceneRuntimeContext::ApplyNodeTransform turns a non-centre layer's anchor offset by the node's rotation (x, then y, then z, the order SceneNode::GetLocalTrans applies), so the named edge stays on the origin and the layer turns about it, as Wallpaper Engine's local-space pivot does; the offset was applied along the scene's axes, so every bar of a scripted ring visualizer (Workshop 2850003448) slid the same way down the screen instead of hanging outward from its circle. The binding records the rotation its cached translate was derived for, and SetNodeRotation, RegisterNodeRotation and the bound-angles pass of Tick re-derive an anchored layer's translate, the last after the translate pass so a bound rotation lands in the same frame. Authored (size * scale) and script-set (scale delta) offset modes are unchanged. Unrotated layers take the same float operations as before, bit for bit. No per-frame work for unanchored layers, extra passes or wallpaper-specific rules; script runtime regressions fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.workshopCreateLayerChanges: 2026-10-10: SceneScript thisScene.createLayer passes on the __workshopId its script declares; when the path as written, the owner layer's workshop folder and the lazy loader all find nothing, the runtime tries <folder>/workshop/<id>/<rest> (numeric ids only), so a path that resolved before still resolves to the same template. The lazy template loader parses the bare model visible, since every created layer starts as a copy of it and the template itself never joins the scene graph, sizes it from its first texture's picture when the model states no size (it was 0x0, so nothing created from it ever drew), and answers a missing path without logging errors, because the runtime now asks for two spellings. Imported audio-visualizer bar assets whose source layers are hidden drew nothing and their scripts threw every frame. No per-frame work, extra passes or wallpaper-specific rules; script runtime and parsed-scene regressions fail with the change removed.
sceneEngine.puppetColorBlendModeChanges: 2026-10-10: An image layer's colorBlendMode on a puppet with bones is applied by the skinned pass that draws the layer on screen (BLENDMODE on that material, which samples the screen behind it) instead of by the separate passthrough effect, which ran before the skinned pass over the texture sheet and so blended the whole screen squeezed into the layer's bounds -- a shrunken copy of the wallpaper inside the layer and opaque mesh-shaped blocks where a multiply shadow belonged. Non-puppet layers and mesh-only puppets keep the passthrough as their last, on-screen effect. Same pass count; the passthrough is dropped, not added. A parsed render-graph regression with a synthetic one-bone puppet fails with the change removed.
sceneEngine.spacePosterContextChanges: 2026-10-08: Carry the host's bounded desktop-poster context through each queued SceneWallpaperBindings readback request and its ready notification. Context is paired with the captured request generation, including retries, so a late frame cannot be credited to a newer Space visit. No pixel, shader, notice, UniFFI or rendering policy changes; Swift validates context before encoding/publishing per-Space posters.
sceneEngine.parentParallaxChanges: 2026-10-03: Resolve parent-controlled parallax depth once at scene load, before material slots and effect cards are constructed. Children use the outermost parent's depth, including zero/default, independent of declaration order; missing/ambiguous parents and cycles do not invent an inherited value. Existing local-camera exclusions and cursor-dependent reuse remain unchanged. Synthetic schema, puppet-slot and direct/effect Metal pixel regressions cover nesting, stale child values, transforms, motion and reversal; the GPU regression fails with inheritance removed. Offscreen probe input now reaches shader and particle pointer state as well as runtime events. No wallpaper-specific branches, asset edits, extra passes, textures or per-frame ancestor work.
sceneEngine.nodeOriginTimelineChanges: 2026-10-02: Authored layer origin timelines now bind through the shared runtime for images, text, groups, particles, models and perspective camera nodes. Three component curves share one existing playback clock; relative offsets use the authored base, missing axes retain their values, and unchanged frames reuse their sample. Script/user bindings retain precedence, alignment and effect-final transforms use the existing path, and orthographic camera shots keep their linked zoom/origin clock. Completed single-shot timelines relinquish animation demand. Synthetic CPU and Metal direct/effect regressions plus the generated Compatibility curtain case cover playback and full-canvas reveal. No wallpaper-specific rules, extra render passes, texture allocations or disabled optimizations.
sceneEngine.scriptColorAndLayerLookupChanges: 2026-10-02: SceneScript addColor converts persisted RGB strings to Vec3 values on initial binding and subsequent property updates, while text properties retain their string type. Duplicate authored layer names resolve to the first declaration through a separate lookup alias; internal node keys and each script's thisLayer remain independent. Synthetic regressions cover repeated color updates, user-property changes, early name lookups, mixed image/group declaration order and runtime-free parsing. Live Solar System was checked with surface-free Vulkan renders; no package-specific rule or private asset is included in source.
sceneEngine.softwareVideoImportChanges: 2026-10-03: Software-decoded BGRA, NV12, YUV420P and YUVJ420P frames allocate their existing output buffer with IOSurface backing and Metal compatibility, so the GPU can import them instead of leaving video wallpapers black. Hardware decode selection, color conversion and frame scheduling are unchanged; no second pixel copy, conversion target or GPU wait is added. apple_video_frame_test.mm runs in playback_gpu_test and checks all four generated formats, strided color/alpha pixels, lease lifetime and direct-import work. An opt-in WE_TEST_VIDEO diagnostic checks a local file read-only; no wallpaper identifiers or assets are embedded.
sceneEngine.videoDecoderSelectionChanges: 2026-10-15: FfmpegVideoTextureSource keeps an already VideoToolbox-capable default decoder, but when FFmpeg's default is software-only it searches the registered decoders for the same codec ID using the existing VideoToolbox/HW_DEVICE_CTX requirement. This lets native AV1 hardware decode remain eligible when libdav1d is the default, without admitting software-only codecs or changing get_format, frame extraction, scheduling or per-frame work. VideoDecoderSelection in playback_gpu_test embeds an original 152-byte solid-red AV1 fixture produced with standalone FFmpeg/SVT-AV1 4.2.0 and checks an IOSurface-backed NV12 first frame plus known Metal pixels after decoder release; generated H.264 still imports and a software-only PPM stream is still rejected. AV1 hardware absence is an explicit skip. No private wallpaper media or identifying rules are embedded.
sceneEngine.puppetEffectLightingChanges: 2026-10-02: Puppet layers with effects disable LIGHTING only on the unassembled input-sheet pass; the existing final skinned pass retains the authored material and lights the assembled geometry once. This removes double attenuation and illumination seams between cut-out pieces without a wallpaper-specific rule, extra pass, allocation or quality reduction. The legacy four-light uniform pack now writes the fourth RGB light into the three vec4 w lanes instead of discarding it. Original Metal pixel coverage checks lit/unlit, puppet/card and effect/direct paths across repeated draws; a uniform regression covers zero through five lights and clearing. Both regressions fail with the fixes disabled.
sceneEngine.sceneProjectionShaderChanges: 2026-10-02: LoadMaterial supplies SCENE_ORTHO from the authored scene projection for both backends and effect chains, overriding material values. Orthographic lit layers no longer take a perspective view direction on their own plane and collapse to ambient-only brightness. The combo participates in existing shader request/cache identity; no passes, textures, per-frame CPU work or wallpaper-specific branches are added. An original Metal pixel regression covers orthographic/perspective, direct/effect and lit/unlit paths and fails without the fix. The pre-existing PerformLighting_V1 approximation is unchanged; exact authored-light parity is not claimed.
sceneEngine.parallaxDelayChanges: 2026-10-02: WPShaderValueUpdater::FrameBegin treats a camera parallax delay of zero (or less) as no smoothing and follows the cursor at once, the limit of its ramp, instead of dividing the elapsed time by the delay. The 0/0 latched NaN into the smoothed cursor, then into g_PointerPosition and every parallax layer's model matrix, so a scene authored with `cameraparallaxdelay: 0` drew only its clear colour on both backends. WPCameraParallax's amount, delay and mouse influence are zero-initialized. Regression: ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.ZeroParallaxDelayFollowsTheCursorAtOnce in script_runtime_compat_test.
sceneEngine.pooledPinChanges: 2026-10-02: TextureCache::PinRenderTarget also refuses a key whose pooled image it took from a key that released it, since that key's prepared passes keep drawing into the image every frame; only keys still mapped to the same allocation (aliases of an elided copy, which write nothing) may share a pinned image. Pinning such a key let Compatibility static reuse skip its writers and leave the other target's pixels in place, so from the second frame a layer read another layer's picture and pooled output diverged from isolated (WE_TEST_NO_REUSE). The refused target is redrawn each frame instead of reused; no allocation is added. Regression: PlaybackGPU.APooledImageAnotherTargetStillDrawsIntoIsNeverPinned in playback_gpu_test.
sceneEngine.hdrAndInteractionParityChanges: 2026-10-01: HDR scenes select HDR shader combinations and RGBA16F color targets across Metal/Vulkan, effects and linked layers; masks/media and SDR remain unchanged. Shipped HDR bloom passes use a general bounded model: spread maps to s/(1+s), pyramid weights normalize extraction energy, strength remains independent, and sample offsets refresh at prepare/resize. Exact proprietary Wallpaper Engine parameter parity is not established. TEX bit23 and the fourth component cross the C++/Rust shader interface, enabling alpha-channel emissive masks. Perspective particle billboards retain object scale without altering authored 2D pixel compensation or count semantics. Property scripts receive initial full settings and later changed-key callbacks once, after complete property propagation. Completed text layouts publish monotonically while retaining newer pending requests, preventing continuously changing readouts from remaining blank. Shared offscreen probe controls exercise clicks, hover exits, audio waves and 60/120 Hz animation without desktop/audio-device access. No private asset edits or wallpaper-specific rendering branches.
sceneEngine.perspectiveSceneCompatibilityChanges: 2026-09-30: Perspective scenes without an authored canvas rasterize at the output extent and selected render scale, retain source mip detail for projected model UVs, and use a screen-space camera for fullscreen effects. Authored transparent sorting schedules depth-tested opaque geometry before translucent cards. Text styles use uniforms over cached glyph masks; FIFO coalescing prevents stale clocks, and effect targets grow only when text exceeds capacity. Property text scripts start on the ordered runtime tick. Script-created layers have independent identity, owner-local factory facades, live tint/alpha and lazy image-template loading. External material references retain hidden producers. All model versions use the flag-aware mesh decoder without legacy attribute loss or first-mesh copies. Compatibility writes live engine uniforms after parser defaults. Original regressions and surface-free probes cover these general paths; no wallpaper asset or identifier is embedded in renderer code.
sceneEngine.equalQualityPerformanceChanges: 2026-09-24: Metal and Vulkan borrow their synchronous per-pass uniform writer through std::cref without changing UpdateUniformOp. ShaderValue packs MatrixBase coefficients column-major into its existing owning inline/vector storage; non-direct expressions evaluate once in the original scalar type. AudioResponseService uses a shared logical FIFO read offset and bounded append-time compaction/geometric capacity growth while retaining the 1024-frame FFT window, 200-frame hop and 24000-frame limit. Matrix ownership/layout and continuous stereo-window regressions cover the changes; oversized comparisons wait for all 115 windows. Upstream revisions are unchanged. 2026-09-27 (video counters off): TextureCache::UpdateVideoFrame reads the decoder's stats, publishes the source identity and observes frame selection only while RendererCounters are enabled. An update that runs while counting is off marks the video texture stale, and the next counted update only records the decoder's totals and seeds the selection tracker with the frame on screen, so work done while counting was off is never reported. Files: src/Vulkan/TextureCache.cpp, src/Vulkan/include/Vulkan/TextureCache.hpp, tests/playback_gpu_test.mm. 2026-09-27 (uniform lookups, R14): each CustomShaderPass update_op owns a UniformMemo built at prepare. Updater names resolve to reflected BlockedUniform pointers through a content-compared memo with a rotating cursor (a miss falls back to member_map.find and is recorded, absent included); material constants are a (BlockedUniform*, ShaderValue*) table in map order, rebuilt when the material or constValues.size() changes (constValues is insert-only or updated in place after parse). A slot's IsRuntimeImage answer is cached and asked again only when the new RuntimeImageSource::NamesGeneration() moves or the slot's name changes. WPShaderValueUpdater double map lookups are collapsed. Every value is still written every frame through WriteUniform and the memcmp-gated upload. Files: src/Scene/VulkanRender/CustomShaderPass.cpp, src/Runtime/RuntimeImageSource.hpp, src/Scene/WPShaderValueUpdater.cpp, tests/playback_gpu_test.mm. 2026-09-27 (framebuffer-only swapchain, R18): Vulkan/Swapchain creates COLOR_ATTACHMENT-only images and drops supportsReadback, so MoltenVK sets the layer framebufferOnly. A requested poster is composed a second time, by the pass that composed the drawable, into a one-frame PosterTarget (VulkanRender CreatePosterTarget; refused when its real VMA allocation exceeds kPosterByteLimit, the existing 128 MiB) through FinPass::recordComposition or CustomShaderPass::recordPresentation with copy-source render passes (final layout TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL), then copied to the readback buffer; the drawable is never read. Files: src/Vulkan/Swapchain.cpp, src/Vulkan/include/Vulkan/Swapchain.hpp, src/Scene/VulkanRender/{VulkanRender.cpp,FinPass.cpp,FinPass.hpp,CustomShaderPass.cpp,CustomShaderPass.hpp}, tests/playback_gpu_test.mm. 2026-09-27 (plain-video direct presentation, R8): CustomShaderPass::Desc::presents_through_final_viewport, set by VulkanRender only for scene.single_video_source, lets canPresentDirectly accept the final composition's viewport/scissor and a target extent unlike the output when exactly one bound texture has the output's extent; executePresentation then draws through ResolvePresentationViewport/Scissor sampling with the output's own sampler (recordDescriptors sampler override). Mirrored frames and frames of another size keep the copy plus FinPass. SceneWallpaperInputTestAccess::CreateVideoProjectNode exposes the production layer to tests. sceneEngine.deferredSurfaceLifetimeChanges: 2026-09-27: The Apple surface factory captures a strong CAMetalLayer in its deferred surface callback so asynchronous backend selection and host layer replacement cannot leave the native-backend handle dangling. playback_gpu_test checks retention after the host releases the layer and release when the scene is deleted; it flushes Core Animation’s implicit transaction to expose missing scene ownership. Upstream CopyPass teardown and its render-scale regression are unchanged.
sceneEngine.note: 2026-09-28 (owed frames): a tick dropped because the previous draw was still running is run at once (ThreadTimer::FireNow, cadence restarted) when that draw ends within a quarter interval of it, so draws just over one period no longer halve the rate; a cadence tick that is late by more than the step its deadline took (the ceiling when a request cut the wait) restarts from now, so requests after a long wait cannot outrun the ceiling. Covered by FrameTimerTest.ADrawSlightlyLongerThanTheIntervalDoesNotHalveTheRate and ThreadTimerTest.RequestsAfterALongWaitStillRespectTheCeiling. SetMinInterval's documentation now says the ceiling is measured from when the last tick was due, not from a late wake. 2026-09-28 (frame clock): ThreadTimer anchors each cadence tick to the deadline it was due at instead of the time the thread woke, so wait slack no longer lengthens the period (a 60 fps ceiling had delivered about 50 frames a second); a tick more than a whole interval late restarts the cadence. Event-driven idle ticks still anchor at the wake time. ThreadTimerTest.CadenceKeepsItsPeriodDespiteWakeSlack covers it. 2026-09-27 (copy pass rebuild): VulkanRender CopyPass::destory now marks the copy unprepared, clears its release list and drops its source/destination image parameters, like the other passes. applyRenderScale and the copy-elision rebuild destroy every pass, drop the render targets and prepare only unprepared passes; a copy that stayed prepared recorded vkCmdCopyImage between freed images and crashed in MoltenVK (a render scale below 1 crashed the compatibility renderer at every launch). playback_gpu_test covers the rebuild. 2026-09-27 (log scopes): Utils/Logging adds a thread-local log scope (SetWallpaperLogScope, WallpaperLogScope); Looper::setLogScope makes a looper thread adopt it at start; SceneWallpaper::setLogScope sets it on the scene's main and render loopers before init. SceneWallpaperBindings exposes owe_current_log_scope and owe_scene_wallpaper_set_log_scope (refused after init). setSceneBackendSelection logs the backend in use and any fallback reason once per scene. Logging only; no rendering change. 2026-09-25 (2D camera shots, parallax and layer composites; Workshop 3521337568): In an orthographic scene a camera layer now frames the canvas instead of being ignored. ParseCameraObj registers each shot with SceneRuntimeContext::RegisterCameraShot; at the end of every tick, after scripts and every visibility and origin writer, ApplyCameraShots passes the last visible shot in authored order to the new Scene::FrameCanvas. zoom narrows the orthographic view about its centre and the origin's x/y is that centre's offset from the canvas centre, the reading 3605722997's shots, the lens scripts of 3605722997 and 3292361861 and 3521337568's intro agree on; with no visible shot the whole canvas is shown. A script- or user-bound origin frames the view only once a tick has applied it. The perspective camera takes the same centre and a fov spanning the same visible height (ApplyCameraFillMode and ApplySceneZoomAnimation use VisibleHeight as well). A zoom and origin keyed together (options.parent) play on one clock, a relative origin curve offsets the authored origin, and DescribeTimeAdvancingWork counts a playback only while it plays (only a script command restarts one), so a finished single-play intro no longer keeps a still scene awake. In 2D scenes a fullscreen layer's last pass is drawn through the new `fullscreen` camera, which always frames the canvas; 3D scenes are unchanged (none checked). A layer sampled as _rt_imageLayerComposite_<id> is drawn into that target through a layer-local camera (LayerCompositeCameraKey, SceneCamera::SetLayerLocal); compose cameras are not flagged, and a composelayer keeps sampling the screen behind it. The static-reuse camera fold is one helper, vulkan::FoldPassCameras in PassCommon.hpp, called by both CustomShaderPass::frameSample (which now takes the scene; offscreen_scene_probe updated) and the Metal backend. In 2D scenes camera parallax is the cursor's offset times depth, amount and influence; the layer-position term the 2026-09-23 entry corrected pushed 3521337568's depth-0.5 planet out of the frame, and 3D scenes keep it. The formula rests on 3521337568's preview, which shows that planet in frame, and on ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.CameraParallaxFollowsTheCursorAndDepthNotThePosition. linux-wallpaperengine's CScene.cpp (GPLv3) was read for behaviour only while checking it; no code from it was copied, translated or adapted. FrameVaryingUniforms takes the pass's camera_override and reports kParallax for a pass parallax moves through that camera (not the effect camera, not a layer-local composite camera), so static reuse redraws its target and an on-demand scene wakes for the pointer. Recorded under Known limitations in docs/testing/renderer.md, not changed here: such targets are never reused, on-demand rendering does not ask for frames while parallax eases, and CustomShaderPass uploads parse-time constants after the value updater's live values. RegisterMaterialTexture no longer folds a zero g_TextureNResolution for a link texture, which the card padding divided by. The new Scripting/ScriptModuleSyntax matches `export` and `export function update` across ECMAScript whitespace (U+00A0, U+FEFF, Zs, line terminators) and only where a statement can start (ExportKeywordAt holds the one boundary rule), for the module rewrite, HasUpdateScript and wrap_script_if_needed; the rewrite erases only the keyword. Regressions: SceneSchema.CameraObjectTimelineGlidesFromItsFirstShotToWhereItRests, .TheLastVisibleCameraObjectFramesTheCanvas, .AScriptedShotOriginFramesTheViewOnceATickHasAppliedIt, .ParserCopiesImageParallaxDepthToPuppetMaterialSlots (cursor moved), ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.CameraParallaxFollowsTheCursorAndDepthNotThePosition (replaces CameraParallaxPlacesAChildLayerByItsScenePosition) and .ParallaxLayersAreReportedAsFollowingTheCursor, ScriptRuntimeCompat.ComposeBackgroundUsesScreenCameraAndParentTransform (composite case), .ExportFollowedByUnicodeWhitespaceStillCompiles, .AnUpdateSeparatedByUnicodeWhitespaceStillDrivesItsProperty, ScriptModuleSyntax.*, LayerTextureReference.AReferencedLayerIsItsCardWhereverTheSceneShowsIt (framing and reuse), .AReferencedCompositeIsSampledAtItsRealSize (both upload orders), .ComposeChildrenKeepTheirPlaceInsideTheLayer, and CameraFraming.AFullscreenLayerCoversTheScreenWhateverTheShot and .MovingTheCameraChangesTheStaticSampleOfAPassItDraws; each fails with its fix reverted. 2026-09-24 (texture decode at pass preparation): CustomShaderPass::prepare asks TextureCache::FindTex before parsing a package or loose image, because CreateTex answers a cached key without reading the pixels it is handed; a texture bound by several passes is no longer decoded once per pass. Runtime images keep resolving through the parser. New TexturePrefetch (Scene/VulkanRender) decodes the images the unprepared passes will parse on up to six worker threads, ahead of the pass that binds them; RenderingResources::texture_prefetch carries it only while VulkanRender::preparePasses runs, and offscreen_scene_probe drives preparation the same way. Uploads, their order and the texture cache stay on the preparing thread. Decoding and untaken images are held under a 256 MiB budget estimated from each header (RGBA8 plus a mip chain; one larger image is admitted alone) and admitted strictly in request order; preparation never waits on an image not yet admitted and decodes that one itself. Videos, sprite sheets, runtime images, render targets and uploaded textures are not prefetched. A 943 MB puppet scene of 122 embedded PNG textures (1264 Mpx) reached its first offscreen frame in 15.6 s, dominated by single-threaded stb_image inflate; 14.7 s with the FindTex check alone and 3.6 s with the prefetch, with a byte-identical frame and peak RSS rising from about 0.8 to 1.1 GB. A worker thread that fails to start is dropped rather than unwinding with joinable threads; with none, preparation decodes every image itself. texture_prefetch_test covers ordering, the budget, admission skipping, a pool that could not start, decode failures and teardown. Upstream revisions are unchanged. 2026-09-24 (interleaved feedback-copy correctness): MetalRender retains pending opening copies by destination texture instead of one copy_into/copy_from slot, so copy A to Ac and copy B to Bc can both remain pending until B then A renders. The per-frame storage is cleared on frame abandonment and graph release. InterleavedFeedbackCopiesPreserveEachReadersImage compares both targets against the ordinary blit path over four frames; restoring single-slot overwrite semantics corrupts A and fails the pixel check. No frame-clock scheduling code changed. 2026-09-24 (Metal render passes, uniform lookups and reuse sampling): MetalRender::drawFrame keeps one render command encoder open across consecutive passes into the same target texture, the rule PlanCustomPassBatches batches the compatibility backend by. A pass starts a new render pass only for another target, another depth attachment, a read of its own target (resolved through the target table, so copy-plan aliases count), or a clear, unless the open render pass began with that same clear and has drawn nothing; a draw that shares a render pass sets the pipeline, the depth-stencil state and every texture and sampler slot it declares, nil included, so nothing the previous draw bound leaks into it. A pass whose layer is hidden (passDraws false, the predicate the old hidden-pass check used) writes no uniforms, uploads no dynamic mesh and opens no encoder unless it carries a clear, as CustomShaderPass::updateFrame does. Per-pass colour and depth textures are resolved once per target-table change (refreshPassTargets, from compile and applySceneOptimizationSetting). writeUniforms resolves reflection members by write position (UniformWriteSlot on PreparedPass and VideoPlaneDraw), comparing names instead of hashing each one into the reflection every frame. StaticSubgraphCache::PassSampled names the passes Plan reads; both backends take no frameSample for the rest, and Metal, like Vulkan already, stops planning while nothing is pinned. Test-only MetalRender::LastFrameEncodeCountsForTests reports render passes, scene-output render passes and blits per frame; metal_scene_draw_smoke prints them with thread CPU per drawFrame for WE_TEST_METAL_PROJECTS and adds LayersSharingATargetShareOneRenderPassAndHiddenLayersCostNone, and static_subgraph_cache_test adds OnlyWritersOfCacheableTargetsAreSampled. Workshop 3620484312 at 3456x2234: 179 to 47 render passes per frame (154 to 22 into the scene's own image; the other 21 each follow a full-frame copy of that image a clipping-mask effect reads), 1.82 to 0.75 ms CPU per drawFrame, byte-identical output. 2026-09-24 (Metal feedback copies): a copy the graph inserts only so the next pass can sample the image it draws into (a material reading _rt_FullFrameBuffer) is replaced by trading the two names' textures. planFeedbackSwaps plans it, after the reuse table, only where exact: both textures private to one name, equal size, RGBA8Unorm, one mip level, no depth attachment on either name, neither target cacheable, and the reader the next pass to touch the source, drawing into it without reading it and loading it (a clearing reader needs no opening copy). At encode time the copy's name takes the source texture, the source's name the copy's texture, and the reader's render pass opens with DontCare and a full-target draw of owe_copy_fragment, which reads the old image texel for texel; a reader that does not render that frame gets the copy as a blit instead, and an abandoned frame undoes its trades. Gated with the rest of the copy plan by scene optimisation; WALLPAPER_MACHINE_FEEDBACK_COPIES=1 forces the copies for A/B measurement. metal_scene_draw_smoke adds AFeedbackCopyTradesTexturesAndDrawsTheSamePicture. Workshop 3620484312: 21 to 0 blits per frame, 47 render passes unchanged, byte-identical output. 2026-09-23 (camera parallax for nested layers): WPShaderValueUpdater offsets a layer by its scene position (the translation of the matrix it is drawn with) instead of its parent-relative origin. A layer inside a group has a local origin near zero, so a full-screen child of a centred group was pushed as if it sat in the canvas corner: in Workshop 3632513108 the intro layer moved 69 x 39 px, beyond its 1.02 overscan, and uncovered the layers beneath it along the left and bottom edges. Top-level layers are unchanged (local and scene origin agree); effect final nodes now follow the same rule; both renderers share this updater. Regression: ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.CameraParallaxPlacesAChildLayerByItsScenePosition in script_runtime_compat_test. 2026-09-22 (scenetexture slots, camera-object zoom, layer parents and alpha): a `usertextures` entry that names one of the wallpaper's own `scenetexture` properties now takes that property's value. A package-relative asset is reduced to the bare texture name the loader addresses, an absolute path the image picker wrote is read from the host by WPTexImageParser, and an unset property keeps the texture the author shipped. Workshop 3588579284 offers eight "choose your own picture" slots that all showed packaged artwork. A camera object's `zoom` now frames an orthographic canvas through SceneCamera::SetZoom, applied when the projection is built so the fill mode's width/height rewrite on every output resize cannot silently drop it; the shot still does not become the active camera on a 2D scene, and `path`/`queuemode` stay parse-only. thisLayer.getParent() answers with the parent layer, or null at the scene root: Workshop 3632513108's dock icon scripts threw "cannot read property 'visible' of undefined" once a frame, so the icons never scaled, faded or opened anything. layer.alpha writes now reach g_UserAlpha for layers whose authored alpha is not already owned by a timeline, an update script or a user property, keeping one writer per frame. A loose asset now carries where it has to be read from (LooseAssetCandidate::isHost) instead of that being re-derived from the path: a mounted /assets/materials/foo.png is absolute too, so deciding by is_absolute() sent every packaged loose picture and video to the host filesystem. A texture property is only taken when the file it names opens now (HostLooseAssetIsReadable), so a picture the user moved, or one the sandboxed lock-screen extension may not read, leaves the slot on the authored texture rather than on a name that decodes to nothing. Pointer mapping reads SceneCamera::VisibleWidth and VisibleHeight, the same zoomed extent the ortho projection is built from, so clicks and mouse-linked particles follow a zoomed 2D scene instead of staying on the unzoomed image. 2026-09-22 (shared layer names): a text label that repeats a name already used by a group, image or model is registered as __we_text_<id> instead of replacing that node. Workshop 3662790108 names both its sun group and a hidden readout s; the readout took the name, getLayer("s") scaled the readout into full-height white bars, and the sun group never received the simulation scale. 2026-09-22 (scripted image alpha): an image alpha update script or user property now writes g_Alpha. Workshop 3662790108's intro card stayed at its authored opacity and covered the star shell; the script can fade it. 2026-09-22 (perspective models and cold apply): mdlv23 meshes with more than 65535 vertices store uint32 indices. Reading them as uint16 rejected Saturn's body and scrambled solar-system meshes that stayed under the old 1 million vertex cap; the cap is now 4 million and the draw uses a 32-bit index buffer. A mat4 written into the std140 mat3 g_NormalModelMatrix spilled into g_ViewProjectionMatrix and collapsed perspective draws to one column; writes are now clamped to the reflected member and the constant is 12 floats. Culled passes keep counter-clockwise on MoltenVK. The perspective far plane is padded slightly so a skybox scaled to exactly far is not clipped. The driver's pipeline cache is saved beside the scene shader cache. The bridge waits 90 seconds for a first frame so a cold MoltenVK compile (measured 27s for workshop 3588579284) can finish. 2026-09-21 (cursor in scene coordinates): `SceneRuntimeContext::SetCursorInput` publishes the point it maps through the presentation's cursor viewport to `Scene::pointerScenePosition`, and a particle system's mouse-linked control point reads that instead of deriving `pointerPosition * ortho`. The canvas is not the window: a 2560x1440 wallpaper filling a 4112x2658 display is cropped to the canvas range [166.3, 2394.2], so the old product agreed with the cursor at the centre of the window and was wrong by 165.8 scene units -- about 306 physical pixels -- at either edge, which is a mouse trail that tracks in the middle of the screen and slides away toward the sides on every wallpaper that has one. 2026-09-21 (camera layers in 2D scenes): a scene with `orthogonalprojection` is projected by that canvas, and every 2D layer's geometry, origin and alignment is authored against it. A `camera` layer in such a scene no longer attaches to, re-poses or activates the perspective camera; it stays an ordinary node the scene's scripts can read and move. It used to take over, so the whole wallpaper was reframed through a perspective camera sitting at the authored shot pose -- typically a few hundred units off the canvas plane at fov 50 -- which left a magnified sliver of one canvas corner and the clear colour everywhere else. Scenes whose `orthogonalprojection` is null are unchanged: there the shot is the projection. 2026-09-21 (screen-bound texture resolution): g_TextureNResolution is re-baked once the output size is known. A target that follows the screen is registered with placeholder dimensions while the scene parses, and that placeholder was folded into the material, so a separable blur stepping by 1/g_Texture0Resolution.zw divided by two and put every tap outside the texture -- an effect chain's background came out a flat wash instead of blurred. 2026-09-21 (corrected): the album-cover rejection added earlier today is withdrawn. Native Metal does keep runtime images current; the measurement that said otherwise came from a harness whose media injection was never called, so every Metal render was made without a cover and the flat grey that produced was read as a backend defect. The Metal harness now says out loud whether it could publish the cover. 2026-09-21 (album cover on Native Metal): a scene that binds a system media slot falls back to Compatibility with a stated reason, because the native backend uploads an image when it prepares and never sees the runtime republish it -- it drew the empty placeholder, so neither the cover nor anything derived from it appeared. metal_scene_draw_smoke also takes WE_TEST_MEDIA_ARTWORK and WE_TEST_MEDIA_EVENTS with the same meaning offscreen_scene_probe gives them, so a media-driven wallpaper can be held against the other backend. 2026-09-21 (shortcut tracing): openUserShortcut logs the property it resolved and the value it resolved to, and the main-looper hop logs whether a request and a callback were both present. A press is rare and deliberate, and without this an unbound button is indistinguishable from one whose request never reached the host. 2026-09-21 (cursor release capture): a button's release is delivered to whichever scripted values and scene scripts took its press, rather than re-hit-tested at release time. Buttons that shrink while held -- workshop 3280146735's transport buttons scale to a tenth -- moved out from under the cursor and never heard their own release, leaving them shrunk for good. 2026-09-21 (progress fill coverage): scene_schema_tests drives workshop 3280146735's own progress-fill origin script through ScriptedDynamicValue, pinning that a published mediaTimelineChanged places the fill and that the author's own first-event ordering divides by an unset duration. 2026-09-21 (power regression, round 6): restoring CMD_SET_RENDER_SCALE dispatch made MetalRender::ApplyRenderScale reachable, and it compiled unconditionally — releasing the graph, closing every video and dropping every uploaded image — while the host pushes the scale as a live property to every open scene on creation and on each power-source change. It now clamps and returns early on an unchanged value, as the compatibility backend already did. The -Werror=switch guard also surfaced a live misreport rather than a stale warning: the host decodes 5 as the converted-but-preparing video path, the C enumeration stopped at 4, and owe_scene_wallpaper_video_path fell out of its switch to NONE, so a scene working towards that path was reported as having no video at all; the enumerator and its case are added. 2026-09-21 (power regression, round 3): a runtime image binding shares ownership of the image it samples rather than borrowing a handle, because a cover change aliases two runtime names onto one Image::key and whichever binding refreshed second retired the key the first had just bound to. RenderHandler's command switch was missing CASE_CMD(SET_RENDER_SCALE), so CMD_SET_RENDER_SCALE reached no handler and the scene render scale stayed at its default however the user set it; the case is restored and the switch is now exhaustive with a fixed-width enum and no default, so -Wswitch names the next command that is posted and not dispatched. 2026-09-21 (power regression, engine side): the configured frame rate bounds every path into a frame, not only the cadence. ThreadTimer takes a minimum interval and applies it to one-shot requests and to appointments including ones already past, so a burst of events coalesces into one frame per period instead of one frame each; an idle clock with nothing pending still waits without a deadline. FrameTimer holds a request until a draw consumes it and re-arms from FrameEnd, which is the only point that sees both a suppressed tick and the scene deciding to idle. A now-playing cover is published into the runtime image source and no longer rebuilds the render graph -- both backends already re-read a runtime image whose version moved -- and an identical cover is dropped before it costs anything, including the wake. TextureCache holds cached images through shared ownership, because two runtime names alias one image on every cover change and retiring one key would otherwise free the image the other still samples. VulkanRender skips the per-frame static-cache sampling and signature walk when no target is pinned, since reuse is then impossible, and writes its skip plan into the buffer it already owns. 2026-09-20 (target dump symmetry): offscreen_scene_probe takes WE_TEST_DUMP_TARGETS with the same meaning the Metal harness gives it, and both write the alpha channel separately under WE_TEST_DUMP_ALPHA. Effects that weight by coverage -- the bokeh downsample divides by the sum of its taps' alpha -- make different colour from the same RGB when alpha differs, so a colour-only dump cannot explain them. 2026-09-20 (sound volume): a sound layer whose volume the author bound to a slider arrives as {"user": …, "value": …} rather than a number. Only the number was read, so the binding was dropped and the user's own slider moved nothing; the parser now records the property and the sound follows it. 2026-09-20 (user shortcut delivery): SceneWallpaper drains the runtime's shortcut requests after the tick that produced them and reports each on the native main looper, with owe_scene_wallpaper_set_user_shortcut_callback following the pointer-callback contract exactly (callback + user_data + drop, userdata untouched on failure). Deciding what a press means must never sit in front of a frame, so nothing is interpreted on the render thread. 2026-09-20 (user shortcuts): engine.openUserShortcut(name) exists. It was missing entirely, so a wallpaper whose transport buttons call it threw TypeError out of cursorDown and the press did nothing at all. The binding resolves the named property against the wallpaper's own declared properties -- naming another throws, rather than passing silently -- and queues the request with that property's VALUE, which is the user's choice and the only thing a host may act on.
