WPSceneParser no longer reduces rope subdivision or rewrites a rope trail as a sprite trail; PlanParticleIndexLayout/ParticleGeometryFits size the mesh with uint64 math against a 1 GiB vertex+index budget shared by both backends. SceneIndexArray gains SceneIndexWidth, DrawIndexCount/DrawIndexBytes and a (quadCount, width) constructor; WPParticleRawGener writes uint32 indices when the mesh says so. MetalRender and CustomShaderPass bind MTLIndexTypeUInt32 / VK_INDEX_TYPE_UINT32 from that width. Tests: scene_mesh_tests capacity math, particle_rope_geometry_test index width and order, metal_scene_draw_smoke ARopeTrailPastTheOldSixteenBitIndexLimitStaysARopeTrail. 2026-09-19 (round 14 item 3): rope/rope-trail UV scale is encoded in the trail-length the generator writes (no author uniform). uvscrolling measures V against mesh/history capacity so a growing rope unrolls instead of stretching. uvsmoothing eases trail-position with smoothstep. Sprite-sheet plus UV scale/scroll is logged as unsupported because genericropeparticle samples the whole texture. Runtime updates go through ParticleSubSystem::SetRopeUv and ParticleRenderScale without re-parsing. 2026-09-19 (round 14 item 2): Native Metal accepts perspective cameras for the layer types it already draws. The whole-scene IsPerspective refusals are gone; projection is SceneCamera's FOV/aspect/near/far through the existing Metal clip-space fold; depth attachments are allocated only for passes whose material depth-tests, at the colour target's size; g_Orientation* follows the camera node; perspective hit tests unproject onto the layer plane. Tests in metal_backend_test and MetalSceneDraw.APerspectiveCameraDrawsThroughTheAuthoredShader. Also 2026-09-19 (round 14 item 1): layer-as-texture. Authored `_rt_imageLayerComposite_<id>[_a|_b]` is resolved in two phases onto `_rt_link_<id>` with explicit missing/duplicate/cycle/history reasons; hidden sources still produce an isolated composite. Both backends consume that description. 2026-09-20 (round 14 empty-key follow-up): MetalRender BuildMetalResourcePlan leaves unsampled in-range texture/sampler slots and an unused GlobalUniforms buffer unbound, matching Vulkan CustomShaderPass empty-name skip / SPIR-V omitted descriptors. prepareDraw missing-image message names slot and shader. 2026-09-19: the build pins the FFmpeg headers pkg-config resolved ahead of every other include directory (wescene_prefer_ffmpeg_headers in CMakeLists.txt, applied to wescene-renderer, wpAudio and the FFmpeg-linking tests) because a second Homebrew FFmpeg linked into /opt/homebrew/include was reaching the compiler first and its AVFrame layout left best_effort_timestamp reading a neighbouring field, which stamped every decoded frame at time zero and froze scene video textures; src/Video/FfmpegAbi.hpp refuses to decode or probe when the loaded libav* majors are not the compiled ones, and a decode thread that dies now logs why instead of leaving the last frame on screen in silence. Scene::first_frame_ok belongs to the frame handler: MetalRender no longer sets it and reports presentation through drawFrame's new `presented` out-parameter (mirrored by VulkanRender and SceneRendererHandle), so a native first frame reaches the host instead of expiring its startup deadline, and a tick that found no drawable is not counted as one. Test: metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm ADrawnFrameIsReportedAsPresentedAndLeavesTheFirstFrameFlagAlone. 2026-09-21 (project rename): the desktop-poster handshake notifications are `WallpaperMachine.requestDesktopPoster` and `WallpaperMachine.desktopPosterReady`, matching the host, content pacing reads `WALLPAPER_MACHINE_CONTENT_PACING`, and metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm falls back to `Application Support/WallpaperMachine/SceneAssets`. Names only; no behavior change.
sceneEngine.gpuAllocationChanges: Apple Vulkan allocators prefer 8 MiB blocks instead of the VMA default 256 MiB to reduce unused shared-memory reservations. Large resources remain supported. The surface-free GPU test verifies that releasing a 40 MiB frame buffer does not retain an oversized empty block; the scene probe reports reserved and allocated bytes for same-pixel comparisons. The follow-up reduces the earlier 32 MiB preference to 8 MiB; the current scene retains 28 MiB less reservation with identical allocated bytes and pixels.
sceneEngine.textureResidencyChanges: Both scene backends set a physical-display texture budget before preparing images (the cut rule here, a power-of-two ceiling of the longest edge, is superseded by textureMipBudgetChanges: a leading level is dropped only while the next one is at least as long as the display's longest edge). WPTexImageParser skips oversized authored mip payloads before decode/upload, preserves layout metadata, and excludes sprite/video/multi-slot/unknown-container inputs. RuntimeImageSource forwards the policy only to packaged fallback assets. Surface rebuilds refresh the budget. TexSchema tests cover selection, restoration, skipped encoded payloads, truncation, and sprite/video exclusions; offscreen_scene_probe exposes WE_TEST_TEXTURE_SURFACE for full-source comparisons. This changes source detail and is not an equal-quality or total-memory guarantee. The local-project Metal harness now honors WE_TEST_RANDOM_SEED for repeatable particle comparisons.
sceneEngine.nativeTargetResidencyChanges: Native Metal allocates only render targets referenced by the compiled pass descriptions or final presentation, both during compile and when scene optimization changes. Hidden draws, source/target copy keys and all texture input keys remain live; declaration-only shadow/mipmap/bloom buffers are not allocated. A GPU regression checks absence and output preservation across optimization toggles. Compile and the optimization toggle create target images through one newSceneTarget helper. A second GPU regression drops a copy the plan marks dead, turns optimization off without recompiling and checks that the copy gets a filled image and encodes no blit while optimization is on; it fails when copy destinations are left out of the referenced set or dead copies are made anyway. The local Metal harness takes its frame count from WE_TEST_METAL_FRAMES (2-3600, parsed after the no-project skip) so the probe's WE_TEST_FRAMES cannot shift its scene time, and prints MetalRender::RenderTargetBytesForTests next to the device-wide allocation.

auditRemediation.changes: Serialize shared-video preparation; conserve decoded audio across short reads, packet backpressure, drain and loops; apply video display matrices across Vulkan, Metal BGRA and direct NV12 paths; advance sprites by full elapsed time. Keep render graph terminal outputs and re-prepared target lifetimes consistent, refresh cached clear colors, propagate Metal archive overrides, balance pinned resources, isolate media caches, and make regression executables enforce assertions and classify GPU failures. Stabilize script program snapshots and hold audio-array bounds/views in native records; require Rust reflection metadata without legacy fallback. Implement text layout limits, local day time and random sound gaps. Correct BMP source-base decoding and stb allocation cleanup; fix miniaudio CoreAudio initialization, route replacement and pre-publication rollback. Enable JPEG NEON on arm64 after scalar-equivalent pixels and decoder-only timing checks. Empty artwork clears current/previous media textures and queued replay state. Original upstream notices and pinned revisions remain unchanged.
auditRemediation.reviewFollowup: PR #24 review: reject transformed BGRA sources when the conversion pipeline is unavailable; consistently skip unavailable video encoders and restore the test allocator through RAII.

puppetPoseBlendChanges.changes: Use effective non-additive layer weights for reference-pose deltas in translation, scale and rotation, matching the existing normalized base-pose budget. Prevent overlapping animations from stacking character-sheet assembly offsets. Additive weights, cached poses, passes and allocations are unchanged. Synthetic regressions cover normalized and partial weights, distinct motion, additive overlays, loop wrap, repeated samples and live blend/visibility changes.

presetAndSwitchLayerChanges.changes: Mount a scene's project folder under its package so a Workshop preset's own pictures and videos beside the base scene.pkg (files/...) resolve, with packaged files still winning; production and the probes share MountSceneSource. Draw a background-copying compose layer that another layer samples into its composite only, so masks that repaint it find their link texture instead of failing the native backend. Run property-script modules against their declared defaults and apply saved and user-bound scriptproperties before init, so top-level code sees the defaults as in Wallpaper Engine. Synthetic regressions cover each; no Workshop asset is committed.

sceneEngine.metalArchiveScratchChanges: 2026-10-13: MetalProgramCache::writeArchive serialises the pipeline archive to a scratch file in NSTemporaryDirectory() (owe-pipelines-<pid>-<serial>.metallib-archive, the serial touched only on the archive queue) and moves it to <store>.tmp<pid> before the existing replace-or-move over the store; a failed move logs and removes the scratch file. -[MTLBinaryArchive serializeToURL:error:] writes a scratch .metallib beside its destination and, when that folder is deleted during the write, double-frees in its error path (EXC_BAD_ACCESS in objc_retain, or a libmalloc abort, on macOS 27; reproduced standalone). The store's folder is the scene shader cache, which Clear shader cache, a cache rebuild or a removed wallpaper delete at any time, and the write runs two seconds after a wallpaper's last new pipeline. Found when unchanged_present_test removed its temporary folder right after a native case. Test-only MetalRender::WaitForPipelineArchiveWritesForTests (MetalProgramCache::finishArchiveWrites). Test: MetalSceneDraw.AStoreFolderDeletedWhileItsArchiveIsWrittenCostsOnlyThatWrite (eight stores written while their folders are deleted and made again in a loop; crashed 4 of 4 runs with serialisation beside the store, passes 4 of 4 with the change). No per-frame work: one extra rename per archive write.
sceneEngine.metalFrameStepChanges: 2026-10-13: MetalRender::drawFrame no longer calls WPShaderValueUpdater::FrameBegin. SceneWallpaper's draw handler already does once per frame for either backend; the second call stepped the parallax cursor's smoothing twice per frame, so the parallax on Native Metal chased the cursor twice as fast and a frame earlier than on Compatibility. Test loops that drive drawFrame directly (AdvanceSceneFrame, the local-project run, ParentedCardsStayJoinedWhileParallaxMovesAndReverses) take the host's step themselves. Test: TheParallaxEasingStepsOnceForEachFrameTheHostDraws.
sceneEngine.metalCullModeChanges: 2026-10-13: Native Metal now culls like Compatibility. A pass into a depth-attached target takes its material's cull mode (ScenePassDescription::cull_mode from SceneMetalCullMode in MetalBlend.hpp, set per draw), with counter-clockwise front faces (kSceneFrontFaceCounterClockwise), matching CustomShaderPass's VK_FRONT_FACE_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE behind its negative viewport; every other pass still culls nothing (kSceneCullMode). It used to cull nothing at all, which drew a planet ring model's unlit back faces over its front. Test: ADepthTestedDrawCullsTheSameFacesAsCompatibility draws each case through both renderers with DrawWithRenderer and requires identical pictures; it fails with culling off and with clockwise front faces.
sceneEngine.nativeMetalCompatibilityChanges: 2026-10-13: The native Metal backend now draws scenes it used to send to Compatibility as a whole. MetalCapability: scene lights are no longer refused (lighting is the author's shader reading g_LightsPosition and g_LightsColorPremultiplied, which WPShaderValueUpdater writes for either backend through reflection), and MetalGraphRejection no longer refuses a target read before it is written: the graph already flags it carriesPreviousFrame and MetalRender keeps one image per target name for the life of the graph; PlanCopyElision never aliases a destination read before its copy, StaticSubgraphCache calls the loop feedback, and the texture trade carries the copy's pixels. MetalRender: computeDemandReasons adds DynamicReason::Feedback when an allocated target carries the previous frame, so on-demand updating keeps the clock for it; a bound texture slot the graph left without a name (no producer, such as a layer texture whose layer draws no composite) marks the pass unproduced_input, which neither draws nor clears, as Compatibility's CustomShaderPass::textureDescriptorsReady does, instead of failing the compile (a name that does not load still fails it), with passClears() as the one answer. Tests: metal_backend_test ASceneWithLightsIsAccepted and ReadingATargetThatIsOnlyWrittenLaterIsAcceptedAsHistory; metal_scene_draw_smoke ASceneLightReachesTheAuthorsLightingUniforms, ALayerReadingThePreviousFrameSeesExactlyThePreviousFrame and AStepSamplingAnImageNothingProducesIsSkippedLikeOnCompatibility; unchanged_present_test AHistoryLoopKeepsTheClockRunningWithoutATimeUniform also runs the still card and the loop on native Metal.
sceneEngine.metalTargetSharingChanges: 2026-10-13: Native Metal render targets share images. MetalRender::Impl::shareTargetImages, run after the reuse table is compiled, gives targets of one shape whose spans of passes in the frame do not overlap one image (greedy by first use), as Compatibility's texture cache pools them; a target qualifies only if its first touch in a frame is a clear that runs (a clear step, or a draw opening with a clear that is not dropped for an unproduced input), no copy writes or reads it, and it is not carriesPreviousFrame, pinned, mip-mapped, depth-attached, an alias or the scene output. compileStaticCache records its pins and never pins an image another key shares. planPooledTrades turns the traded copies of one source into a pooled trade when every one of them is the only writer of its name, read only by later draws, not carried over and not pinned: the group owns as many images as copies are ever alive at once (simulated over the pass order) plus the source's; a copy takes a free image when it runs (traded: the copy's name takes the source's image and the source carries on in the free one, with the existing opening copy; not traded: a blit into the free one) and gives its image back at the pass after its last reader. beginPooledTrades resets the free sets and snapshots every pooled name each frame, abandonPooledTrades restores them, releasePooledTrades gives every pooled copy an image of its own again before an optimisation toggle reallocates, and a frame that ran a pooled copy is never treated as a repeat. WALLPAPER_MACHINE_METAL_TARGET_SHARING=0 (and the test-only MetalRender::SetTargetSharingForTests) turns both off. On a local scene with 42 traded screen copies the target memory went from 926 MB to 247 MB with no blit added. Test: TargetsThatAreNeverAliveTogetherShareImagesAndDrawTheSamePicture.
sceneEngine.rendererComparisonChanges: 2026-10-13: Test-only. metal_scene_draw_smoke gains WE_TEST_METAL_WARMUP_TICKS (runtime ticks before the graph is built, to put the local-project run on offscreen_scene_probe's clock) and the env-gated LocalProjectsDrawTheSamePictureOnBothRenderers (WE_TEST_COMPARE_PROJECTS, WE_TEST_COMPARE_SURFACE), which parses each local project twice and draws it through DrawWithRenderer on each renderer, printing the difference of the two posters. unchanged_present_test gains the env-gated LocalProjectEnergyIsMeasuredHeadlessly (WE_TEST_ENERGY_*): one local project on one renderer through the production SceneWallpaper at 60 FPS into an unattached layer, printing process CPU time and CPU energy, the GPU time of the process's own command buffers (a wrapper on the device's command-buffer commit counts MoltenVK's and the native backend's alike), all-coalition GPU energy, frames and footprint. Neither runs without its environment variable.
sceneEngine.simulationUniformChanges: 2026-10-14: WPShaderValueUpdater supplies the built-in uniforms Wallpaper Engine 2.8 defines that no scene shader received: g_Frametime (the frame's scene step, scene.frameTime), g_PointerPositionLast (the cursor the previous frame's shaders saw), g_PointerState (primary button held in x, y and z, 0 in w; SceneWallpaper hands the frame's held-or-pressed buttons through IShaderValueUpdater::MouseButtonsInput, the same snapshot scripts get), g_TextureReductionScale (1: textures are never loaded reduced), g_EffectModelMatrix (the effect quad's model matrix, the one g_EffectModelViewProjectionMatrix projects) and g_EffectModelViewProjectionMatrixInverse. Left at zero, the stock cursorripple and fluidsimulation effects never moved (their steps scale by g_Frametime and their push by g_PointerState.z), and blend with TRANSFORMUV divided its offset by zero. g_Frametime counts as time and the pointer pair as pointer in FrameVaryingUniforms, so static reuse never freezes them and a still scene wakes for the cursor. Semantics read from the shipped effects and the 2.8.42 binary's uniform table (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.SimulationEffectsSeeFrameTimeCursorTravelAndButtons and .EffectModelMatrixAndInverseProjectionMatchTheEffectProjection; scene_probe_controls hands probe buttons to the updater like SceneWallpaper.
sceneEngine.pointerPressHitTestChanges: 2026-10-14: A mouse press reaches scenes only when it lands on the desktop, as in Wallpaper Engine 2.8, whose render loop sets the pointer-down flag only while WindowFromPoint(cursor) is the desktop or its own wallpaper window. core/src/window.rs: MouseButtonTracker takes an injected PressHitTest, asked on the main thread once per new press (global monitor edge or sampled level), never for motion, held samples or a release; a press over another window is withheld, so scenes see neither it, its held level nor its release, while a delivered press is always released. A button the tracker first sees held after the monitors were away is adopted as a level only over the desktop; one it saw before keeps its verdict. press_lands_on_desktop asks NSWindow windowNumberAtPoint:belowWindowWithWindowNumber: at NSEvent.mouseLocation and reads that window's kCGWindowLayer from CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo; a window below layer 0 (system wallpaper, Finder's icons, desktop widgets, our wallpaper windows), no window, or a window gone before its layer was read counts as the desktop, the same rule as the app's WebWallpaperMouseRouting. engine/mod.rs builds the engine's tracker with it; MouseButtonTracker::new (every press on the desktop) is test-only. No API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.lenientEffectJsonChanges: 2026-10-14: ParseJson retries a document strict parsing rejected with commas that directly precede a closing ] or } removed outside strings, because Wallpaper Engine reads such JSON and ships it: its own effects/fluidsimulation/effect.json (and presets/water/preset.json) end arrays with a comma, and workshop packages copy the file, so every fluid simulation effect was dropped with a parse error. Valid documents parse once as before. Test: SceneSchema.EffectFilesWithTrailingCommasLoadTheirPasses.
sceneEngine.cursorReleaseTestChanges: 2026-10-14: Test-only. scenescript_sound_layer_smoke's LayerScriptDoesNotReceiveCursorUpAfterLeavingWindow had failed since ee53a324 (2026-09-21), which gives a button's release to whatever took its press wherever the cursor has gone: it pressed on the layer, so its expectation of no cursorUp after leaving the window described the rule that commit replaced, not a runtime regression (85366304 changes only core/src/window.rs, which this test does not reach). It is split into LayerScriptReceivesCursorUpForItsPressAfterLeavingWindow (the layer that took the press hears exactly one cursorUp outside the window) and LayerScriptDoesNotReceiveCursorUpForAnotherPressAfterLeavingWindow (a layer the press missed, entered and left while the button was held, hears none). Each fails under its own mutation of SceneRuntimeContext::DispatchCursorFrameEvents: ignoring who took the press fails the first, delivering an out-of-window release to every layer script fails the second. The binary joins check_renderer.py's REGRESSION_BINARIES (CPU only, fake sound streams), so it is no longer run only by hand. No runtime, API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.registeredTestBinaryChanges: 2026-10-14: Test-only. scene_schema_tests, script_runtime_compat_test, mouse_input_test, mdl_schema_tests, tex_schema_tests, media_thumbnail_texture_smoke and scenescript_media_event_smoke join check_renderer.py's REGRESSION_BINARIES (CPU only); all passed at 33a7e6aa, 3 of 3 runs each, under 1 s. To run there without hardware or a shared directory: four scene_schema_tests sound tests (DuplicateParsedImageClickScriptsGateRealAssetSoundLayers, ASoundFollowsTheSliderValueTheUserActuallyHas, ASoundWithNoBindingKeepsTheAuthorsVolume, AButtonSoundStartsSilentAndPlaysWhenAsked) construct their SoundManager with OutputBackend::Null, as the file's other parsing tests do, because WPSoundParser::Parse mounts the layer and a mount initialized the Core Audio default output device; and tex_schema_tests (TempPkg files and the host-asset, readable-picture and scene-source-mount folders) and media_thumbnail_texture_smoke (the user-texture folder) put the process id in their temporary names, as the registered video and Metal tests do; so does the already registered shader_cache_metadata_test, which now also deletes its folder when the test ends. With fixed names, 12 concurrent copies failed 10 to 12 (tex_schema_tests), 3 to 8 (media_thumbnail_texture_smoke) and 11 to 12 (shader_cache_metadata_test) times per round, and 0 after. Assertions are unchanged. No runtime, API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.corpusTestBinaryChanges: 2026-10-14: Test-only. The last test executables check_renderer.py did not run are settled. shader_preprocessor_compat_test, video_texture_submission_smoke, vulkan_render_batch_planner_smoke (plain asserts, kept in Release by -UNDEBUG), unpack_shader_compile_smoke and version_tests join REGRESSION_BINARIES (CPU only); wpdump (an inspection tool, not a test) goes into a new MANUAL_BINARIES list with the reason, and a check_renderer unit test fails on any tests/CMakeLists.txt executable that is in neither. Corpus roots are read at run time instead of being compiled in: unpack_shader_compile_smoke drops the UNPACK_SHADER_COMPILE_SMOKE_CORPUS_ROOT and _COMMON_ASSETS cache paths (another developer's home directory, so its corpus test failed on every other machine) for WALLPAPER_MACHINE_UNPACK_ROOT (default upstream/renderer/unpack) and WALLPAPER_MACHINE_ASSETS_ROOT (default the Steam install under HOME), as crates/shader/tests/pipeline.rs resolves them, and skips when the corpus is missing; its corpus sweep becomes DISABLED_ParsesCorpusAndProducesShaderSpirv, run on request, because over 60 locally unpacked scenes it took 300 to 363 s (it passed, 3 of 3). corpus.cpp's WorkshopRoot() reads WALLPAPER_MACHINE_WORKSHOP_ROOT before the build-time workshop/ folder. Without a corpus version_tests allows its uninstantiated suites and CorpusSmoke.NonEmpty skips (9 of 9 failed before). Over the app's 60-item library version_tests failed 12 of 35 on two stale test-side expectations, not renderer regressions: dump.cpp read a property-bound or scripted visible ({"value": ..., "user"/"script": ...}) as a bool and threw, which lost 49 of the 60 scene dumps, and now reads its value; CheckMdlInvariants required bones on every parsed model, but 12 MDLV0023/MDLS0001 models have none and the renderer draws such a model as a static mesh (PuppetHasBones), so it requires geometry instead, and bones only for a model with animations (true of all 116 local models). Now 35 of 35 pass in about 3 s. deep_version_tests is removed with tests/version/ (35 files), tests/fixtures/ (56 snapshots), fixture_helpers.hpp and WAYWALLEN_FIXTURE_DIR: its snapshots pinned DumpWorkshop output for 53 particular Workshop items that neither the repository nor the local library has (56 of 56 failed, none can be regenerated here), and 18 of them recorded the dumper exception above as the expected scene. shader_preprocessor_compat_test removes its per-test temporary folders when each test ends (16 were left per run) and unpack_shader_compile_smoke's scene folder carries the process id. No runtime, API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.materialPassStateChanges: 2026-10-14: A material pass reads depthtest, depthwrite and cullmode the way Wallpaper Engine 2.8 does: each is a two-value enum (disabled/enabled, normal/nocull) and a value outside the list takes the list's first entry, so only "enabled" depth-tests or writes depth and anything but "nocull" culls back faces. ApplyMaterialDepth used to read "less" and "lessorequal" as enabled and flag any other word as an unsupported depth compare, which sent the whole scene to Compatibility on Native Metal; ParseSceneCullMode read "inverted"/"front"/"clockwise" as front-face culling and other words as none. Neither alias exists in Wallpaper Engine. SceneMaterial::depth_compare_unsupported and its Native Metal refusal are gone. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary's material pass property table and pass begin/end state code (interoperability; no code copied). Test: SceneSchema.PassStateValuesOutsideWallpaperEnginesListsReadAsTheirFirstEntry.
sceneEngine.lightingV1Changes: 2026-10-14: Scene lights work as in Wallpaper Engine 2.8. SceneLight gains the light kind (lpoint, lspot, ltube, ldirectional; `point` and unknown words stay the legacy kind), exponent, cone angles and control point, with WE's defaults (exponent 2, cones 20/30 degrees, control point 2,0,0); WPLightObject is a WPMiscObjectBase and keeps the colour/intensity/radius/exponent settings. ParseLightObj registers the light's node with the runtime like a layer (visibility, origin, scale and angles bindings, scene scripts) and leaves it to the shared attach pass, so it follows its parent (it used to hang off the root with its authored values only); an intensity timeline, and user/script bindings of colour, intensity, radius and exponent, update the light. general.lightconfig becomes Scene::light_config and, when it names any light, LIGHTS_POINT/SPOT/TUBE/DIRECTIONAL combos on every material. WPShaderValueUpdater fills the LightingV1 arrays per draw from the visible lights of each kind in scene order up to the configured count: colour x intensity with radius, world position with exponent, spot cos(inner)/cos(outer) and its world x axis, tube far end = world matrix x (control point, 1), directional colour with w 1 and direction = -(world x axis); the legacy four-light packing now takes only legacy lights, visible ones, at their world position. g_NormalModelMatrix is the draw's model matrix with normalised axes (a constant identity before) and g_LightSkylightColor the scene's skylight colour. IShaderValueUpdater::LightStateHash hashes the lights a material reads, and both renderers' static pass samples fold it in, so a lit pass is not reused after a light moved or changed. Shadow maps, cookies and volumetrics are not drawn (shadow factor 1, as WE with nothing casting a shadow). Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary's light uniform builder and generator (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: SceneSchema.LightsOfEachKindFillWallpaperEnginesLightingArrays, .LightsFollowTheirUserPropertyScriptAndIntensityTimeline, .TheNormalMatrixIsTheDrawsRotationWithoutItsScale; MetalSceneDraw.ALayerLitByScenePointAndDirectionalLightsIsTheSameOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.fogChanges: 2026-10-14: Scene fog works as in Wallpaper Engine 2.8. WPSceneGeneral reads fogdistancestartdensity/enddensity and fogheightstartdensity/enddensity and takes WE's defaults (distance 1..5, height 1..-3, density 0..1, colour black; it used 0..0 and white). Scene::fog_distance/fog_height carry the switches; LoadMaterial compiles a pass once, reads its effective FOG combo (the material's or the shader annotation default), and when the scene has fog and FOG is on compiles it again with FOG_DIST, FOG_HEIGHT and FOG_COMPUTED, as WE sets them only for such passes. The global base uniforms gain g_FogDistanceColor/g_FogHeightColor and g_FogDistanceParams/g_FogHeightParams = (start, end - start, start density, end density - start density). Before, the keys were parsed and no fog was ever drawn. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary's general-settings builder and combo injection (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: SceneSchema.FogIsCompiledIntoPassesWhoseFogComboIsOnWithWallpaperEnginesParameters; shader pipeline every_asset_shader_that_requires_lighting_compiles_lit_and_fogged_on_both_backends.
sceneEngine.textureTexelChanges: 2026-10-14: Every texture slot also gets Wallpaper Engine's g_Texture<N>Texel = (1/width, 1/height, width, height) of the texture it samples, wherever g_Texture<N>Resolution is supplied: folded into the material at parse for files and known render targets (WE_GLTEX_TEXEL_NAMES), written per frame by WPShaderValueUpdater for render-target slots and by the Native Metal backend for video slots. WE's morph-target shaders (chroma4, foliage4 g_Texture5Texel), downsample_quarter and the shadow PCF read it; it was always zero. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary's per-draw uniform switch (interoperability; no code copied). Test: SceneSchema.ATextureSlotsTexelIsTheStepOfTheTextureItSamples.
sceneEngine.effectBufferChanges: 2026-10-14: Effect buffers (an effect.json's `fbos`) are made as Wallpaper Engine 2.8 makes them, and its `swap` command works. WPEffectFbo reads width, height and fit; FixedEffectFboExtent gives a buffer with any of them a fixed size (own size else the layer's, longer side shrunk to fit with the aspect kept, sizes above 4096 ignored, then divided by scale) and EffectFboFormat its format (r16f/rg1616f/rgba16161616f/32-bit floats -> RGBA16F, rgba8888/rgb888/rg88/r8 -> RGBA8, rgba_backbuffer and anything else follow the scene's HDR); both used to be the layer size and the scene format whatever was authored, so a fluid simulation's signed velocity clamped at zero. LowerEffectCommands (shared by the image-layer and text-layer effect paths) lowers `copy` as before and `swap` to copies at the command's pass position: one copy into the first buffer when the effect draws the second before reading it again (EffectReadsBeforeWriting, which also counts any copy reading it), else a three-copy exchange through a `<second>_swap` temporary. `swap` used to be logged as unknown and dropped, so WE's fluidsimulation never carried state and its never-written history buffers differed between the renderers (a local scene running it: mean difference 16.5 between Compatibility and Native Metal, 0 after). FBO `clear` colours, `conditions` and sharing of non-unique buffers are not implemented. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary's effect loader and FBO sizing (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: SceneSchema.EffectBuffersTakeWallpaperEnginesSizesFormatsAndSwaps, MetalSceneDraw.AnEffectsSwappedBuffersAccumulateAndItsFloatBuffersKeepTheirSignOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.cursorAndEffectUniformChanges: 2026-10-14: Cursor and effect uniforms follow Wallpaper Engine 2.8's per-draw switch. g_PointerState.z is 1 only on the frame the primary button went down (x and y stay the held button): WE sets it when the button is down and was not down the previous frame, so a cursor ripple or fluid gets one push per click instead of one every frame it is held (MouseButtonsInput keeps the previous frame's buttons). g_EffectTextureProjectionMatrix(Inverse) is written per effect pass as the active camera's view-projection x the layer's model x Scale(effect extent / 2), WE's layer-card projection, for intermediate and final passes alike; it was an identity constant, so cursor ripple, fluid, x-ray and depth-parallax effects mapped the cursor wrongly on any layer that does not exactly fill the canvas. Parallax eases as WE eases it: each frame the parallax point closes (1 - delay/3) * 10 * frametime of the way to the cursor clamped to the window, while g_PointerPosition/Last are the cursor itself (both used to be one cursor smoothed with delay as a time constant, so pointer effects lagged by the parallax delay and parallax moved about 7x slower than WE's at delay 2). Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary's uniform switch and parallax update (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: ShaderValueUpdaterCompat.SimulationEffectsSeeFrameTimeCursorTravelAndButtons, .EffectTextureProjectionMapsTheLayerCardOntoTheScreen, .ParallaxEasesAsWallpaperEngineWhileShadersSeeTheCursor.
sceneEngine.cameraShakeChanges: 2026-10-14: Camera shake works as in Wallpaper Engine 2.8; `general.camerashake*` were never read. WPSceneGeneral reads camerashake (bool or binding; ReadScalarSetting now reads booleans), camerashakeamplitude, camerashakespeed and camerashakeroughness with their settings; SceneRuntimeContext::RegisterCameraShake binds the four (static, user property or script) and ApplyCameraShake sets the active camera's shake offset each tick after the camera shots: t = speed^2 * runtime seconds, v = (cos t, sin 1.333t, sin t), |v| raised to roughness^3 unless that is <= 0.001 or exactly 1, times amplitude * 0.1, and in an orthographic scene times ortho height * 0.1 with z = 0. SceneCamera adds the offset to its view matrix and position (eye and centre move together); the static cache already hashes the camera's view-projection, and DescribeTimeAdvancingWork reports Animation while a scene shakes. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary's FUN_140199580 (interoperability; no code copied). Test: SceneSchema.TheSceneCameraShakesAsWallpaperEngineWhileItsPropertyIsOn.
sceneEngine.fullscreenParentChanges: 2026-10-15: A fullscreen image layer is placed by its own transform alone, whichever group it sits in. SceneNode gains IgnoresParentTransform: UpdateTrans builds its world matrix from its local one without the parent's, while EffectiveVisible still follows the hierarchy, and ParseImageObj sets it for a layer whose model says `fullscreen` (SceneRuntimeContext's CloneNodeShallow keeps it for script-created copies). Every reader of the layer's world matrix follows with no per-frame cost: SyncImageEffectFinalTransforms and SyncEffectFinalNode, which copy it onto the effect's final card (that card was drawn displaced, scaled and turned by the group, with the screen's own corner showing in the opposite one), the effect's model-view-projection and texture-projection uniforms, and cursor hit tests; WPShaderValueUpdater's parallax walk to the outermost layer of a tree stops at such a layer, so a group no longer carries it with the cursor. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's own frames: a fullscreen post-process layer under a group at (2166,1360) in 3479521040 drew an opaque pixel-exact copy of our frame's bottom-left corner over the top right (x >= 1960, y < 750) at 8 s and 15 s, where Wallpaper Engine's frames show none although the layer's last pass writes alpha 1 (a displaced card would have been opaque there too); the same render with the group hidden has no patch, and a canvas-sized card translated by the group's origin reproduces the patch's size and place exactly. With the change that scene's picture differs from before only inside the patch, where the mean difference to Wallpaper Engine's frames falls from 74 and 76 to 8 and 4 (8 s and 15 s). The 2.8.42 binary was not read for this change. Tests: CameraFraming.AFullscreenLayerCoversTheScreenWhereverItsParentSits, CameraFraming.ParallaxDoesNotCarryAFullscreenLayerWithItsParent, CameraFraming.AGroupStillDecidesWhetherAFullscreenLayerShows, MetalSceneDraw.AFullscreenLayerCoversTheScreenWhereverItsGroupSitsOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.fullscreenChildrenChanges: 2026-10-16: The layers saved below a fullscreen layer are placed from the transform the scene saved for it, and its effects reach them. SceneNode gains a child frame (SetChildFrame, CopyChildFrame, ChildTrans): UpdateTrans builds the node's own matrix as before (a fullscreen layer ignores its parent and is drawn at the canvas centre) and a second matrix, parent's ChildTrans x the saved local transform, that children compose on in place of ModelTrans; ParseImageObj gives a fullscreen node scale 1 and angles 0 and the saved origin, scale and angles as its child frame (CloneNodeShallow keeps it for script-created copies). WPShaderValueUpdater's parallax walk starts at a fullscreen layer but passes it for the layers below, taking its child frame as the root's origin. A fullscreen pass-through layer with effects and children is rendered as a composition layer (render_as_compose), so the children are drawn into its target and its effects run over them; they are drawn there through the scene camera (SceneCamera::ChildrenUseSceneCamera, set for a fullscreen compose layer and read by SceneToRenderGraph's ResolveNearestComposeTarget, which then leaves the draw's camera alone), not the layer's fixed compose camera, so zoom, camera shake and camera shots reach them as they reach the screen; the binary sets a layer-local composite camera (inverse model matrix, ortho of the layer size) only when the fullscreen flag 0x2 is clear. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's binary (the fullscreen flag 0x2 of an image object selects fixed screen matrices in its draw and picking, and no site that alters the node's model matrix was found; a pass-through layer renders its children into its composite before the effects) and 3804689861, whose picture saved at the canvas centre under a Post-processing Layer with no origin drew a quarter of itself at the top right: after the change it fills the frame. 3743578252 (fullscreen layers under animated, scaled groups) is the only other local scene with children under one; its fish now follow their groups. Tests: CameraFraming.TheChildrenOfAFullscreenLayerAreSavedAgainstItsSavedTransform, MetalSceneDraw.TheChildrenOfAFullscreenLayerAreSavedAgainstItsOwnTransformOnBothRenderers, MetalSceneDraw.TheEffectsOfAFullscreenLayerReachItsChildrenOnBothRenderers, MetalSceneDraw.TheChildrenOfAFullscreenLayerFollowTheSceneCameraOnBothRenderers, MetalSceneDraw.ParallaxMovesTheChildrenOfAFullscreenLayerWithTheirTreeOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.fullscreenParallaxChanges: 2026-10-17: Camera parallax no longer moves a fullscreen image layer. WPImageObject::FromJson never reads parallaxDepth for a fullscreen layer, so it kept the default depth 1, and the last pass of its effects (drawn through the `fullscreen` camera with the layer's own parallax data) was moved by the cursor: the copy of the screen it draws back was drawn a second time, shifted, over the scene, with the scene underneath showing along two edges. ParseImageObj now gives a fullscreen layer depth 0 with the screen-filling size, origin, scale and angles it already forces, so its own pass, its effect passes and the screen read of its first pass stand still; the layers below it keep their tree's depth from the scene file (ResolveLayerParallax). Consistent with the 2.8.42 binary's fullscreen flag 0x2 selecting fixed screen matrices for the layer's draw (see fullscreenChildrenChanges); found on 3521337568, whose film-grain post-processing layer drew a second, cursor-shifted copy of the scene, and which draws one picture after the change with the cursor in either corner. No Wallpaper Engine frame of that scene was compared. Test: MetalSceneDraw.AFullscreenLayerStaysOverTheScreenWhileParallaxMovesTheSceneOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.particleEmitterOriginChanges: 2026-10-15: LoadEmitter no longer divides an emitter's origin by the layer's world scale for a particle file without the worldspace flag, so the layer's model matrix scales it with the rest of the system, as Wallpaper Engine draws a layer-space system; a worldspace file keeps the division (origin added unscaled). Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's frames: snow emitters at local y 650 under layers scaled about 2-2.5 sit above the canvas there and fill the picture from the top edge, where the divided origin left the top 400 px empty (3379996991, 3819288707); rose petals scaled 3x spawned below the field (3257043844). Child system origins are not changed here (see childSystemOriginChanges). Test: SceneSchema.AnEmitterOriginScalesWithItsLayerUnlessTheFileIsWorldspace.
sceneEngine.childSystemOriginChanges: 2026-10-15: A child particle system's origin is no longer divided by the parent's world scale unless the parent's file is worldspace (ParseParticleObj; ParticleChildPtr::parent_worldspace), so the parent's model matrix scales it with the rest of the system and a row of static children under a scaled layer spreads out with the layer. Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42 stores a child as a 4x4 matrix (rotation and scale rows, origin as the translation row; the particle file loader FUN_1401c5490) and composes it with the parent's. A layer-space system is put on the matrix stack as its own matrix times the top, a worldspace one as its own matrix alone (FUN_140229760). A static child's own matrix is its bare local one (FUN_14022ebe0). An event child's is its local matrix times a translation to the parent particle and, only when exactly one of the two files is worldspace, times the matrix on the stack, inverted when the parent is the worldspace one (FUN_14022a360; FUN_14005f730 is a 4x4 inverse). The origin is never divided: an event child's origin is scaled with the layer exactly when its parent is layer-space, whatever its own file says, and a worldspace parent ends in world units. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's frames: a code-rain layer at scale 1.476 with 66 static children 50 units apart (3226487183) shows glyph columns out to about 81 percent of the frame width in Wallpaper Engine, where the layer origin plus the scaled offsets predicts 80.5 percent and the unscaled offsets 39 percent, and ours stopped at the left 39 percent. The worldspace-parent half and the event-child half are read from the binary only: no local reference scene has a worldspace parent with a child origin, and the one event child with an origin under a layer-space parent (3743578252) is a 32-unit offset. A static child under a layer-space parent whose own file is worldspace is not settled and keeps the previous world-unit offset: the update pass builds it from its bare local matrix while the draw pass (FUN_1402366f0, 140236b78) multiplies a child's matrix in only for a layer-space child, and how a worldspace system's spawn matrix uses either was not traced; no local scene has one. Child scale and angles, and a child file's own worldspace flag for its emitters, are unchanged. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary (interoperability; no code copied). Test: SceneSchema.AChildSystemOriginScalesWithItsLayerUnlessItsParentIsWorldspace.
sceneEngine.particleLayerScaleChanges: 2026-10-15: A particle's sprite, rope and trail sizes go out as authored in an authored 2D canvas too: ParticleSubSystem::RenderScale no longer divides them by the owner layer's scale (the inverse_x/inverse_y/isotropic_inverse fields of ParticleRenderScale are gone), so the layer's model matrix scales the billboard as Wallpaper Engine's genericparticle shader does (ComputeParticlePosition in model space, then g_ModelViewProjectionMatrix). Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's own frames: the same ember preset matched at layer scale 1 and drew at 1/scale where its layer was scaled about 2x (2294547604), and scaled bird and flare layers likewise. Tests: ParticleMouseControlpoint.RawParticleSizeIsTheAuthoredSizeWhateverTheLayerScale, ParticleMouseControlpoint.AuthoredCanvasBillboardsScaleWithTheirLayer, ParticleRopeGeometry.ThickFormatWritesEndColourAndEndHalfSize.
sceneEngine.worldspaceParticleChanges: 2026-10-15: A particle file with the `worldspace` flag is simulated and drawn in scene units, not through its layer's model matrix, as Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42 draws it. ParticleSubSystem::KeepWorldPositions gives every node that draws the system (the layer's and each mirror renderer's) a render transform that is only the layer's origin, and keeps live particles in place when the origin moves (it used to carry them through the whole matrix, turning and rescaling them with the layer). The layer's rotation and scale reach the system once, at a particle's birth: ParticleControlpoint::world_linear is the linear part of the layer matrix, ResolveEmitterFrame hands it to the box and sphere emitters, which turn and scale the spawn offset by it, add the emitter origin after (unscaled, unturned) and send the particle along the new offset's direction at its authored speed; each emitter also writes the matrix its control point carries (none for a layer-space system or a pinned control point) into the system's ParticleSpawnContext before its particles are initialized (ParticleBoxEmitterArgs::spawn), and the velocity `velocityrandom` and `turbulentvelocityrandom` draw is turned and scaled by it. Control point offsets are the layer matrix applied to the authored offset (a pinned control point and the cursor's are scene places less the origin; a pinned point's matrix carries no layer matrix, so an emitter on it is not stretched), a movement operator's gravity needs no turning, and an event follower of a worldspace parent hangs where the layer's matrix puts the parent's particle (its bound position goes through the inverse linear part). LoadEmitter no longer divides a layer's own worldspace emitter origin by the layer's scale. A system's prewarm runs once every layer sits under its parent group (ParseContext::pending_prewarms, run after AttachRemainingLayerNodes), because the matrix a worldspace particle is born by is its layer's final one; it ran while the layer was still unparented, so a layer under a scaled group was prewarmed by its own scale alone (and a pinned control point of a layer-space system, carried through the inverse of the layer's matrix, by an unfinished one). Before, a worldspace system lived in layer space and was drawn through the layer's matrix, so since ad2a3340 the size of every sprite and rope was stretched by the layer along with the paths: a rope on a layer 24 times wider than tall was folded into wide horizontal sheets that drew hard lines. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary (interoperability; no code copied): the system draw FUN_1402366f0 (wallpaper64.c 391838) replaces the model matrix on the stack with the base matrix kept at ctx+0xaf0 when the system's flag bit 0 is set (the identity except while a layer draws its own child objects, which FUN_1401ecb20 and FUN_140207b50 set and clear), where FUN_140236600 multiplies the layer's world matrix in for a layer-space system; FUN_14022bd40 (386640-386990) builds a worldspace system's control point matrices as the layer's world matrix times each point's own, except that a point pinned to the world (flag 2, never the first) keeps its own matrix and a point flagged 1 (the cursor's) is skipped, while a layer-space system's are the point's own and a pinned point's is taken through the inverse of the layer's world matrix; the emitter spawn FUN_1402378a0 (438930-439260) reads the matrix of the emitter's own control point (its index is in the emitter record, 438910-438911 for the box emitter and 439247-439249 for the sphere) and multiplies the offset by its 3x3 when the flag is set, adds the origin and the matrix translation after, and sets the velocity to the speed along the normalised transformed offset; the initializer switch FUN_14023b340 is handed that matrix (439120 and 439478) and passes its 3x3 to the velocity cases 7 and 9 (velocityrandom, turbulentvelocityrandom), which multiply their velocity by it through FUN_140184440 (case 8, the control point's own velocity, does the same after taking it back to the layer's space, so it stays in scene units here); sizes and the operators are not touched. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's own frames: the local scene 3233141951 draws a worldspace rope (vapor0) on a layer scaled 24 by 1, whose strips drew hard lines of a pixel or two in ours and a soft band 44 to 50 px thick in Wallpaper Engine's 15 s frame (a row profile, 1703 to 1747: 117 against a background of 90); after this the 175 by 170 px patch where the sheets were differs from Wallpaper Engine's frame by 0.76 at the 8 s frame and 5.3 at the 15 s one (the band itself is a random draw), from 16.9 and 11.8; the shooting stars of 3544823846 (a worldspace rope trail on a layer scaled 6.5 by -4.4) drew as wide bright bars and are now the thin streaks Wallpaper Engine's 8 s frame shows. Not covered: a worldspace system's child systems still draw through the layer's matrix times their own, as the binary draws a child that is not itself worldspace (FUN_1402366f0 restores the system's own matrix before it recurses into its children); what the base matrix is while a layer draws its own child objects was not traced, so a worldspace layer drawn there keeps the scene origin. Tests: ParticleMouseControlpoint.AWorldspaceSystemKeepsItsBillboardSizeWhateverItsLayerScale, ParticleMouseControlpoint.AWorldspaceEmitterStretchesItsSpawnsAndTheirHeadingButNotTheirSpeed, ParticleMouseControlpoint.AWorldspaceLayersMatrixScalesTheVelocityInitializersDraw, SceneSchema.AWorldspaceLayerStretchesItsSpawnsButNotTheSpeedOfItsParticles, WorldSpace.ARotatingOrScalingLayerLeavesLiveParticlesAndTheirVelocityAlone (replaces the one that expected the velocity turned back), WorldSpace.AFollowerHangsWhereItsLayersMatrixPutsAWorldspaceParentsParticle, WorldSpace.EveryRendererOfAFileIsDrawnFromItsLayersOriginAloneOrThroughItsWholeMatrix, WorldSpace.ALayerUnderAScaledGroupIsDrawnFromItsOriginAndSpreadByTheWholeChain, Movement.FlagOneGravityOfAWorldspaceSystemNeedsNoTurningByItsLayer, ParticleMouseControlpoint.AWorldspaceSystemsControlpointsAreWhereItsLayersMatrixPutsThem, ParticleMouseControlpoint.AWorldspaceEmitterOnAPinnedControlpointIsNotStretchedByItsLayer, Prewarm.AWorldspaceSystemIsPrewarmedAgainstTheMatrixItsLayerEndsUpWith, Prewarm.AStaticChildIsPrewarmedOnceItsLayerHasJoinedItsGroup, and SceneSchema.AnEmitterOriginScalesWithItsLayerUnlessTheFileIsWorldspace (now reads where the origin is drawn).
sceneEngine.particleSizeOverrideChanges: 2026-10-15: A scene object's instance `size` override scales a particle's size at its birth and again by every `sizechange` ramp of its file, as Wallpaper Engine does, and a particle file that sets the "ignore size override" flag (128 of its `flags`) keeps it out of both (ParticleParseContext::size_override, wpscene::Particle::AppliesSizeOverride; a ramp reads the override at each step, so a bound size property still moves it). A ramp multiplies the running size by `override * ramp`, so a particle under n ramps is the override to the power n + 1: the cherry petals of 3195212886 (override 1.27, two ramps) are 1.27^3 times the size they would be without it. An earlier change (apply a particle's size override once) took the override out of the ramps and drew those petals 1.27^2 too small; this restores the ramp factor and adds the flag. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary (interoperability; no code copied): the particle file loader (FUN_1401c5490, wallpaper64.c 787646) builds each `sizerandom` record (FUN_1401d8500, the minimum, the range and the exponent; test at 794559) and each `sizechange` record (FUN_1401d8a50 at 1401cb994, 797266-797340; the test is at 795881) from the file's own numbers, and beside each, unless bit 128 of the file's flags is set (the guards at 794598 and 797332), a binding record (FUN_1401d8470, type 6, at 794605 and FUN_1401d8430, type 7, at 797339) that names the record's float slots and the override property to scale them by. That property is tag 0xcc (794631, 797364), which is `size` in the override block's property table (397117-397277: alpha 0xc8, size 0xcc, count 0xd0, speed 0xd4, lifetime 0xd8, rate 0xdc, brightness 0xe0, colorn 0xe4). FUN_1401d15a0 (332500) rewrites the bound slots from the override whenever an instance is built or its override changes (FUN_14022bd40 at 386740 and FUN_14022f890 at 389533): a type 6 binding sets a `sizerandom` record's minimum to the override times it and its range to the override times the span (332651), a type 7 binding a `sizechange` record's start value and change to the override times theirs (332660). The operator's kernel (case 4 of FUN_14023fbc0, 799686-799727) then multiplies the running size, which the pass first copies from the birth size array (799342-799346), by clamp((t - start) / length, 0, 1) * change + start with the override already in start and change: the ramp scales the running size, it does not set it from the birth size. The same loader gates the speed bindings (tag 0xd4; 788606, 794745) with bit 16 and the lifetime binding (tag 0xd8; 795671) with bit 64, and other bindings with bits 8 and 32; only 16 was implemented before. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's own frames (3456x2024, the 8 s and 15 s shots): in the 260x320 px box of the cherry petals of 3195212886 (layer 160) the bluish petal pixels number 5352 and 5767 in Wallpaper Engine, 5455 and 4699 with the ramps scaled and 2122 and 1836 without (the base of this change), and the largest petals cover 1260, 1022 and 883 px in Wallpaper Engine's first shot against 1395, 1081 and 860 with the ramps scaled and 422, 360 and 300 without. The vapor of 3233141951 (layer 187, override 2.38, one ramp), which the earlier change was made for, does not tell the rules apart: the two builds' frames differ by 0.00 (8 s) and 0.20 (15 s) mean abs over the 1056x360 px strip where the rope draws, and the clean patch differs from Wallpaper Engine's by 0.50 and 5.31 either way, so that case is no evidence for taking the override out of the ramps. Not covered: the binary scales each `sizerandom` record where this multiplies the finished size once, the same for a file with one size initializer (every local preset that has an override); a file with two would be the override squared there and one with none would not be scaled. Tests: ParticleMouseControlpoint.ASizeOverrideScalesTheBirthSizeAndEverySizeRamp (replaces ASizeOverrideScalesAShrinkingParticleOnceNotTwice, which required the opposite), ParticleMouseControlpoint.EachSizeRampScalesTheRunningSizeByItsOwnValueTimesTheOverride, ParticleMouseControlpoint.AFileThatIgnoresTheSizeOverrideKeepsItOutOfTheBirthSizeAndEveryRamp, InstanceOverride.TheSizeOverrideScalesTheBirthSizeAndEachSizeRampUnlessTheFileIgnoresIt, ParseLevel.TheIgnoreSizeOverrideFlagIsTheOneHundredTwentyEightBitOfTheFilesFlags.
sceneEngine.hiddenScriptedLayerChanges: 2026-10-15: A layer the scene file hides outright is built, hidden, when it carries a script or a script spells out its name (CollectScriptReachableIds joins the layers kept for texture references), so its scripts run and a script can find and show it, as Wallpaper Engine builds every layer: a hidden controller layer's effect scripts often compute what other layers show (a day/night switch through shared). A name a script computes is not seen. Sound and light objects are not kept, since neither reads its visibility. Hidden layers stay out of the render graph until shown. Tests: MetalSceneDraw.AHiddenLayersScriptsStillRunOnBothRenderers, MetalSceneDraw.AScriptCanShowAHiddenLayerItNamesOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.textEffectsOffChanges: 2026-10-15: A text layer whose every effect is off (in the scene file, or by a property at load) is drawn as plain text: ParseTextObj decides the effect chain, the card's blend and its frame from the effects it actually builds (EffectIsBuilt), not from a non-empty effects list, as ParseImageObj does. It used to draw the card into a chain with no effect, which never reached the screen. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's frames (a weekday label and a clock whose effects were all off are visible there and were missing here). Test: MetalSceneDraw.ATextLayerWhoseEffectsAreAllOffIsDrawnAsPlainTextOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.scriptedEffectVisibilityChanges: 2026-10-15: An effect whose visible a script decides follows the script while the scene runs, as Wallpaper Engine 2.8's effect object does. WPImageEffect keeps a scripted visible setting (scripted_visible); the image and text effect chains build such an effect whatever its stored value (EffectIsBuilt) and bind it through SceneRuntimeContext::RegisterEffectVisibility, which marks the scene graph changed on a switch. SceneImageEffectLayer::ResolveEffect keeps each node's authored ping-pong placeholders and resolves the chain again over the effects that run, and sceneToRenderGraph skips the others, so a switch rebuilds the render graph at the next frame and costs nothing per frame. A chain whose every effect is scripted ends in a passthrough that runs only while no other effect does; Wallpaper Engine draws such a layer as one without effects, so that state costs one layer-sized pass more here (chosen by the user over keeping two layer set-ups). User-bound effect visibility stays load-only. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary (the effect object's visible setter flips a flag the layer's per-frame effect loop tests; its change callback recounts the visible passes and rebuilds the layer, which draws without its effect chain when none is visible) (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: MetalSceneDraw.AnEffectAScriptSwitchesIsFollowedWhileTheSceneRunsOnBothRenderers, MetalSceneDraw.ALayerWhoseEffectsAScriptHasAllSwitchedOffIsStillDrawnOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.scriptTextWriteChanges: 2026-10-15: A text script that writes `thisLayer.text` from `update()` and returns nothing keeps the string it wrote, as Wallpaper Engine shows it. ScriptedDynamicValue::reevaluate runs each update() inside a SceneRuntimeContext::OwnTextWrite, which SetNodeText fills when the script writes the layer whose text property that scripted value is (a write by any other script, or by this one to another layer, is not recorded); when update() returned nothing (PropertyScriptProgram::UpdateReturnedValue is false) the value publishes that string instead of its current value, so the next update(value) is given it and the per-tick apply of the text binding puts the same string back. Before, update() returning undefined republished the current value, still the authored placeholder, and the same tick's apply put it back over the write: a 12-hour clock text layer showed its placeholder where Wallpaper Engine shows the time. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's own frames of a 12-hour clock text layer (3819637149): at a 23:16 capture it shows 11:16 PM, the string its script writes from update(), where this renderer showed the placeholder, in both shots. Deliberately not changed, because no Wallpaper Engine frame decides it: a returned string still replaces a write; a write from a script that does not own the text property (visibility script, scene script, cursor or media handler, another layer's script, or the text script's own handlers) lasts only until the property's own value is applied on the next tick. The same widget's title layer (3819637149, text script returns the empty title, visibility script writes the sound layer's name every tick) is blank in both Wallpaper Engine shots; an earlier form of this change made every script's write the property's value and drew the sound layer's name there, so the owning script's value stays on screen. Reading the binary (FUN_1401a4db0 builds one script binding per scripted property, FUN_140175880 compiles an object's bindings into one per-object script handle) did not show the order in which an object's scripts run, and whether the sound layer was playing in the capture VM is unknown (the sound layer's isPlaying, FUN_1401f6fb0, needs a live voice), so which script Wallpaper Engine lets win when two write one text is not established (interoperability; no code copied). Cost: one pointer save and restore per scripted evaluation; a text write made during one scans the scene's text bindings by name (a handful); nothing is added per frame and no relayout happens unless the text changes. Tests: TextObjectRuntime.ScriptTextWrittenInUpdateIsKeptWhenUpdateReturnsNothing, .ScriptReadsTheTextItWroteOnTheNextUpdate, .ScriptReturnValueStillReplacesTextTheScriptWrote, .TextWrittenByAnotherScriptDoesNotReplaceWhatTheTextScriptReturns, .TextScriptWritingAnotherLayersTextKeepsItsOwnValue.
sceneEngine.colorBlendModeChanges: 2026-10-14: Colour blend modes follow Wallpaper Engine 2.8. ParseImageObj no longer appends the effectpassthrough material for colorBlendMode 31 (kAdditiveColorBlendMode): the layer is drawn with additive blending straight onto the scene, its own material when it has no effects (puppet material slots included) and the effect layer's final blend otherwise, with no screen copy. For every other non-zero mode the appended passthrough gets g_Color4 = (1,1,1,1) and is not registered for the layer's alpha or user-bound colour, since the layer's first pass already applied them; it used to apply them a second time. Semantics read from the 2.8.42 binary (the composite resets the colour state to white and forces blend 2 for mode 31; the layer draw forces blend 2 for mode 31; BLENDMODE 31 builds as 0) (interoperability; no code copied). Tests: MetalSceneDraw.AColorBlendLayersColourAndAlphaApplyOnceOnBothRenderers, MetalSceneDraw.AnAddColorBlendLayerIsAddedOntoTheSceneOnBothRenderers, RenderGraph.addColorBlendLayersAddOntoTheSceneWithoutSamplingIt; unpack_shader_compile_smoke expects no passthrough for mode 31.
sceneEngine.metalEarlySceneReadChanges: 2026-10-14: Native Metal clears the scene's own image before a pass that copies or samples it ahead of any draw into it this frame (ScenePassDescription ClearSceneBeforeAnEarlyRead inserts a scene-coloured Clear description). Compatibility's PrePass clears that image at the start of every frame; Native Metal cleared it only in its first writer, so a colour-blend layer drawn first copied an uncleared, transparent image (the previous frame after the first) and vanished. Test: MetalSceneDraw.AScreenReadBeforeAnyDrawSeesTheBackgroundEveryFrameOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.parallaxAnchorChanges: 2026-10-14: 2D camera parallax follows Wallpaper Engine 2.8. WPShaderValueUpdater adds, in a canvas scene, the outermost layer's distance from the camera position (the view centre, where the eased cursor point rests) to the cursor offset before scaling by depth and amount, so each layer tree moves by (rootOrigin - par) * amount * depth as in the binary's per-drawable parallax (FUN_14018aac0, root found through the parent chain, origin and parallaxDepth read live; par from FUN_1401891a0). The root is found by walking the drawn node's parents up to the scene graph root, from WPShaderValueData::parallax_layer for effect passes (image and text effect nodes) and from the node itself otherwise. An omitted parallaxDepth defaults to (1, 1) as the binary's object constructor sets it (WPImageObject, WPParticleObject, WPMiscObjectBase, ResolveLayerParallax). sceneEngine.sceneScriptParityChanges: 2026-10-14: SceneScript API parity with Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42, for interoperability. The behaviour comes from reading Wallpaper Engine's shipped script classes and modules (assets/scripts/jsclasses/baseclasses.js, jsmodules/wemath.js, wecolor.js, wevector.js), the names its script host registers (scenescript64.dll) and the class tables its renderer registers (wallpaper64.exe), and from the scripts of the user's own local wallpapers. The implementation is written from that behaviour: the vector and matrix classes (Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Mat3, Mat4) have the shipped classes' method set, argument forms and results, but their code is this project's own. The matrix routines (determinant by expansion along columns, the inverse as adjugate over determinant, Euler angles, axis-angle, decompose and view matrices as products of elementary turns) were derived from the mathematics with the shipped file not open, and the vector routines whose statement order and local names followed the shipped file (project, refract, toSpherical, fromSpherical, the constructor's component fill, Mat3.decompose's angle) were reshaped. What a comparison with that file still finds is no verbatim line and no shared comment, only short formulas the mathematics or Wallpaper Engine's observable behaviour fixes (normalize, perpendicular, cross, reflect, the atan2 angle conventions, the normal matrix, the steps of decompose and lookAt); WEColor's HSV conversion is the textbook one. The classes were compared with the shipped ones outside the repository with randomized inputs (about 5 million calls in the last run): no value or class differs except two leniencies kept on purpose, a Vec4 beside a Vec2 (the shipped one gives NaN for z and w, this one leaves them) and a vector built from a wider vector or a plain object (the shipped one stores the object in every component, this one takes the components). Script host (Scripting/ScriptEngine.cpp): WEMath.deg2rad and rad2deg are the factors (numbers), mix is a + (b - a) * v; WEColor gains rgb2hsv, normalizeColor and expandColor, and hsv2rgb neither clamps the saturation nor wraps the hue (a negative hue is black); WEVector gains vectorAngle2; localStorage gains delete (remove stays an alias); input.cursorScreenPosition is the window-normalized pointer times the display resolution (pixels, y from the top) and input.cursorLeftDown the primary button; Vec2, Vec3 and Vec4 are classes with the shipped method set and semantics (reflect, dot, cross, distance, lengthSqr, negate, equals, min, max, clamp, abs, sign, round, floor, ceil, fract, mod, step, smoothStep, angle, angleBetween, rotate, project, perpendicular, refract, toSpherical, fromSpherical, string constructors, toString as 'x y z'), Mat3 and Mat4 are new, and the vector classes are installed before the host fills engine and input with vectors, so those are instances from the first frame (they were bare objects until the host values first changed). The frozen __WEVec2/3/4 names the host builds vectors through are kept. thisScene gains getLayerCount (a number), getLayer(index), enumerateLayers, getLayerByID and getInitialLayerConfig (a fresh parsed copy each call); the first four answer the cached wrapper objects getLayer(name) answers, and layer.name is the name the scene file gives the layer (empty for an unnamed one) even where the layer is registered under a generated key; getLayer(index), getLayerCount, enumerateLayers, getLayerIndex and sortLayer are one order, which sortLayer changes and the draw order among siblings follows; only layers the parser instantiated are counted (an object the scene file marks statically invisible is never built, so it has no index or id). Layer wrappers gain font, pointsize (read back as the float it is), horizontalalign (left, center, right), verticalalign (top, center, bottom) and parallaxDepth (a write reaches the layer, its effect passes and the layers below it, and one that starts or stops following the cursor asks for a new render graph), and getTextureAnimation() gains play, pause, stop, isPlaying, rate (read back as written; a rate that is not a positive speed holds the sheet), fps, frameCount, duration and name. getAnimationLayerCount reports the puppet's own count. createLayer accepts a text configuration and honours size, name, parent (a parent that names no layer leaves the layer beside its creator) and parallaxDepth; destroyLayer also removes the layers a script made below the layer it removes, and the raster of a destroyed text layer is dropped once the graph that drew it is gone (RuntimeImageSource gains RemoveImage). A script's destroy(), resizeScreen(size) and applyGeneralSettings({ language }) are called (destroy once, when a script that started is torn down, which Scene's destructor does first, before any member is destroyed; applyGeneralSettings right after init and again when the language set with SetLanguage changes; resizeScreen when the display size changes). Nothing calls SetLanguage yet, so scripts are always told en-us. thisObject of a script bound to animationlayers[i] is that animation layer, the same object getAnimationLayer gives for its name or position, with the layer's authored name. Scene scripts (those that only register listeners) start last in the parse, after the layer order, ids, object list and text hooks are installed. Runtime (Runtime/SceneRuntimeContext, ScriptedDynamicValue, SceneSettingResolver): layer order, id, authored-name and object lookups for the enumeration calls (the scene's object list is kept only for a scene whose scripts read it), LayerIndex and SortLayer, SetLanguage and the resize and language notifications dispatched from Tick, TearDownScripts, scripted values that leave the registry when destroyed before the runtime, DispatchPuppetLayerEvents for addEndedCallback, text style and text layer creation hooks the parser installs (font resolution is the parser's own rule, extracted as ResolveTextLayerFont), SetNodeParent, SetNodeSize (a stretched card of the layer's own: copies of a template share its vertices) and parallax depth through the shader value updater. WPPuppetLayer records the single-shot layers that finished and names its layers; SceneNode carries the texture animation's pause, rate and last drawn frame, which WPShaderValueUpdater honours (a paused sheet advances by no time); TextLayer gains SetPointSize, SetFont and SetAlignment; IShaderValueUpdater gains SetNodeParallaxDepth (answering whether anything started or stopped following the cursor) and NodeParallaxDepth.
