sceneEngine.particleParityChanges: 2026-10-14: Particle systems follow Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42, for interoperability; the behaviour comes from reading the decompiled renderer (the particle definition loader FUN_1401c5490 and its per-type default fillers, the emission step FUN_1402378a0, the initializer step FUN_14023b340, the operator step FUN_14023fbc0, the per-frame driver FUN_140236cd0, the prewarm of FUN_14022ebe0/FUN_14022f430, the instance override application FUN_1401d15a0, the control point build FUN_14022e3e0/FUN_14022bd40, the renderer records FUN_1401d2340/FUN_1401c22e0, the audio level FUN_14022a8a0 and the blend window FUN_14022a530) and WE's shipped particle shaders and presets; no code, shader text or script is copied. A particle gets one random seed at spawn (Particle::seed, also the randomframe value, replacing a hash of the spawn state). Emitters: ParticleEmitter.cpp samples sphererandom as a unit-ball point stretched by directions with the distance taken from the stretched length (cone narrows it about +x, a particle on the centre leaves along a random direction) and boxrandom as a signed per-axis fold of distancemin..distancemax; EmitterClock runs delay, duration, periodic windows (flags 4, the four *periodic* keys, maxtoemitperperiod), flags 2 as at most one a frame at the rate, and pays an instantaneous burst out of the rate accumulator; every ParticleInstance holds its own copies of the emitters and initializers so a recycled instance restarts its schedule. ParticleSubSystem::Advance/AdvanceInstance split the step from mesh building; Prewarm (start time as a float, 0.05 s steps or 0.2 s from 500 particles, at most 6000 steps with the rest added to the system clock) and PrewarmInstance (event children) run it before the first frame; an eventfollow instance keeps its particles after its bound particle ends and stops following; a worldspace file keeps live particles in place when the layer matrix changes; extra renderer entries become mirror subsystems that draw the same instances through their own mesh, material and node. Initializers (WPParticleParser.cpp): the exponent of every random draw, the 0.001 lifetime floor, pixel/scene-unit defaults chosen by WPSceneGeneral::pixelCanvas, hsvcolorrandom (hue step = range / (steps - 1), plus one when the range is a whole number of turns within 1/360, a range of no width taken as one turn, one step or none keeps the start hue; the executor's index runs 0..steps), colorlist (a uniform draw over value plus and minus the noise with both ends kept inside 0..1, the instance shift added after the draw, hue wrapped by floor and saturation and value clamped), inheritcontrolpointvelocity, positionoffsetrandom (Perlin noise stands for WE's unidentified noise), mapsequencearoundcontrolpoint, mapsequencebetweencontrolpoints, inheritinitialvaluefromevent, and the instance colour override as an HSV re-tint of the colour sources (analyzeColorSources finds the preset's representative colour). Operators: movement/angularmovement integrate position and rotation in operator order with v*(1-min(drag*dt,0.9999999)) and nothing else advances a particle (the step ends after the operator pass: FUN_140236cd0 only copies the control point matrices, so a file without them keeps its particles still); a movement operator with flags 1 takes gravity through the layer's 3x3 transposed without normalising it (FUN_1400dd7d0, FUN_1401f87e0); controlpointattract falls off linearly, with flag 2 clamp, no operator origin, and flag 1 testing the segment from the position the movement operator found the particle at (it copies the positions first when the system asks for it, FUN_14022a150) to its current one against deletethreshold; the oscillators use the particle seed, the difference of two sines and the blend window; turbulence uses per-particle phase and speed, mask weights, the blend window and the audio level; vortex measures from control point plus offset with flags 1 and the audio level; capvelocity, reducemovementnearcontrolpoint, maintaindistancetocontrolpoint, maintaindistancebetweencontrolpoints, collisionplane and collisionsphere are new (the collision kernels FUN_14024f5e0/FUN_14024f620 mask only on the particle being behind the plane or inside the sphere and always add the normal speed times -(1+bouncefactor), or -1 for a slide, along the normal, so no sign test on the velocity; the sphere's default origin is 0 -200 0 in a pixel scene, FUN_1401c0740; with flags 1 the executor overwrites the sphere's centre with the control point translation and the plane's normal with the control point matrix applied to it and its offset with the new normal dotted with the translation, so origin and distance are not read); the colorchange start value defaults to one; control point indices above six name the seventh index. Renderer records: rope subdivision N draws N+1 pieces per pair, rope trails record `segments` points and subdivide between them, defaults and clamps per renderer, plain rope in the thick layout, and the 2D eye position's z is 2000. Instance override control points and angles (instanceoverride.controlpointN/controlpointangleN) and HDR brightness are read and, as user properties, followed while the scene runs. The override's speed (the loader binds property offset 0xd4 into the emitters' and velocity initializers' speed pairs, movement gravity, angularmovement force, vortex speeds, turbulence speed pair, the controlpointattract scale and the oscillateposition frequency pair, FUN_1401d15a0 cases 5 to 9, each skipped when the particle file's flags & 16) scales those records, and the file flag 16 keeps it out of them. An explicitly empty renderer array draws nothing (the loader appends the default sprite renderer only when the key is not an array: FUN_1401c5490), so the system is simulated without a mesh. A scene without an orthogonalprojection key keeps drawing as the default canvas here, and its particle defaults follow that (WE's scene constructor starts without an orthogonal projection: flags 0x26, bit 3 clear, a difference noted in docs/testing/renderer.md). Not implemented and documented in docs/testing/renderer.md: vortex_v2, boids, remapvalue, remapinitialvalue, layerimage, renderer orientation/fade keys, the geometry-shader rope path, control point chaining. Tests: tests/particle_parity_test.cpp (new, in scripts/check_renderer.py; scene-level cases drive the real scene parser with a probe shader whose reflection shows which combos reached it), particle_mouse_controlpoint_test (attract, movement, audio-band and frame-value cases updated), particle_rope_geometry_test (its subsystem fixtures gain a movement operator), metal_scene_draw_smoke (the 32-bit rope trail fixture names its segments and subdivision).
sceneEngine.textLayoutParityChanges: 2026-10-14: Text layout follows Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42, for interoperability; the behaviour is read from the binary's text layout and style functions (FUN_1401b0410 layout, FUN_140256f20 style and card fill, FUN_140258900 card size, FUN_1401a3fc0 Vec2 properties, FUN_1401acaf0 face sizing) and written independently, no code copied. (1) Sizing: the face is requested with FT_Set_Char_Size at 300 dpi from the point size clamped to 1..256 (4.17 px per point, FreeType rounding the em where the font asks), replacing a 4.0 px per point integer pixel size; the fallback boxes and EstimateTextLayerSize use the same pixels. (2) `padding` and `spacing` are Vec2 properties (number = both lanes, "x y" string, lone "x" = (x, 0), object `value`; a JSON array is not a form FUN_1401a3fc0 reads); `padding` defaults to 32 on both axes and each lane is capped at 512 from above only, with no floor (FUN_140258900 tests only the upper bound), so a negative padding takes the card in. The margin applies only to a layer with a visible effect pass, a colour blend other than none and add (31), an LED source or an opaque background, or in a scene that enables distance fog or height fog (ResolveTextCardPadding, from the flag test in FUN_140258900 and FUN_1401e6f50, which also tests bits 0x800000 and 0x1000000 of the renderer's scene state; FUN_140186440 sets those from the `general` booleans `fogdistance`, setter FUN_14019bb40, and `fogheight`, setter FUN_14019bd70, so a scene with either pads every text layer; the composite flag it also sets and the FOG_COMPUTED combo change nothing a text layer draws here); it used to be one scalar read with json.get<uint32_t>(), which a string never parsed, applied to every layer. The wrap width is `maxwidth` as authored, with no allowance for padding (FUN_140256f20 hands the raw value to the layout), and the card is no longer capped at `maxwidth`. (3) `spacing` x is added to every glyph's advance, y to the line pitch, which is the face's line height (no clamp at 1); a row is the extent of its glyph ink and of the pen at each glyph start, always including the row origin, instead of the last advance, and the block is the first row's ascender line (or the tallest ink) down to `rows * pitch` below it (FUN_1401b0410 extents), so a face's line gap is part of the card, as the saved sizes of real text objects show. Text is cut into paragraphs at line breaks before it is laid out, and a break with nothing after it makes no paragraph (the segment loop of FUN_1401b0410): "ab\n" is one row. A row wraps before a non-space glyph whose ink would end past the limit, once it holds a glyph. Where `maxrows` allows another row (none set, or fewer finished rows than `maxrows` less one), the wrap is at the last space, tab or carriage return before the glyph, found by index in the paragraph's text: the row keeps everything before that character (a second space before it stays), the next row starts at the glyph and has its leading white space dropped, and a row with no such character is cut at the glyph. On the last row `maxrows` allows there is no such search: with the ellipsis flag the text is cut to the characters before the glyph and then one character at a time until it, followed by U+2026, fits inside the limit (the trailing white space is measured, then removed before the marker; a paragraph ending where more follows has white space removed and U+2026 appended, FUN_1401b0360, before it is laid out); without the flag the row keeps every glyph placed before the glyph. An empty text is a 2 by 2 card. (4) `blockalign` is read: a row that ended at a word wrap with a row after it is stretched to exactly `maxwidth` by adding the slack over its spaces and tabs to their advances (FUN_1401b0410 justification); the last row of a paragraph, a row a line break or the row limit ended, and a row with no space are left alone. (5) Pen advances are the glyph's unhinted advance (FT_Get_Advance with FT_LOAD_NO_HINTING, 16.16 to 26.6) plus the font's `kern` table kerning against the next glyph of the same face (FT_Get_Kerning, unfitted), cut to whole pixels and then given `spacing` x, as the shaper's advances are read (`>> 6` of the 26.6 positions in FUN_1401b0410); it used the hinted advance of the rendered glyph. Five cards of text in Arial that real scenes saved are reproduced exactly. (6) The defaults of a text object that leaves keys out are Wallpaper Engine's: 32 points, `maxwidth` 500, `maxrows` 1 (constructor FUN_140256ae0). TextLayerState carries the effective padding, `spacing` and `block_align`, all in the cache identity. (7) Not followed: FUN_140258900 sets the object's size from the layout box plus twice the padding every time the text is laid out and never reads the scene's authored `size` (the byte FUN_1401e6f50 sets while the object is built only keeps it from running early); here the authored `size` stays the layout box a layer is aligned in and the smallest the raster is, so text that gets shorter keeps a stale card. Tests: TextObjectRuntime.PointSizeIsRequestedFromTheFontAt300Dpi, .PointSizeIsClampedToTheRangeWallpaperEngineAccepts, .EmptyTextIsATwoByTwoCardPlusPadding, .ANegativePaddingTakesTheCardInAndOnlyTheTopIsCapped, .ASceneWithFogPadsEveryTextLayerWhateverItsEffects, .TheLastRowTheLimitAllowsIsCutAtTheGlyphThatDidNotFit, .AnEllipsisReplacesTheEndOfTheLastRowAtTheGlyphThatDidNotFit, .ALineBreakWithNothingAfterItAddsNoRowAndNoEllipsis, .ARowThatWrapsAtADoubleSpaceKeepsAllButOneOfTheSpaces, .CardPaddingSizesTheCardAndNeverNarrowsTheWrap, .CardPaddingInsetsAlignedTextOnEachAxis, .PaddingAndSpacingReadTheFormsWallpaperEngineReads, .CardPaddingAppliesOnlyToLayersWallpaperEnginePads, .SpacingAddsToEveryAdvanceAndToTheLinePitch, .SpacingMovesTheRowsOfRasterisedText, .BlockAlignJustifiesOnlyRowsThatEndedAtAWordWrap, .BlockAlignNeedsAWidthLimitAndALineThatWraps, .SpacingAndBlockAlignReachTheLayerState, .TextMeasuresToTheCardsWallpaperEngineSaved, .PenAdvancesAreUnhintedWholePixelsKernedWithTheNextGlyph.
sceneEngine.textColorBlendModeChanges: 2026-10-14: A text layer's colorBlendMode is applied as an image layer's is (it was parsed and never read). Wallpaper Engine's text object shares the image object's composite setup (FUN_1401e6f50 sets the composite flag for a mode other than 0 and 31; the text override FUN_140257840 rebuilds the layer material as the effectpassthrough material with BLENDMODE = the mode, 0 for 31, as FUN_1401ebbc0 does for images), for interoperability; no code copied. ParseTextObj appends the same passthrough effect (MakeColorBlendEffect, shared with ParseImageObj) as the layer's last effect, binds it a white g_Color4 through AttachEffectsToNode's new screen_blend_effect parameter, because the text card's first pass has already applied the layer's colour and alpha, and for mode 31 draws the text card, or the effect chain's final pass, with additive blending straight onto the scene. A text layer whose only effect is that passthrough keeps its ping-pong buffers at the card's size (ResolveTextEffectCapacity's author_effects), not the room an authored effect over text gets, so blend-only text costs two card-sized targets. sceneEngine.textScreenAnchorChanges: 2026-10-14: A text layer's `anchor` is Wallpaper Engine's screen anchor, not a local pivot, for interoperability; no code copied. The text class's vtable slot at +0xa8 (FUN_1402585c0) adds an offset to the parent matrix before the layer's own transform, from the renderer's visible-area margins left, top, right and bottom (FUN_140183a70, which also builds the orthographic projection from them): centre ((L-R)/2, (B-T)/2), top ((L-R)/2, -T), bottom ((L-R)/2, B), left (L, (B-T)/2), right (-R, (B-T)/2) and the four corners (+-L or -R by -T or +B), zero for none; the margins are positive where the canvas is cropped, negative where the display shows more, and zero in a scene without an orthogonal canvas or one shown whole. TextAnchorForObject no longer returns the `anchor` key as a placement string (it placed the layer's own box when `horizontalalign` and `verticalalign` were absent, and was dropped when present). SceneRuntimeContext::SetNodeScreenAnchor keeps the anchor in the node's alignment binding; UpdatePresentedMargins, run by SetCursorViewport, derives the margins from the published window rectangle (L = origin.x, B = origin.y, R = canvas width - (origin.x + size.x), T = canvas height - (origin.y + size.y)) and moves the pinned layers; the shift was in the parent's space (superseded by textPlacementChanges: it is a world-space draw offset now). TextScreenAnchor, PresentedMargins, ParseTextScreenAnchor and TextScreenAnchorOffset are in Text/TextLayer. Whether Wallpaper Engine's children inherit the shift was not established here; textPlacementChanges settles it from the decompile (they do not). Tests: TextObjectRuntime.ScreenAnchorOffsetsPinTheLayerToTheEdgeItNames, .ScreenAnchoredTextFollowsThePresentedAreaAndNothingElseDoes.
sceneEngine.textStyleChanges: 2026-10-14: Text `outline`, `blur` and `dropshadow` are drawn, for interoperability; the behaviour is read from the binary (FUN_140256f20 and FUN_1401b0410 choose the distance-field path from the style flags, FUN_1401ae080 builds glyphs at 32 px to the em with a 12 px margin each side, FUN_1401b3b60 turns the sizes into g_RenderVar0..3 with k = 32 / pointsize * 0.24 and caps them) and from the shipped font shader's formulae (assets/shaders/font.frag), and written independently, no code copied. 0.24 * ppem / pointsize is one, so every size, offset and radius is pixels of the finished text; the caps (outline 5.1, blur and shadow 6, offsets 6, outline + blur at most 5.1) stay in atlas units and so grow with the text; an outline is at least 1 px, blur and shadow sizes at least 0.01; the glyph's edges soften over half a pixel when a shadow is on, over max(blur, 0.5) atlas pixels when blur is, and the shadow samples the glyph shifted by the offset, widened by the outline. Instead of an atlas, the CPU rasteriser leaves three coverage masks in the texture's channels, computed from a signed distance field of the glyph coverage (a squared distance transform over the ink's bounding box plus the style's reach): red the glyph, green the glyph with its outline, blue the shadow with its opacity; a styled layer uses a second text program that mixes them with the layer's colour for the glyph only and its own colours for outline and shadow, as the font shader's ApplyOutline and ApplyDropShadow do: `text_styled_outline` for a layer with an outline, which mixes the outline colour into the glyph by its coverage, and `text_styled` for blur or shadow alone, whose glyph is the layer's colour whatever its coverage, as the shader's path without OUTLINE_ENABLED returns it (an outline colour the layer never asked for would otherwise darken every partly covered pixel). The outline and shadow colours are uniforms and follow a property or script bound to them live; the switches, sizes and opacity are baked into the card's pixels, so a property bound to one is read once as the scene loads, with the user's value, and noted load-only (ResolveLoadTimeTextStyle). TextStyle in TextLayerState carries the keys with Wallpaper Engine's defaults (outline thickness 4, blur 6, shadow size 6, opacity 1, offset 4 4); TextStyleMargin is the room the style reaches, which the raster and the card (TextLayerRenderBoundsForRasterSize) grow by on every side, the layout size unchanged. `msdf` alone is read and changes nothing. Cost: the distance field is built when a styled text is rasterised, in the layout worker, over the ink box plus the reach, never per frame; unstyled text takes the old path unchanged. Tests: TextObjectRuntime.OutlineGrowsTheGlyphByItsThicknessInPixels, .OutlineThicknessIsCappedWithTheGlyphAtlasAndNeverBelowOnePixel, .BlurSoftensEdgesOverItsSizeAndKeepsTheGlyphWhereItIs, .DropShadowFollowsItsOffsetAndOpacityAndOutlineWidth, .StyledTextCardGrowsOutwardAndKeepsTheLayoutBoxWhereItWas, .ParserReadsTheFontShaderStyleAndPicksTheStyledShader, .StyledTextCardCoversTheStyleWhenTheLayerIsParsed, .StyleColoursFollowTheirPropertiesAndTheBakedKeysAreReadOnceAndHeld, MetalSceneDraw.StyledTextIsDrawnWithItsOutlineAndShadowByTheNativeBackend, MetalSceneDraw.StyledTextWithoutAnOutlineKeepsTheLayersColourAtItsEdgesOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.layerRenderTargetSamplerChanges: 2026-10-14: An image layer's own render targets are sampled as Wallpaper Engine samples them, for interoperability; no code copied. FUN_1401ea500 (the layer's render-target allocation) is the only reader of the layer's `nointerpolation` and `clampuvs` bits: the ping-pong pair its effects run through and the composite another layer reads are created point-sampled when the layer asks or the texture header of its primary texture does (the virtual FUN_1402091e0), and wrapped instead of clamped when `clampuvs` is off, through the sampler states FUN_140099980 builds; per-effect buffers keep clamp and linear. WPImageObject reads `nointerpolation`; ParseImageObj gives the ping-pong target LayerRenderTargetSample (copied to its second buffer) and RegisterImageComposite the layer's filter; the filter is taken from the primary texture's header read from its file, so it does not depend on which layer was parsed first (the composite of a layer another layer reads is registered before the layer's own material is loaded). FUN_140099980 builds the sampler from a flags word whose bit 0 selects the all-point filter (min, mag and mip, filter 0 of the sampler description) and bit 1 clamping, and the flags of a file texture are the ones of its `.tex` header (the texture object's flags field at +0x1c, tested for the header's video bit in the same function, is the argument): a texture whose header says `noInterpolation` is sampled with its mip level picked by point too. TextureSample::mipFilter carries that (set by WPTexImageParser from the header flag, linear for every other sample, including render targets, which have one level, and the default-constructed fallbacks); the Metal sampler (MTLSamplerMipFilterNearest) and the Vulkan sampler (VK_SAMPLER_MIPMAP_MODE_NEAREST, in the sampler cache's hash) honour it. The trilinear versus 8x anisotropic split for file textures and the comparison sampler of the shadow atlas are not implemented. Tests: LayerTextureReference.LayerTargetsFollowNointerpolationClampuvsAndTheTextureHeader, .ACompositeFollowsItsLayersTextureHeaderWhateverIsParsedFirst, MetalSceneDraw.AnImageLayersTargetsArePointSampledWhenItAsksOnBothRenderers (a 16 by 12 target shown 16 times larger on both renderers), MetalSceneDraw.ATexturePointSampledByItsHeaderPicksItsMipLevelByPointOnBothRenderers (a mip chain minified, point mip with the flag, blended without it, on both renderers).
sceneEngine.cursorTargetingChanges: 2026-10-14: The cursor reaches layers as Wallpaper Engine's per-frame walk does (FUN_140189e10; the properties come from the base registry FUN_1401e0530), for interoperability; no code copied. Only objects with `solid` (default true) of kind image, text or model are hit-tested, by their quad; a visible hit object with `disablepropagation` (default false) ends the walk, so layers behind it are never visited that frame. The objects read `solid` and `disablepropagation` (image, text and model; text's `solid` default was false and is now true); SceneRuntimeContext::SetNodeCursorTarget records, per layer, whether it is a hit-tested kind (groups, particles, lights and cameras are not), solid and blocking, and is rolled back with the layer's other registrations. VisitCursorLayer returns Outside, Inside or Skipped (a layer a visible blocker in front of it covers); DispatchCursorFrameEvents lets a skipped layer keep its state and hear no enter, leave or move, and a press reaches only inside layers. The layer order is SceneRuntimeContext's. The frontmost visible blocker under the cursor is found once for a frame's cursor events (FrontmostCursorBlocker, a walk from the front that hit-tests blockers only) and a layer is skipped when its rank in the order, looked up in a map rebuilt when the order changes and without making a string, is below it; the result is dropped again whenever a cursor callback has run. The cost has not been measured on a scene with many scripted layers. The capture rule (no stopping while a button is held), click on release and the coverage mask are unchanged or not modelled. Tests: MouseInput.OnlySolidImageTextAndModelLayersAreHitTested, .ALayerThatDisablesPropagationHidesTheLayersBehindItFromTheCursor, .OnlyAVisibleBlockerInFrontStopsTheWalk, .ALayerBehindABlockerHearsNeitherTheDownNorTheClickOfAPress, .TheBlockerInFrontFollowsTheLayerOrderAndAFrameInProgress, .ARolledBackRegistrationRestoresTheCursorTargetOfTheLayerItReplaced, TextObjectRuntime.ATextLayerRegistersItsSolidAndPropagationFlagsForTheCursor, SceneSchema.ParserRegistersWhatTheCursorMakesOfAModelLayer, LayerTextureReference.ImageLayersAndGroupsRegisterTheirCursorTargeting, .LightsCamerasParticlesAndGroupsAreNeverHitTestedForTheCursor.
sceneEngine.layerModelFlagChanges: 2026-10-14: The model flags of the layer utilities are read, for interoperability; no code copied. FUN_1401fac50 reads `fullscreen`, `nopadding`, `autosize`, `passthrough`, `solidlayer`, `projectlayer` and `instanced` from a layer's model JSON, and has no test of the composition layer's path: composition comes from the passthrough flag and the shader. WPImageObject reads `autosize`, `projectlayer` and `solidlayer`; ParseImageObj composes a layer whose model is `models/util/composelayer.json` or its depth-testing variant (IsComposeLayerModel; it was the first only), and sizes a layer with both `autosize` and `projectlayer` by the scene's canvas, as the layer-size resolver FUN_140209360 does, keeping the scene file's origin. `projectlayer` and `solidlayer` models still take the passthrough path, not the compose one, and `autosize` alone still takes the saved size (a texture's own size is not known to the parser). Tests: LayerTextureReference.TheDepthTestedComposeModelComposesLikeTheOthers, .AProjectLayerTakesTheCanvasSizeAndKeepsItsOrigin.
sceneEngine.shapeObjectChanges: 2026-10-14: `shape` objects are drawn, for interoperability; no code copied. Wallpaper Engine builds an object whose `shape` key is a string, and which has no other kind's key, on the image object base (the factory FUN_14018ff60), sizes it by the canvas height on both axes (FUN_14025fac0), forces `combos.DIRECTDRAW = 1` in every pass of its effects while they load (FUN_14025ff50, a slot only shape fills), builds a 4-vertex quad from `point0` to `point3` of the first effect's first pass when all four are there (FUN_140260190: position (S*p.x - S/2, S*(1-p.y) - S/2), texture coordinate p) and the whole square otherwise, and draws the last effect of the list, every pass, straight onto the scene (FUN_14025faf0 through FUN_1401ebf60) with the effect's final pass forced additive for the draw (the shape vtable's blend hook, which writes blend mode 2). ParseLayerNodes already makes such an object a group node with its transform, parent chain, visibility and scripts; ParseShapeObj (WPShapeObject read as an image layer's `effects` are) gives that node a mesh (GenShapeMesh) and the last visible effect's material with DIRECTDRAW forced, as BlendMode::Additive, registering its constants, user bindings and node data as an effect pass's. An effect of more than one pass is not drawn (its earlier passes would draw into buffers, which a mesh drawn onto the scene cannot). Tests: LayerTextureReference.AShapeDrawsItsLastEffectAdditivelyOntoTheScene, MetalSceneDraw.AShapeIsAddedOntoTheSceneOnBothRenderers (identical pictures on both renderers).
sceneEngine.comparisonInputChanges: 2026-10-15: Test-only. metal_scene_draw_smoke's renderer comparison feeds WE_TEST_INPUT_JSON's synthetic pointer events through the renderer's cursor mapping as the host does (DrawWithRenderer takes an optional SceneProbeControls; the other callers pass none), so a script's input.cursorWorldPosition sees the pointer a reference capture had; WE_TEST_COMPARE_REALTIME paces its frames in real time so wall-clock script time (Date.now()) passes with the scene's. No runtime, API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.nativeOnlyComparisonChanges: 2026-10-15: Test-only. metal_scene_draw_smoke's renderer comparison draws and writes only the Native Metal picture, and compares nothing, when WE_TEST_COMPARE_NATIVE_ONLY is set; its printed mean difference and off-pixel share are otherwise unchanged. No runtime, API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.textStraightAlphaFringeChanges: 2026-10-15: A plain text layer's card texture holds the text's colour in every texel, the clear ones included, with the glyph coverage as the alpha (RasterizeTextLayer in Text/TextLayer.cpp fills the colour first; the styled path's coverage masks are untouched). The glyphs go onto the scene as straight alpha and the texture is sampled with linear filtering, so a layer scaled up past its raster (a small pixel font drawn about three pixels to the texel) reads edges between a glyph texel and a clear one; the clear texels were (0,0,0,0), so the sampled colour fell toward black as the alpha did and the blend then multiplied it by that alpha again, a dark ring round every stroke that drawing the scene at the display's resolution made deeper (the card is magnified once, at the display's size, where before it was drawn at the canvas's and stretched). Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's frames of a pixel-font scene (3195212886, 3456x2024 shot): along a row across a stroke edge Wallpaper Engine reads 179 192 199 (the background, a mid value, the glyph) with no dip, and the darkest pixel of each text window is 158 to 160 against 121 to 126 before; Wallpaper Engine's glyph pass writes the layer colour with the coverage as alpha (the shipped font shader, shaders/font.frag, ends in vec4(g_Color4.rgb, coverage * g_Color4.a) on its distance-field path without an outline and on its plain path, over the font material's translucent blend), so no texel's colour there depends on its coverage. The fringe energy sum(max(0, 158 - R)) of the Fri, eren and clock windows was 38733, 30637 and 30230 and is 0, 0 and 0 with the change (Wallpaper Engine 0), the darkest pixels 158, 160 and 161, and the picture changes only in the text windows; black text is unchanged (probetext4 draws the same picture byte for byte, so the alpha-cubed through-effect stem coverages stay), and the effect chain's composite card, which draws the texture over the scene it seeds from at about its own size, was never dark. Wherever else the card's texture is sampled between texels or written without blending (an effect chain whose buffer differs from the raster, the direct draw while every effect is off), a coloured text's clear texels now hold its colour too, at alpha 0, and every blend there weighs the card by its alpha; no test covers those two paths. A text with a colour blend is the exception that mattered: its card is written without blending and the shipped passthrough (genericimage3 with common_blending.h in SceneAssets) takes Darker Color (5) and Lighter Color (10) as min and max of the screen and the card's colour with no alpha, so the colour in the clear texels reached the screen as a solid box over the card (a flat box of the text's colour in mode 10, a dark one in mode 5, reproduced with the shipped shader: 40592 pixels changed against 5029 for the text). Inferring (not checked against its frames) that Wallpaper Engine draws a text through its effects, the colour blend's passthrough among them, from a composite seeded with the scene, so its clear area is the screen, BuildTextSceneShader (WPSceneParser.cpp) therefore writes, for those two modes only, mix(white or black, colour, alpha) as the card's colour, the colour that min or max passes the screen by (mode 10 is drawn as it was before this change at full layer alpha, and the layer's alpha now weighs it as the reference's glyph pass writes it; mode 5 loses the black box the old clear texels drew), and the other modes, which mix by alpha, are untouched. At a layer alpha of 1 its stems match a seeded composite's; below 1 Darker Color text fades out faster than one would (orange at 0.5 over navy leaves the scene unchanged) and Lighter Color text is slightly darker. A rasterisation-time fill, so no frame, memory or energy cost. Tests: MetalSceneDraw.ATextLayersColourBlendModesDrawItsTextAndNoBoxOnBothRenderers, MetalSceneDraw.ATextLayersColourBlendModesDrawItsTextAndNoBoxThroughTheShippedPassthrough, TextObjectRuntime.EveryTexelOfRasterizedTextCarriesTheTextsColourWhateverItsCoverage, TextObjectRuntime.StyledTextLeavesEveryTexelOutsideItsMasksClear, MetalSceneDraw.AMagnifiedTextsEdgesFadeToItsColourNotToBlackOnBothRenderers. No API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.placeholderPictureColorChanges: 2026-10-17: A picture a `scenetexture` property puts in a solid placeholder layer's slot is drawn as it is, not tinted by the layer's colour. A solid instance layer (an `instance` block over a `solidlayer` model whose material ships `util/white`) paints that placeholder in its `color`, often bound to the scheme colour; WPImageObject already dropped the colour, and a binding of it, for a cover slot the runtime supplies, but left a slot that names a project property tinted because the property table is not readable there. WPImageObject now keeps the instance's `usertextures` (instance_usertextures), and ParseImageObj resolves them against the properties the scene loads with through ApplySystemUserTextures, exactly as the material will: when a picture actually takes a slot (a preset's own `files/...` picture or the user's readable file) the colour becomes white and its `color` binding is dropped, so a later scheme colour does not reach it either; unset, or a file that cannot be opened, keeps the placeholder and its colour. The slot is load-only, so a running scene holds the decision until it reloads. Parse-time only, no per-frame cost. Established against the Workshop preview Wallpaper Engine rendered for a preset (issue #53): its 3440x1440 picture fills the background at full strength, where ours multiplied it by a 0.031 scheme colour and drew the wallpaper black. Tests: PlaceholderPicture.APictureChosenForAPlaceholderIsNotTintedByItsColour, PlaceholderPicture.WithNoPictureChosenThePlaceholderKeepsItsColour.
sceneEngine.passthroughCardGroupChanges: 2026-10-17: A pass-through layer drawn through effects copies the part of the screen it is drawn over, under its groups. Its card mesh (PassthroughCardVertices, or PassthroughClipSpaceVertices for the `passthrough` material) bakes that region from a transform, and ParseImageObj built it from the layer's local transform while the layer was not yet under its parent; a project layer (a "Full Composition Layer") saved with no origin in a group at the canvas centre therefore copied the screen half a canvas off and showed a half-sized copy of the whole scene in one quadrant, on both renderers. ParseImageObj now records each such card (ParseContext::passthrough_cards) and LayOutPassthroughCards lays it out again from the node's world matrix once AttachRemainingLayerNodes and RegisterLayerAttachments have put every layer under its parent, beside SyncImageEffectFinalTransforms, which already placed the layer's final card there. A layer outside any group is unchanged, a fullscreen layer keeps ignoring its parent, and a layer created later by a script keeps its own transform as before. Parse-time only, no per-frame cost. Established on issue #53's preset and its base (3088099655), whose CRT layer is a project layer under a centred group: both drew the quadrant copy before and the full picture after, matching the Workshop preview Wallpaper Engine rendered, with Native Metal and Compatibility pixel-identical. A transform a script or property changes after load (here a zoom slider on the group) is followed since passthroughCardLiveGroupChanges. Test: MetalSceneDraw.APassThroughLayerInAGroupReadsTheScreenWhereItIsDrawnOnBothRenderers.
sceneEngine.passthroughCardLiveGroupChanges: 2026-10-17: A pass-through layer drawn through effects copies the screen where it is drawn also after a group above it moves while the scene runs (a user property on the group's scale changed through live property edits, a script, a timeline). The card was laid out once at parse (passthroughCardGroupChanges), so it went on copying the region the layer had covered at load while the final card, which SyncEffectFinalNode places from the layer's world matrix every tick, drew it somewhere else, until the scene was loaded again. The card's layout moved into Scene/Parse/PassthroughCard.hpp (PassthroughCardVertices and PassthroughClipSpaceVertices unchanged; PassthroughCard keeps the size, the clip-space flag, the canvas and the transform it was last laid out from). ParseImageObj builds the card's mesh as MeshUpdate::OnEvent and hands the card to RegisterNodeEffectFinal; SyncEffectFinalNode lays it out again from the matrix it places the final card with (world matrix plus a screen anchor's draw offset) only when that matrix differs from the one the card was last laid out from, writes the four corners and calls SetDirty, which Native Metal accepts as the four-corner card IsDynamicCardMesh already allowed for text, and which both renderers' existing dynamic-mesh upload (Vulkan's dynamic buffer, Native Metal's per-frame ring) copies on the next frame; the parse-time layout records its matrix too, so a still scene never lays the card out again. Cost: per tick, one 4x4 comparison per such layer beside the one SyncEffectFinalNode already makes; per move, four vertices rebuilt and copied (80 bytes) once into each frame-in-flight buffer; no graph rebuild. An event mesh keeps a target out of pixel reuse, and the targets a pass-through card draws into were never reusable, since they read the screen that the layer's own last pass writes: on a synthetic scene (a still pass-through layer in a group, a spinning layer drawn after it) the base and fixed renderers report the same 0 cacheable targets and 300 executed passes in 60 frames (offscreen_scene_probe), the same 3.0 render passes per frame and 524288 render-target bytes on Native Metal, and byte-identical last frames; with a script moving the group the fixed frames follow it. A pass-through layer created from a template is unaffected: a layer with an effect chain is never copied. Test: MetalSceneDraw.APassThroughLayerReadsTheScreenWhereItsGroupMovesItWhileTheSceneRunsOnBothRenderers (before: 87146 and 38188 of 294912 channel values off the backdrop on both renderers for the slider and the script; after: none, and the card laid out exactly once more).
sceneEngine.newTargetClearChanges: 2026-10-17: A render target the Compatibility backend allocates starts as transparent black, as on Native Metal. TextureCache::CreateTex(TextureKey) moved a new image from UNDEFINED to its final layout and nothing else, so it held whatever its memory held; TransImgLayout gains a `zero` flag and, for single-sample colour images (the only ones a pass samples), clears all mip levels to zero on the way through TRANSFER_DST. Native Metal already zeroed every new target at compile (MetalRender clearTargetsOnce). A target read before anything writes it, an effect's swapped history buffer or a carried-over target from ReserveCarriedOverTargets, read 1.0 (red, the channel the test samples) on its first frame on an Apple M3 Max, so an accumulating swap effect saturated on Compatibility from frame one while Native Metal counted up from zero; a hosted runner's paravirtual GPU returns zeroed memory, so the difference never showed there. The clear runs once per allocation, where CreateTex already waits for the GPU; no pass, frame work or memory is added. Test: MetalSceneDraw.AnEffectsSwappedBuffersAccumulateAndItsFloatBuffersKeepTheirSignOnBothRenderers (fails on an Apple GPU with the change removed).
sceneEngine.scriptVectorNumberChanges: 2026-10-17: A number a property script returns for a vector property is that number on every component, and the property stays a vector. FillDynamicValueFromJS (Scripting/ScriptEngine.cpp) turned a JavaScript number into a Float whatever the hinted type, so a `scale` script whose update(value) returns `value.x + (target - value.x) * speed` (a hover zoom on a clock widget that is on by default) handed its next update a bare number: `value.x` was undefined and the layer's scale, and with it its position, went NaN from the second frame, so the layer was never drawn. UpdateVectorFromNumber now fills a Vec2/Vec3/Vec4 or IVec2/IVec3/IVec4 hint from a number for a JavaScript integer or double; any other hint, and a value that is not a number (null, undefined), keeps the old reading. The same conversion serves the thisLayer setters: `color` and `parallaxDepth` now take a number on every component where they ignored it, and `origin`, `scale` and `angles` read the same vector as before. The layer's `origin` script, whose init() returns thisLayer.origin, was not the cause (an init result is not applied and it exports no update). Inferred, not compared against Wallpaper Engine's frames: its shipped Vec2 and Vec3 classes fill every component from one number, and the widget relies on a returned number. No per-frame cost beyond the existing conversion. Tests: ScriptRuntimeCompat.ANumberReturnedForAVectorPropertyFillsEveryAxisAndStaysAVector, ScriptRuntimeCompat.ANumberReturnedForAShaderVectorFillsEveryComponent, ScriptRuntimeCompat.ANumberWrittenToALayersColourOrParallaxDepthFillsEveryComponent. No API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.conditionedScriptPropertyChanges: 2026-10-17: A value bound to a combo with a condition (`{"user": {"name": ..., "condition": ...}}`) is a flag typed as one. DynamicValue::update (Runtime/DynamicValue.cpp), from a string or copied from a bound string property, set its bool to whether the choice equals the condition but kept the String type and the choice, so DynamicValueToJS handed a script property the choice itself ("2"), true in JavaScript whatever the condition; a clock offering its three date formats as three flags over one combo always took the first. A conditioned value now becomes a Boolean in one update. Consumers that read getBool() (layer and effect visibility) see what they saw before; a shader constant bound with a condition reads 1 or 0 where it read the choice as a number. A numeric combo value keeps its old reading. Test: ScriptRuntimeCompat.AScriptPropertyBoundToAComboChoiceReadsWhetherTheChoiceMatches. No API, schema or binding change.
sceneEngine.layerSavedSizeChanges: 2026-10-17: An image layer is as large as the size its scene object saved (`size`, which the editor's size field sets); the `width` and `height` a layer's model states, which the editor writes for a sprite sheet (one frame's size, beside `nopadding`), size only a layer that saved no size or one that cannot be read, for interoperability; no code copied. WPImageObject::FromJson took the model's size first, so a sprite layer resized in the editor was drawn at its frame's size. Established against Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42's frames of a scene (2440387496, 3456x2024 shots 8 and 15 s in) whose CRT screen is a sprite-sheet layer saved at 400x300 over a 300x200 frame, under a picture with the screen cut out: Wallpaper Engine's dark screen fills the monitor's bezel and its bars are 1.5 times as tall as ours were (300/200), where ours left a grey border of background inside the bezel. The mean difference to Wallpaper Engine's frames went from 2.74 and 2.71 to 1.03 and 0.99 (brightness correlation 0.952 to 0.99); only the screen's rectangle changed, where the remaining difference is the sprite's animation frame at the shot's moment. In the 86-item local library 31 layers of 13 scenes have a model that states a size, all sprite sheets with `nopadding`, and only three layers of that one scene saved a different size (two of them hidden unless a property shows them). A layer a script makes from a bare model saves no size and is unchanged. Chosen once at parse time, so no frame, memory or energy cost. Test: SceneSchema.ALayerIsDrawnAtTheSizeItsSceneSavedRatherThanItsModels.

lockScreenExtension.note: Extension/Phosphene-LICENSE.txt records the third-party notice for the private wallpaper-extension ABI reference used while implementing it.
lockScreenExtension.idleResidencyChanges: Unlocked lock-screen surfaces retain an owned static poster and IOSurface snapshot, then release their renderer. Eligible locks reload behind the poster; failure preserves the poster and waits for a fresh unlock/lock cycle. Same-scene metadata updates reuse retained content without recreating an idle renderer. The poster CGImage reads its read-locked IOSurface through a no-copy Data provider instead of copying it into a second bitmap; releasing the image unlocks and releases the surface. Whether Core Animation keeps its own display copy is unmeasured. The snapshot and poster name the pixel format through kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA.

workshopBrowser.implementation: Independently implemented for this application; no Unayung GPLv3 source copied.

distributionStatus: Blocked. Source policy is GPL-2.0-only (root LICENSE); the intended model is a free Developer ID signed and notarized download plus a one-time Supporter purchase that sells a sponsor place and priority support, never the software, with every GPL right retained by recipients and corresponding source offered alongside (LICENSING.md). Homebrew's GPLv3 ffmpeg@8 has been replaced by the LGPL-2.1-or-later build in Formula/mwe-ffmpeg.rb. Distribution of any binary remains blocked by Apache-2.0 components in the link closure: MoltenVK, vulkan-loader, SPIRV-Tools, the Apache-2.0 part of glslang, vendored spirv_reflect, and the Rust crates compiled into libwallpaper_bridge.a that are Apache-2.0 (codespan-reporting, spirv, miette, supports-color, supports-hyperlinks, supports-unicode, unicode-linebreak) or declared MIT AND Apache-2.0 (shadow-rs, is_debug). Retiring the Vulkan path alone does not clear them: codespan-reporting is required by naga for Native Metal shaders too, spirv leaves only with naga's spv-out feature, and the miette group and shadow-rs/is_debug serve neither renderer path. The Rust crates were audited by declared license on 2026-10-16 (LICENSING.md, Rust crates), not file by file; Eigen and glslang are not audited file by file either, and the license of third_party/glad, which the renderer build does not compile or link, is unchecked. scripts/package.py signs ad hoc only; signing and notarization are not implemented and would not constitute license clearance.
